You'll be our first Enterprise Marketing Manager and a hands-on IC (not a people manager). There's no playbook yet, so you'll write it, and you'll do the work yourself: the story, the assets, the programs.

As a team, we are focused on moving numbers across the funnel. Some of what you ship will be rolled back after a week because the data said so, other work will single handedly deliver months of revenue growth.

To apply, you must complete our Values Assessment Questionnaire here. We will consider your responses alongside your qualifications and experience as part of our overall hiring process.

Ideally, you'll have:

  • 5+ years in B2B SaaS product marketing, including supporting mid-market or enterprise deals directly.
  • A revenue mindset. You know how enterprise buyers buy, how deals move, and where they stall.
  • Written the deck, sat in the deal, and rewritten the deck after you lost.
  • Created demand for something buyers didn't know they needed yet.
  • Turned customer calls and win/loss notes into positioning within a few weeks.
  • A writer's ear. You make a complex product sound simple, in a publisher's or a CMO's own language.
  • A track record as a trusted partner to sales and CS leaders. You’ve partnered on pipeline or retention targets and built assets reps use in live deals.

Bonus Points

  • You've sold or marketed software to newsrooms, publishers or media companies.
  • You've marketed to CMOs and growth leaders at SaaS companies.
  • You've marketed email, lifecycle or messaging tools.
  • You've worked in sales or another revenue-facing role.
  • You already use AI daily to do more with less.

What you'll be responsible for:

In year one, expect roughly 40% on enabling sales and CS across segments (including large creators and existing accounts), 35% on publishers, and 25% on B2B brands. You own the story, offers and flagship assets that create enterprise demand. Our paid, outbound and lifecycle teams run the channels.

  • Set the enterprise story. Clarify our segments (publishers, B2B brands, large creators) and the story for each, building on our existing enterprise deck and one-pager.
  • Launch for publishers. Take our new enterprise products for publishers to market, starting from what our won and lost deals tell us.
  • Make the case for B2B brands. Work out with sales why enterprise matters for B2B brands, then turn it into the offers, hooks and follow-ups our paid and outbound teams run.
  • Own the enterprise sales kit. Decks, one-pagers, talk tracks, objection handling and demo stories, kept current.
  • Enable sales and CS. Train the team, sit in deals, track what gets used and fix what doesn't land. Give Customer Success the stories that renew and expand accounts.
  • Fix where deals stall. Use win/loss and funnel data to find where enterprise deals get stuck, then fix it with messaging, assets or programs.
  • Build proof. Pick the customer stories we need most, brief our content team on them, and keep a bench of references sales can call.
  • Run enterprise programs. Webinars, reports, ABM plays and conference presence, briefed to our content, creative and channel teams.
  • Make enterprise simple to sell. Turn a broad platform into short, repeatable messages a rep can say in one breath.

Why this role might be for you:

  • You want to be first into a new area and see your work in deals within weeks.
  • You like being the person who writes the story and the person who makes it work in the field.
  • You want a clear first win and a lot of room after it.

Why this role might not be for you:

  • You need a dedicated demand gen partner or a long ramp before you ship.
  • You want months of research before committing to a point of view. Here, v1 goes out early and gets better in the field.
  • You'd rather specialize in one thing (only decks, only events, only ABM).
  • You see enablement as handing off a deck. Here it means coaching reps and fixing what doesn't land.

Why beehiiv?

Our values aren't a poster on the wall — they're the bar. It’s how we operate, publicly and privately, and what we should return to when making decisions. That’s how we keep our team's momentum. That’s how we hire and keep A players.

beehiiv’s core values:

  • There's no room for B players ⭐: the best makes everyone better.
  • Maniacal sense of urgency ⚡: speed is our superpower.
  • Say what you think with positive intent 💬: disagree openly and give hard feedback directly, with the intent to help someone improve.
  • User-obsessed 🐝: every decision starts with one question: how does this add value for the user?
  • Ego comes second, winning comes first 🏆: we're here to create the best outcome; the team comes before the individual.

We'll take care of you:

  • Competitive salary
  • Stock options
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) employer match
  • Unlimited PTO (mandatory 10 days per year minimum)
  • Annual in-person team offsite
  • Unlimited book budget
  • Monthly Wellness Days (every third Friday of the month)

To apply, you must complete our Values Assessment Questionnaire here.

jobs.excerpt: About AppOmni AppOmni is redefining SaaS security for the age of agentic security operations.
jobs.description:
About AppOmni

AppOmni is redefining SaaS security for the age of agentic security operations. As AI transforms the way security teams build, operate, and defend their environments, AppOmni is pioneering a new approach to securing the world’s most critical SaaS ecosystems.

From its roots as a leader in SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM), AppOmni is driving the next evolution of SaaS security - bringing intelligence, automation, and agentic capabilities into security operations. AppOmni empowers organizations to move beyond traditional visibility and posture management toward more intelligent, proactive, and autonomous security.

Recognized as aFrost Radar™ 2025 Leaderand Great Place To Work®, AppOmni continues to set the standard for innovation and customer value in SaaS security.

About the Role

This position in a rapidly growing security engineering company is an opportunity to build the automation and AI workflows behind AppOmni's security research. AppOmni Labs, our security research team, writes the content behind our SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) platform: posture, detection and correlation rules. Much of a researcher's week still goes to repeatable work: finding the right data, checking how rules behave, and triaging schema changes and various feedback signals.

You will report to the Head of Security Research Engineering and work day to day with researchers and our data scientist. You will build ETL pipelines that bring together data from our SaaS data lake, intel feeds, rule telemetry and feedback signals, and build AI workflows on top of them in which carefully chosen, cost-effective LLMs triage issues and hand researchers a ranked, explained queue. These are open engineering problems in a part of the security industry without defined solutions, and we're looking for someone who enjoys solving them creatively.

What You'll Do

  • Build and maintain ETL pipelines that pull data from AppOmni's SaaS data lake and other internal and external sources, transform it, and deliver it to researchers and to the agents that work alongside them.
  • Build automation workflows in which LLMs triage incoming signals, such as vendor change announcements, security feeds, rule health and customer feedback, and route what matters to the right researcher with the reasoning attached.
  • Choose the right model for each step: small or tuned models where they are good enough, larger ones only where they pay off. Keep improving cost, latency and accuracy for every workflow.
  • Build tools that let researchers and agents query and explore data without hand-written queries or engineering tickets.
  • Work alongside researchers to find the repeatable steps in their work, then turn them into automated, observable systems.
  • Build evaluation into every AI workflow, using researchers' accept and reject decisions to measure quality and improve prompts, models and routing. Partner with our data scientist on evaluation methods and on learning from customer feedback.
  • Operate what you build, with monitoring, alerting and cost tracking, and keep tenant isolation, data security and access controls intact across every pipeline and every data surface an agent can reach.
  • Build CI, testing, performance and false-positive tooling for posture and detection rules, so researchers know before a change ships whether it breaks what already works.
  • At Staff level, set standards for automation and agent workflows across engineering and shape how the data platform supports them.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience for Senior, or 8+ years including setting technical direction across teams for Staff.
  • Strong production experience in Python or Go. Go is ideal; strength in one and willingness to work in the other can be accommodated.
  • Experience building and operating production data or ETL pipelines, including pulling from external APIs and data lakes.
  • Hands-on experience building LLM workflows that run in production, including prompting, tool calling, structured output and evaluation.
  • Interest in making AI workflows cheaper and better, for example through model selection, routing and caching.
  • A self-starter who can take a loosely defined problem, find a creative way to solve it, ship it and iterate without a detailed spec.
  • Experience with a major cloud provider, ideally Google Cloud, and with Kubernetes.
  • Ability to work directly with researchers and other internal customers, turn loosely defined workflows into clear requirements, and explain tradeoffs to technical and non-technical audiences.

You Might Also Have

  • A background in security research tooling, detection engineering or security analytics.
  • Experience integrating with the APIs of enterprise SaaS platforms such as Salesforce,
  • Microsoft 365, ServiceNow, Workday, Google Workspace, Github or Atlassian.
  • Experience building MCPs/CLIs or tools for agent frameworks.
  • Proven track record designing and operating robust data pipelines using tooling like
  • Apache Airflow, Dataflow, Dataproc, or Pub/Sub.
  • Prior experience with SSPM, CSPM, ITDR or other posture and identity security products.
  • Experience with LLM observability and evaluation tools such as LangSmith/Arize, or with
  • fine-tuning or distilling smaller models.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 days: Learn where researchers spend time on repeatable work and how data reaches them today. Follow given use cases and ship a first LLM triage workflow with AppOmni Labs, with its cost and accuracy measured.
First year: Several triage workflows run continuously alongside researchers, each with its cost and accuracy tracked and improving. Researchers spend measurably less time on manual triage and query data through self-serve tools. Other teams build faster on the pipelines and patterns you established, without compromising quality or data controls.

The Technology You'll Work With

  • Python and Go (Echo, gRPC, pgx, OpenTelemetry)

Culture

Our talented team is collaborative and supportive as we move quickly to research and develop new ideas, deliver new features to our customers, and iterate on ideas and innovations. We accomplish this by focusing on our five core values: Trust, Transparency, Quality, Customer Focus, and Delivery. Our team is determined to make a difference to positively impact our way of life by securing the technology that is changing the world.

AppOmni is proud to be Certified by Great Place to WorkⓇ, as we seek to build a culture where all employees feel appreciated and supported, especially with clear and honest leadership, employee recognition, and an environment that fosters innovation and collaboration.

We believe diversity fuels innovation and drives growth by bringing a wealth of different perspectives and skills. We’re committed to fostering an inclusive environment where every employee feels valued, heard, and empowered to reach their full potential. Join us in building a workplace where we can all thrive.

Compensation & Benefits

AppOmni is committed to supporting our employees' financial, professional, and personal well-being. To do this, we take a holistic view of compensation, one that values not just the immediate financial package but also the long-term growth of both our employees and our company. We're committed to pay equity and transparency and encourage all candidates to discuss their salary expectations with us early in the application process.

Our total rewards package includes the following:

  • Base Salary: The annual base salary compensation range in the U.S. for this role is: $200,000 - $300,000 USD. Final offer amounts are determined by factors such as the final candidate’s location, skills, qualifications, and experience, as well as business considerations and peer compensation.
  • Stock Options: Our vision is to not just grow as a company but to grow together. By offering stock options, we are inviting you to be an integral part of our journey forward.
  • Benefits: Generous paid time off, paid company holidays, paid floating holidays, paid parental leave, paid sick time and paid family leave for applicable states, health insurance - medical, dental, and vision with HSA option, LifeWorks Employee Assistance Program, company-provided life insurance, AD&D, STD/LTD and additional supplemental life insurance options, 401(k) and Roth retirement saving accounts, and a monthly wellness benefit reimbursement. All benefits are subject to eligibility requirements and plan details.

AppOmni is an equal-opportunity employer. Applicants will not be discriminated against because of race, color, creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, religion, disability, pregnancy, marital status, veteran status, medical condition, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. AppOmni is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures.

jobs.excerpt: About QSIC QSIC is reinventing in-store audio.  We use Audio, Intelligence (AI) and Creativity to redefine the value of in-store audio and drive growth for retailers and brands.
jobs.description:
About QSIC

QSIC is reinventing in-store audio. We use Audio, Intelligence (AI) and Creativity to redefine the value of in-store audio and drive growth for retailers and brands. Our story began in Australia over a decade ago with a love for music and a simple purpose: to create value that others can’t see. We sought to bring that to life through exceptional audio experiences, so we built the leading intelligent in-store audio platform for retailers and brands. At QSIC, in-store audio has never been just “background noise.” Audio has the power to change the atmosphere, spark emotion and shift the atmosphere. When it’s seamlessly woven into an in-store experience, it doesn’t just play – it connects. It engages shoppers without distracting them, influences decisions where it matters most, and elevates the entire shopping journey. Today, QSIC technology powers thousands of stores across three continents, reaching over 100 million shoppers each month.

- QSIC’s Ad Platform removes the friction of ad production, and instantly creates targeted, brand-aligned messaging with AI. Advertisers can use our Planning solution to eliminate guesswork by having their messages dynamically placed in the market - at the right time, for maximum impact. Every ad play is recorded and verified, providing unprecedented transparency.

- QSIC’s In-Store Audio solutions deliver intelligent, scalable and personalised playlists to match brand identities, and automated volume control to adjust for every moment!

- QSIC Intelligence provides enhanced targeting, and predicts the right message for every moment using our data-driven insights. The QSIC Intelligence solution includes performance analytics and self-service reporting.

Our motivation is to create value that others don’t see. Our promise is to use audio, intelligence and relentless dedication to transform spaces and deliver results. We have team members based in Australia, the United States and Mexico, and received Series B funding in January 2025. We’re just getting started!

The Opportunity

The QSIC ad sales team works with leading brands, agencies and retailers to generate highly performant in-store media campaigns. This is an individual contributor, quota-carrying, business development role. You'll open, grow and close advertising partnerships with a named list of target accounts across CPG, BevAlc, Pharma and non-endemic categories. You'll sell in-store audio across QSIC's national network of leading retailers.

You'll sell directly to brands and through their agency partners, including the major holding companies. You'll take a channel that most brands haven't budgeted for yet and turn it into a planned, repeatable line in the media plan. That means more than taking orders. You'll find the right decision makers, identify the funding source, build the case, and close.

Success in this role means consistently exceeding revenue targets, opening new national advertiser relationships, and converting emerging in-store audio opportunities into long-term, recurring advertising partnerships.

This role suits a proven hunter who has sold an emerging media channel before and enjoys building something from the ground up. You'll work closely with the SVP, Ad Revenue and dedicated support across marketing, sales planning, creative production and finance.

What You'll Do

  • Revenue Ownership: Own and deliver against an annual advertising revenue quota, driving new business acquisition and account expansion across CPG, BevAlc, Pharma, and non-endemic categories.
  • Strategic Account Development: Develop and execute strategic account plans, identifying high-value opportunities and engaging key decision-makers across brand marketing, shopper marketing, media, and innovation teams.
  • Agency Partnerships: Build and manage relationships with major holding companies (Publicis, Omnicom, WPP, Dentsu, Havas), independent agencies, and shopper marketing agencies to generate new advertising opportunities.
  • Full-Cycle Sales Execution: Lead the entire sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery through proposals, pricing negotiations, insertion orders (IOs), and renewals.
  • Market Development: Educate advertisers on the value of in-store audio, leveraging creative solutions, case studies, campaign measurement, and ROI insights to establish the channel as a recurring component of national media plans.
  • Account Growth: Convert initial campaign investments into multi-flight, annual, and network-wide advertising partnerships that drive sustainable revenue growth.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with sales planning, marketing, creative production, and campaign teams to develop compelling proposals, execute successful campaigns, and demonstrate measurable advertiser outcomes.
  • Industry Engagement: Represent QSIC at industry events, client meetings, and hosted experiences while staying informed on evolving retail media trends and competitive opportunities.
  • Pipeline Management & Forecasting: Maintain a healthy, qualified pipeline, accurate CRM records, and reliable revenue forecasts, actively participating in weekly pipeline and forecast reviews.

What We're Looking For

  • 7+ years of quota-carrying media sales experience, with a track record of meeting or exceeding new business targets
  • Sales experience in one or more of the following: in-store media, retail media, DOOH, programmatic or digital media, digital audio, or national advertising sales
  • Proven success opening new accounts and closing enterprise advertising deals with national brands, not only managing an existing book
  • Established relationships with brand marketers, shopper marketers and agency teams, ideally including HoldCo agencies
  • Experience selling a new or emerging media channel in a high growth vertical.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience
  • Proficiency with CRM platforms (HubSpot, Salesforce or similar) and prospecting tools such as ZoomInfo, Winmo or MediaRadar
  • Category experience in CPG, BevAlc, Pharma/OTC or consumer health is a strong advantage
  • Familiarity with alcohol advertising compliance (including tied-house considerations) is a plus
  • Startup or high-growth company experience is a plus
  • A hunter's mindset: self-directed, persistent, and creative in how you open doors
  • Consultative seller who can navigate multiple stakeholders and unresolved budget ownership
  • Strong storyteller who can turn data, measurement and creative into a clear business case
  • Comfortable with long, complex sales cycles and disciplined about pipeline management and forecasting
  • Entrepreneurial and adaptable. Energized by building a new channel and a new team
  • Thrives in a fully remote, collaborative team environment

What We Offer

  • Competitive base salary plus uncapped commission with target on-track earnings.
  • Remote-first position based in the United States, with flexibility to work from an approved location. National travel is expected for client meetings, agency engagements, industry events, and team collaboration.
  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Direct exposure to one of the fastest-growing channels in retail — in-store media
  • A team that wins together, supports each other, and genuinely enjoys the work

Ready to shape the future of retail media?

We'd love to hear from you. Apply with your resume and a short note on why QSIC and this role excite you.

QSIC is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Development Associate
jobs.excerpt: Development Associate Together for Girls works around the world and combines state-of-the-art data with powerful advocacy to end violence against children and adolescents, especially sexual violence.
jobs.description:
Development Associate

Together for Girls works around the world and combines state-of-the-art data with powerful advocacy to end violence against children and adolescents, especially sexual violence. As the host of the Brave Movement, a survivor-led global advocacy initiative, we support and mobilize survivors and allies worldwide to drive political will, influence policy, and ensure that inaction is not an option.

By connecting the dots between understanding the problem, identifying effective solutions, tracking progress, and getting solutions into the hands of those with the power to make change, TfG amplifies our impact and drives toward the ultimate goal of creating a safer world for children and adolescents.

We are rooted in the conviction that violence is preventable and chance is possible, drawing upon 19 years of data from the Violence Against Children and Youth Surveys (VACS), new and emerging science, and lived experience. The Safe Futures Solutions Hub shares evidence and practice-based knowledge to inform effective prevention and response efforts, ensuring access to proven solutions across sectors. The Out of the Shadows Index tracks countries’ progress in addressing violence, providing an accountability framework and benchmark for advocacy. Brave Movement members and other activists leverage these tools to transform evidence into collective action for prevention, healing, and justice.

We are a nimble and highly impactful team that continues to grow and evolve. We work with a broad range of organizations, researchers, and advocates to drive change.

Position Overview

We are seeking a highly organised and proactive Development Associate to provide essential operational and coordination support across the Development team.

The Associate will help ensure that the Development function operates efficiently by maintaining the CRM and fundraising records, conducting prospect and opportunity research, tracking funding opportunities and deadlines, supporting proposal development, and coordinating fundraising materials and events.

This is a hands-on role requiring strong attention to detail, excellent organisation and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines. The Associate will work closely with colleagues in the Development team, as well as across Communications, Programmes and Finance.

Reporting to the Deputy Director, Development, the role will provide broad exposure to institutional and foundations fundraising, individual giving and donor engagement, and Development operations, with opportunities to build expertise across different areas of fundraising.

Key Responsibilities & Duties

1. Prospect Research & Funding Opportunities

  • Conduct research on prospective foundations, institutional donors and other funding opportunities.
  • Monitor donor websites, funding portals, sector resources and other sources for relevant funding opportunities.
  • Maintain accurate records of prospects, opportunities, deadlines and cultivation activity.
  • Support the Development team to assess and map prospects and identify appropriate next steps.

2. Proposal & Pitch Support

  • Support the preparation and submission of funding proposals, reports and other donor materials.
  • Coordinate proposal timelines, deadlines, inputs and approvals, ensuring materials are submitted on time.
  • Gather organizational information, program data, budgets and other required inputs from colleagues.
  • Maintain and organize the Development proposal library, including boilerplate language and supporting materials.

3. CRM & Development Data

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date records in the Development CRM, including donor, prospect and opportunity information.
  • Ensure fundraising activity, communications and relevant donor information are recorded consistently.
  • Support data entry, reporting, list management and basic analysis for Development activities.
  • Help maintain data quality and support the team to use the CRM effectively.

4. Donor Engagement & Events

  • Support the coordination of donor meetings, briefings, events and other Development activities
  • Prepare meeting materials, presentations, briefing documents and other information as required.
  • Coordinate logistics, invitations, follow-up and administrative arrangements for Development events and engagement opportunities.
  • Support donor acknowledgements and other routine stewardship activity.

5. Development Operations

  • Help ensure Development processes and information are well organized, accessible and consistently maintained.
  • Identify opportunities to improve systems and processes and support the team in implementing them.

Other duties, as assigned.

Desired Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

Essential

  • At least 2 years' experience in fundraising, development, nonprofit administration.
  • Excellent organizational skills and strong attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines and inputs from different colleagues.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Experience conducting research and synthesising information clearly and accurately.
  • Strong administrative and project coordination skills.
  • Experience using CRM or database systems, or demonstrated ability to learn new systems quickly.
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and standard digital tools.
  • Ability to work collaboratively across teams and with colleagues in different locations.
  • Proactive, reliable and able to follow through on tasks with limited day-to-day supervision.
  • Comfortable working in a remote-first, international environment.

Desirable

  • Experience supporting institutional or foundation fundraising.
  • Experience with prospect research or funding databases.
  • Experience supporting proposal development and donor reporting.
  • Experience working in an international nonprofit or global advocacy organisation.
  • Interest in developing a career in fundraising and Development.

Location & Ways of Working

This position is a full-time position that can be based in the Washington, DC metro area or Nairobi, Kenya. Applicants should have work authorization for their preferred location.

This is currently a remote position with the expectation to travel to attend some in-person meetings periodically. This position will also require travel up to 10%.

All team members are expected to be available during Together for Girls’ core working hours of 8:00 AM - 12:00 PM Eastern Standard Time. The other four hours that the team member chooses to work are flexible and may be coordinated with their supervisor.

Compensation

This role offers a competitive salary adjusted to the cost of labor in the city where the candidate resides. Final salary within this location adjusted range will also be determined by the candidate’s qualifications and years and type of experience.

For example, the annual salary for the position for a candidate based in

  • Washington, D.C. will be $50,000 - $61,500
  • Nairobi, Kenya will be Ksh 3,826,000 - 4,739,000

Together for Girls offers competitive pay, paid leave, and comprehensive health insurance. Specific benefits vary by country.

Culture and Values

Together for Girls seeks to create a courageous, inclusive, and flexible culture that empowers our staff to have the capacity and ability to deliver change. We strive to build and maintain psychological safety, trust, and accountability among team members in order to foster honesty and openness about our needs and challenges while also prioritizing self-care. We are a rapidly expanding organization that requires staff to be nimble and flexible, comfortable with uncertainty and able to adapt in real time to emerging opportunities.

Brave Movement Applicants

We warmly encourage members of the Brave Movement to apply. While membership is not a requirement for this role, we value the lived experience, leadership, and commitment that members bring to advancing survivor-centered advocacy and strengthening our global movement.

Application Information

Together for Girls, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer and committed to maintaining an inclusive and diverse working environment free from discrimination and harassment. Qualified applicants from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Together for Girls, Inc. is a registered 501(c)(3) non-profit organization in the U.S.

NOTICE—All job candidates must apply online and submit an application through our official process. Together for Girls does not send unsolicited job offers

Voyager is an innovative defense, national security and space technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart. 

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager.

Job Summary:

The Systems Engineer - Project Engineer VI serves as a senior technical authority and strategic integrator for high-complexity defense and aerospace programs. The individual provides technical direction and programmatic oversight across engineering disciplines, ensuring alignment of design, performance, and risk with mission and contractual requirements. The Level VI engineer represents engineering leadership at the enterprise level, contributing to organizational strategy, process improvement, and technology development initiatives.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as chief project engineer or senior technical lead for large, multi-phase, or multi-contract defense and aerospace programs
  • Define and guide system architecture, integration, and verification strategies aligned with customer and mission objectives

  • Lead technical baseline definition, configuration management, and system integration planning

  • Serve as the primary engineering interface to executive management and DoD customers, supporting technical interchange meetings and milestone reviews

  • Develop and implement advanced risk and opportunity management frameworks across enterprise-level programs

jobs.title: Chief Development Officer
jobs.excerpt: Thrive Scholars has partnered with Orr Group to lead the search for this position.
jobs.description:
Thrive Scholars has partnered with Orr Group to lead the search for this position. All applicants must submit their applications directly through this link.Applications submitted through Rippling will not be considered.

Location: While this is a fully remote position, candidates based in Chicago, New York, or Los Angeles preferred; other major U.S. metros considered.

Travel Expectations: Up to 40%

EmploymentType: Full Time, Exempt

Salary Range: $225,000 - $275,000

The Organization

For 25 years, Thrive Scholars has helped extraordinarily talented young people gain access to opportunities too often shaped by family income, geography, networks, and exposure. Thrive's mission is to empower high-achieving students from low-income backgrounds with the skills, guidance, and professional networks they need to excel in top colleges and launch careers that lead to economic mobility.

Thrive's six-year model supports Scholars from their junior year of high school through college graduation. It combines rigorous academic preparation, college access and success advising, individualized coaching, career development, and opportunities with leading colleges and employers.

The results are strong. More than 90 percent of Scholars attend top colleges, Scholars earn an average college GPA of about 3.4, roughly 80 percent persist in STEM, and 99 percent graduate from college. Thrive serves more than 1,400 Scholars, most of them first-generation college students, and their average starting salary is roughly double their household income.

Thrive is in the second year of an ambitious five-year strategic plan developed with Bain & Company. In 2026, Thrive welcomed about 575 Scholars, its largest incoming class ever, and it plans to grow its annual incoming cohort to about 1,000 Scholars over the next four years while maintaining or improving outcomes. Strengthening fundraising is a core pillar of that plan, and the Chief Development Officer (CDO) will lead it

The Position

Thrive Scholars seeks a disciplined, entrepreneurial, and results-driven CDO to shape the fundraising engine that will power its next chapter of growth. Thrive has a proven model, a national base of loyal supporters, and a strong development team. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and serving on the senior leadership team, the next CDO will build on that foundation to create a sustainable, growing, and diversified revenue stream.

With contributed revenue of roughly $18 million annually, Thrive Scholars is poised for its next stage of growth. The incoming CDO will lead the effort to raise contributed revenue to $25 million in the years ahead, while creating a revenue base that is sustainable, growing, and diversified.

The CDO leads the development team by setting a clear strategy, refining roles and goals, monitoring the pipeline, and holding staff accountable for results. Equally important, this leader personally manages a small number of large, transformational opportunities with major national funders.

Corporate partnerships, which are critical to Thrive’s model, will also be a key area of focus. Companies invest not only as funders but as employers who meet, hire, and develop Scholars. The organization aims to increase corporate support as a share of total revenue.

Fundraising will benefit from a sales-minded approach. That means creating playbooks, measuring what is working by account and region, and giving leadership real-time visibility into results, all while preserving the relationship-driven culture that makes Thrive’s development efforts so successful.

This is a hands-on, visible leadership role. The CDO will spend meaningful time on the road with donors, partners, Board members, and regional teams in Thrive's key markets, including New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Boston, Detroit, and Jacksonville.

Key Responsibilities

Build a Disciplined Pipeline-Driven Fundraising Program

  • Develop and execute annual and multi-year fundraising plans with the CEO that support Thrive's five-year strategic plan.
  • Diversify Thrive’s revenue base by identifying and securing new funders, partners, and revenue streams while maximizing revenue nationally and across Thrive’s regions from individuals, foundations, and corporations.
  • Dedicate a meaningful share of time to personally cultivating, soliciting, and closing major gifts from individuals, foundations, and corporations, including managing a focused portfolio of major national prospects with the potential for making transformational, multi-year investments.
  • Strengthen and grow Thrive's broad base of existing donors by defining clear stewardship expectations and building an organization-wide donor recognition strategy, applied consistently across national and regional teams, that drives retention and increased giving.
  • In partnership with finance, ensure Thrive’s fundraising meets legal, ethical, and policy requirements, including gift acceptance, donor restrictions, gift acknowledgment, and grant reporting.
  • Provide clear, timely reporting on fundraising performance to the CEO, finance team, and Board.
  • Use Salesforce and data to forecast revenue, measure performance, and inform decisions.

Lead and Manage a High-Performing Development Team

  • Lead and manage a development team of ~12, including regional executive directors, corporate partnerships, and development operations.
  • Translate the development strategy into specific goals, roles, and accountabilities for every team member.
  • Know the state of the pipeline at all times, including what has closed, what is at risk, and what each team member is working on, using disciplined routines such as regular pipeline reviews, activity tracking, and progress against targets.
  • Hire, onboard, coach, and develop strong fundraisers as the department and revenue grows.
  • Identify and integrate AI-enabled tools and practices that sharpen prospect identification, forecasting, and personalized stewardship, ensuring the team uses them responsibly and effectively
  • Foster a team culture grounded in Thrive's Cultural Commitments, with high expectations, candid feedback, collaboration, and connection to the mission.

Corporate Partnerships

  • Lead the corporate partnerships strategy, with the goal of growing corporate support as a share of total revenue.
  • Partner closely with the Chief Program Officer and the program and career teams to design corporate partnerships that Thrive can deliver on with excellence, building long-term sustainable and meaningful relationships with these corporations.
  • Partner with the CEO, Board, and Senior Leadership
  • Serve as a strategic thought partner to the CEO and deploy the CEO's time on the highest-value fundraising opportunities while accompanying and preparing the CEO for donor meetings when appropriate.
  • As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, contribute to organization-wide decisions and build strong partnerships with program, finance, and operations leaders.
  • Work with the CEO and Board members to map and open their personal and professional networks, and support them in their own cultivation and solicitation of donors.
  • Engage the National Board and regional boards as fundraisers, connectors, and ambassadors, and secure clear annual fundraising commitments from Board members.
  • Collaborate closely with the marketing and communications team so that Thrive’s brand, storytelling, impact reporting, and donor communications directly support fundraising goals and the donor pipeline.
  • Foster a culture of philanthropy across Thrive, and ensure that systems and processes support fundraising.

Experience and Qualifications

The strongest candidates will bring many of the following:

  • Connection to Thrive's mission: A deep commitment to expanding opportunity for talented young people from low-income backgrounds. Lived experience that reflects the backgrounds of Thrive's scholars is valued.
  • Measurable fundraising results: At least 12 years of fundraising experience, or transferable for-profit sales experience, with a track record of growing revenue over time, including bringing in new funders and revenue streams, and personally closing six- and seven-figure gifts from individuals, foundations, and/or corporations.
  • Proven team leadership: At least 7 years leading a team at a multi-site or national organization. A clear record of hiring strong people and holding a team accountable to goals.
  • Pipeline discipline: Experience running fundraising with the rigor of a sales organization, including pipeline management, forecasting, playbooks, and performance metrics, using a CRM (preferably Salesforce). Experience in or alongside for-profit sales or business development is a plus.
  • Major institutional relationships: Experience cultivating long-cycle relationships with national foundations, corporations, and/or major donors.
  • Corporate partnerships: Experience building corporate partnerships that combine philanthropy with deeper engagement, such as talent pipelines or employee involvement.
  • Board and executive partnership: Ability to quickly earn the trust of a CEO, Board members, and senior colleagues, and to engage volunteers effectively in fundraising, including securing Board giving commitments.
  • Willingness to travel: Comfort with significant travel, up to 40% of the time, to Thrive's key markets
  • Systems and data: Experience using a CRM, preferably Salesforce, to manage pipeline and report results.
  • Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to tell Thrive's story compellingly to donors and partners.

Employee Relations Manager – W2 Consultants

Position: Employee Relations Manager – W2 Consultants
Employment Type: Full-Time
Industry: IT Staffing & Professional Services
Location: Remote / Hybrid

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced and highly professional Employee Relations Manager – W2 Consultants to serve as the primary point of contact for our W2 consultant workforce.

This position will be responsible for developing and maintaining strong relationships with consultants throughout their employment lifecycle and ensuring that their questions, concerns, and requests are addressed promptly and professionally.

The ideal candidate will combine strong employee-relations expertise, communication skills, IT staffing knowledge, and operational judgment. This individual should be approachable and responsive while maintaining professionalism, confidentiality, and appropriate boundaries when handling sensitive employee matters.

Key Responsibilities

Employee & Consultant Relations

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for W2 consultants regarding employment-related questions, concerns, and requests.
  • Establish and maintain professional, trusted relationships with consultants throughout their employment lifecycle.
  • Provide timely communication and appropriate follow-up on consultant inquiries and concerns.
  • Listen to employee concerns, understand the underlying issue, and coordinate with the appropriate internal stakeholders to achieve resolution.
  • Handle sensitive and escalated matters with discretion, professionalism, and confidentiality.

  • Maintain accurate records of employee concerns, communications, actions taken, and resolutions.

Payroll & Employment Support

  • Coordinate with Payroll and HR regarding questions related to salary, payroll processing, timesheets, deductions, reimbursements, benefits, and employment documentation.
  • Assist consultants in understanding company processes and requirements.
  • Monitor outstanding payroll or employment-related issues and ensure appropriate follow-up through resolution.
  • Escalate complex or sensitive matters to the appropriate management or functional team.

Immigration Coordination

  • Serve as the communication liaison between consultants and the organization's Immigration/Legal team.
  • Coordinate requests and documentation related to H-1B transfers, extensions, amendments, OPT/EAD, and other employment authorization matters.
  • Ensure consultants receive timely updates regarding the status of immigration-related requests.
  • Facilitate communication and follow-up without providing independent legal or immigration advice.

Marketing, Projects & Consultant Support

  • Coordinate with Recruiting, Marketing/Bench Sales, and Account Management regarding consultant marketing status, job opportunities, submissions, interviews, project assignments, and placement activities.
  • Ensure consultants receive appropriate updates regarding their project or marketing status.
  • Assist consultants during onboarding, project transitions, client interviews, assignments, and offboarding.
  • Identify and escalate issues that may impact consultant engagement, retention, or project continuity.

Cross-Functional Coordination

  • Partner effectively with HR, Payroll, Immigration, Recruiting, Marketing/Bench Sales, Sales, Account Management, and senior management.
  • Take ownership of consultant issues and ensure they are routed to the appropriate department.
  • Maintain visibility into open issues and proactively follow up until resolution.
  • Identify recurring employee concerns and recommend improvements to policies, processes, and communication.
  • Develop and maintain effective communication processes between consultants and internal departments.

Ideal Candidate Profile

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Management, or a related field preferred.
  • 3–7+ years of experience in Employee Relations, HR Operations, Consultant Relations, IT Staffing, Workforce Management, or a related field.
  • Previous experience supporting W2 IT consultants within a U.S. staffing or consulting organization is strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of the U.S. IT staffing and consulting environment.
  • Familiarity with H-1B, H-1B transfers, OPT/EAD, and employment authorization processes.
  • Experience coordinating with Payroll, Immigration, Recruiting, HR, and staffing operations.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-management capabilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage sensitive employee concerns with professionalism and discretion.
  • Strong organizational, problem-solving, and follow-through skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and documentation skills.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across multiple departments.

Key Competencies

  • Employee & Consultant Relationship Management
  • Conflict Resolution & Issue Management
  • Cross-Functional Coordination
  • Professional Communication
  • Problem Solving & Ownership
  • Confidentiality & Professional Judgment
  • U.S. Staffing Operations
  • Payroll & Employment Processes
  • Immigration Coordination
  • Consultant Engagement & Retention

Performance Expectations

Success in this role will be measured by the ability to provide W2 consultants with a consistent, responsive, and professional employee experience.

The Employee Relations Manager is expected to:

  • Establish strong relationships and trust with the consultant workforce.
  • Respond to consultant inquiries in a timely manner.
  • Ensure issues are appropriately assigned, tracked, and resolved.
  • Maintain clear and consistent communication throughout the resolution process.
  • Minimize recurring consultant concerns through proactive communication and process improvement.
  • Strengthen collaboration between consultants and internal departments.
  • Support overall consultant engagement, satisfaction, and retention.

The Role in One Sentence

The Employee Relations Manager will serve as the central point of contact and advocate for our W2 consultants, coordinating across HR, Payroll, Immigration, Recruiting, Marketing, and Management to ensure their employment-related needs are addressed professionally and efficiently.

We’re looking for someone to take ownership of Cronometer’s privacy and compliance programs and help us build the processes needed as the business grows. This work currently spans multiple teams. We want a dedicated person who can identify what needs attention, bring in the right expertise, establish clear priorities, and drive work through to completion.

Privacy and compliance will be the main focus. Over time, the role could expand to other company-wide programs where coordinated planning and ongoing ownership would help.We see this initially as a senior individual contributor role. “Manager” refers to ownership of programs; people management is not an initial requirement.

What this person will own:

  1. Privacy and Compliance programs
    1. Build and maintain a practical roadmap covering our privacy, compliance, and assurance priorities.
    2. Work with external counsel and specialists to understand applicable requirements and turn their advice into clear actions.
    3. Maintain a register of obligations, risks, decisions, owners, and deadlines.
    4. Monitor relevant changes in the global privacy landscape and assess what needs further review or action.
    5. Coordinate privacy policy updates and ensure our disclosures reflect how our products and business actually operate.
    6. Establish and maintain processes for privacy requests, retention and deletion, consent, and customer-data access.
  2. Audits and external assurance
    1. Lead readiness and coordination for relevant audits, assessments, and certifications, including HIPAA-related assessments, ISO certifications, and CASA assessments.
    2. Help determine which assurance programs are appropriate for our business and customer needs.
    3. Manage external assessors, timelines, evidence collection, findings, and remediation.
    4. Conduct internal readiness reviews and arrange independent review where needed.
    5. Keep controls and evidence current between assessments.
  3. Product and operational reviews
    1. Bring privacy and compliance considerations into upcoming projects early enough to shape the work.

Reporting to the VP of Professional Services, the Delivery Executive serves as Clariti's senior strategic relationship leader, designated Executive Sponsor, and project P&L owner for our largest, most complex government customers. Engagement Managers retain day-to-day project execution responsibility; you provide executive accountability, strategic direction, and financial oversight. Bonus Points

Welcome to Clearway Health - At Clearway Health, we’ve been recognized as a Great Place to Work® for four years in a row—and we’re just getting started. Position Summary:

The Director, Infusion Services will lead the day-to-day operations of infusion-related patient access, with a primary focus on benefits investigation, prior authorization, payor requirements, and reimbursement support. This is a hands-on leadership role responsible for executing core operational activities, resolving complex access issues, developing efficient workflows, and building a team to support the growth of infusion services.

The Director will bring a strong foundation in infusion authorization and patient access, with the ability to navigate medical and pharmacy benefits, work directly with payors and providers, and ensure patients can access prescribed therapies with minimal administrative delays. The role will also support site-of-care determination and transitions, 340B program optimization, and collaboration with Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs).

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Lead a distributed team of infusion access specialists embedded at client sites. Ensure consistent workflows, quality, and performance standards across locations. Serve as the primary escalation point and subject matter expert for complex benefits, authorization, and site of care cases. Establish clear operating agreements with client leadership on work assignment, escalation, and performance management.
  • Infusion Access and Prior Authorization: Manage and oversee benefits investigations, insurance verification, prior authorizations, reauthorizations, and payor-related escalations. Resolve complex cases, address missing documentation, and work with providers and clinical teams to minimize delays in treatment.
  • Daily Operations: Manage day-to-day workflows, prioritize cases, monitor authorization status and turnaround times, troubleshoot access barriers, and ensure timely and accurate completion of infusion-related activities.
  • Team Building and Leadership: Build and develop the infusion services team as operational needs grow. Establish workflows, train team members, set performance expectations, and provide hands-on coaching and support to ensure consistent execution and quality.
  • Payor and Provider Coordination: Work directly with health plans, PBMs, provider offices, and health-system partners to clarify coverage requirements, resolve authorization issues, address denials, and coordinate the information needed to support treatment access.
  • Site-of-Care Determination: Review site-of-care requirements and support the identification and coordination of appropriate alternative infusion settings.
  • PBM and Benefit Management: Support operational activities involving PBMs and specialty drug benefit programs, including coverage requirements, utilization management, authorization processes, and payor policy changes. Identify issues and implement workflow adjustments as needed.
  • Process Improvement and Reporting: Develop and maintain standard operating procedures, identify workflow gaps, and implement practical improvements. Track key metrics such as authorization turnaround time, approval and denial trends, outstanding cases, referral conversion, and other measures of operational performance.

Education:

  • Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, nursing, pharmacy, or a related field
  • Master's degree in healthcare administration (MHA), business administration (MBA), or a related field, preferred.

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations Required:

  • Clinical licensure or credentialing, such as RN, PharmD, or CPhT.
  • Certification such as CHAA, CHAM, CRCR, or a relevant specialty pharmacy credential, preferred.

Experience:

  • 5+ of experience in infusion services, patient access, specialty pharmacy, or a related healthcare setting, including at least four years of direct experience with infusion or provider-administered specialty drug benefits investigation and prior authorization.
  • 3+ years of people leadership experience, including experience supervising staff, developing team capabilities, and managing operational performance.
  • Experience working with PBMs, health plans, or specialty drug benefit management and 340B programs.

Knowledge/Skills:

  • Familiarity with HCPCS/J-codes, CPT, ICD-10, and NDC billing.
  • Proficiency with Epic or a comparable electronic health record (EHR), payor portals, and electronic prior authorization tools.

Special Working Conditions (On-call, travel, shift, coverage):

  • Up to 30% travel may be required to new client-sites or pharmacy implementations within the United States.

jobs.description:
Job Description

AECOM is seeking a highly motivated Utility Infrastructure Telecom Design QC Engineer / Specialist to support the planning, design, and quality assurance of telecommunications outside plant (OSP) infrastructure programs.

This role will focus on the design, review, and modeling of underground conduit systems supporting fiber optic networks, data center connectivity, metro fiber deployments, and utility infrastructure projects.

The successful candidate will possess practical experience designing and reviewing underground conduit networks, duct banks, handholes, manholes, and associated civil infrastructure. The position requires proficiency with Civil 3D and related engineering and design software for developing, reviewing, and validating designs throughout the project lifecycle.

This is a fully remote position requiring the ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary engineering teams, utility stakeholders, permitting agencies, clients, and construction personnel across multiple geographic regions.

Key Responsibilities

Underground Telecommunications Infrastructure Design

  • Develop and review underground OSP designs for fiber optic network deployments.
  • Design conduit systems, duct banks, manholes, handholes, roadway crossings, and utility corridors.
  • Perform route evaluations and constructability assessments for greenfield and brownfield projects.
  • Incorporate utility conflicts, right-of-way constraints, environmental considerations, and permitting requirements into design solutions.
  • Support the development of construction drawings, plan and profile sheets, details, specifications, and permit packages.
  • Review existing conditions, survey information, utility records, and subsurface utility information as part of design development.
  • Coordinate telecommunications infrastructure designs with civil, electrical, structural, and other engineering disciplines.

Engineering Review and Quality Assurance

  • Perform technical and quality reviews of telecommunications and utility infrastructure design packages.
  • Verify compliance with client standards, engineering requirements, design criteria, and construction requirements.
  • Review conduit sizing and occupancy, bend radii, separation requirements, depth of cover, pulling considerations, and access structure placement.
  • Validate designs for compliance with applicable municipal, DOT, utility, NEC, NESC, and client-specific requirements.
  • Review drawings for design coordination, completeness, constructability, and technical accuracy.
  • Identify design deficiencies, conflicts, and constructability risks and provide clear recommendations for corrective action.
  • Support interdisciplinary design reviews and formal QA/QC processes.

Utility Coordination and Permitting Support

  • Coordinate with utility owners, municipalities, transportation agencies, and permitting authorities.
  • Support utility conflict identification, resolution, and relocation planning.
  • Assist in the development of permit applications and responses to agency review comments.
  • Participate in design review meetings, utility coordination meetings, and constructability reviews.
  • Incorporate permitting and agency requirements into final design packages.

Construction Support

  • Provide engineering and design support during construction activities.
  • Review contractor questions, RFIs, submittals, and field change requests.
  • Evaluate field conditions and recommend practical engineering solutions.
  • Support resolution of utility conflicts and unforeseen field conditions.
  • Support development and review of record drawings, as-built documentation, and project closeout information.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Engineering Technology, Telecommunications Engineering, or a related discipline plus 2 years of relevant experience, or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
  • Experience supporting civil infrastructure, utility, telecommunications, fiber optic, or OSP design projects.
  • Experience interpreting engineering drawings, specifications, and construction documents.
  • Ability to communicate and coordinate effectively within multidisciplinary and geographically distributed project teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with civil infrastructure, utility design, telecommunications engineering, or OSP design.
  • Proficiency with Autodesk Civil 3D and AutoCAD.
  • Experience with Bluebeam Revu, Microsoft Excel, Smartsheet, utility conflict analysis tools, and digital engineering/model-based design workflows.
  • Experience designing and/or reviewing underground conduit systems and telecommunications infrastructure.
  • Working knowledge of utility coordination, permitting processes, easements, and right-of-way requirements.
  • Experience developing and reviewing plan and profile drawings, construction details, specifications, and permit packages.
  • Experience supporting hyperscale, broadband, municipal, utility, transportation, or data center infrastructure projects.
  • Understanding of underground utility engineering, subsurface utility coordination, and utility conflict analysis.
  • Familiarity with NEC, NESC, DOT requirements, utility accommodation policies, and telecommunications industry standards.
  • Knowledge of fiber optic network architecture and OSP construction practices.
  • Experience performing quantity takeoffs, cost estimating, constructability reviews, and design QA/QC.
  • Experience coordinating telecommunications infrastructure with other civil and utility systems.
  • Professional Engineering (PE) license or Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification preferred but not required.
  • Relocation is not available for this role
  • Sponsorship for US Employment Authorization is not available for this role now or in the future

jobs.excerpt: Bulletproof created a category.  Now we’re writing its next chapter, and we’re looking for the leader who will shape it.
jobs.description:
Bulletproof created a category. Now we’re writing its next chapter, and we’re looking for the leader who will shape it.

As VP of Marketing, you will lead the next chapter of Bulletproof's growth by building a more distinctive brand, creating consumer demand, and developing breakthrough innovation. You will connect deep consumer understanding with exceptional creativity, modern marketing capabilities, and commercially meaningful product innovation. Working closely with our commercial leaders, you will turn brand strength into measurable growth across Retail, Amazon, and DTC.

You report to the CEO and join a highly engaged leadership team. You are a true thought partner: someone who brings a point of view, makes the case for bold choices, and challenges our thinking.

What You Will Do

Creative Excellence: Build a brand people talk about

  • Elevate the quality, originality, and effectiveness of our creative work, building distinctive brand assets and breakthrough campaigns that stand out in culture, on retail shelves, and across digital platforms. Establish a high-performing creative operating model that combines strong strategic briefs, exceptional execution, rapid testing, and measurable results.
  • Set a brand strategy and a creative strategy that work as one and bring them to life in every channel.
  • Partner with the Retail, Marketplaces and DTC channel GMs so marketing fuels growth in each channel.

Turn Brand into Growth

  • Build a modern, full-funnel marketing approach that connects brand investment with customer acquisition, consideration, conversion, and retention.
  • Partner with our channel GMs to improve paid media effectiveness, creative testing, audience targeting, and marketing ROI, while ensuring agencies are held accountable for measurable business outcomes.
  • Specific familiarity with Meta, Google, Amazon Ads, retail media, creator marketing, and marketing measurement

Lead what we make next

  • Make the consumer the starting point for every brand, product and planning decision.
  • Build a consumer insights capability that combines qualitative and quantitative research, behavioral data, purchase drivers, barriers, segmentation, and competitive intelligence. Translate those insights into sharper brand positioning, more effective creative, better channel activation, and innovation platforms that address meaningful consumer needs.
  • Build a multi-year, consumer-led innovation portfolio focused on differentiated propositions, validated demand, meaningful incrementality, and profitable growth. Strengthen our stage-gate process with clear consumer validation, commercial business cases, technical feasibility, and post-launch performance reviews.

Build a team that wins

  • Raise the bar for talent across Brand, Creative, Innovation, and R&D – build capabilities that we are missing and develop leaders who can grow with the business. Set clear goals, ownership, and measures for every function.
  • Be a true thought partner with the leadership team, channel GMs, and entire organization; communicate who owns what, so marketing and channel GMs win together.
  • Model our values, starting with candor: say what needs to be said, and expect the same in return.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you’ll rapidly move from learning the business to leading its growth. By doing so you will have done the following:

1) Built a differentiated, commercially meaningful innovation pipeline that can materially contribute to our 2027–2030 ambitions.

2) Made consumer insights a core organizational capability, informing brand positioning, channel activation, and innovation.

3) Turned marketing into a measurable demand-generation engine, with stronger creative effectiveness and performance marketing capabilities.

4) Built a distinctive, culturally relevant brand that consumers recognize, desire, and choose.

You’re a proven marketing leader with range and desires beyond marketing, and you’re energized by building something bigger. If you meet most of what follows but not all of it, we still want to hear from you.

Required

  • Previous experience in a senior marketing leadership role at a food/beverage consumer packaged goods (CPG) brand, including ownership of brand strategy. Coffee industry experience is strongly preferred. We’ll also welcome candidates from better-for-you CPG or beverage brands who have grown a brand in a crowded, competitive category.
  • The ideal candidate will have both large and small company experience with demonstrated experience achieving growth goals.
  • A track record of leading creative teams or agencies to work that built a brand and achieved growth goals.
  • Experience leading product innovation from consumer insight through launch.
  • A track record of building a multi-year growth strategy that leadership adopted, and of turning it into annual plans and results.
  • Experience presenting to a board, investors or parent-company leadership.
  • Commercial fluency: you read a P&L easily and connect marketing choices to revenue and margin.
  • Strong analytical and financial skill: you can size a market, build a business case and model scenarios with Finance.
  • Experience across more than one sales channel, such as retail, marketplaces and direct to consumer.
  • A record of building and developing strong teams, including leaders of functions outside your own background.
  • The confidence to challenge senior leaders respectfully, and the openness to be challenged in return.

How We Work

  • Remote first. We have no office. You can be based anywhere in the United States (lower 48).
  • Connected. We collaborate on Microsoft Teams across U.S. time zones, and we make time to connect even when we’re miles apart.
  • Your closest partners. The CEO; channel leaders of Retail, Marketplaces and DTC; Operations; Finance and HR.
  • Our values. Candor, Adaptability, Ownership, Connection and Ambition guide how we work together.

Compensation and Benefits

We invest in the people who drive our growth. Annual base salary $250,000 - $275,000. The base salary range represents the anticipated low and high end of the salary range for this position. The base salary is one component of the total compensation package for employees. Other benefits include performance bonus program, generous time-off, flexible schedules, comprehensive health insurance (several options to choose from), 401k program with company match, paid parental leave, company paid disability insurance, and bulletproof.com store discount & credit.

Grupo Mariposa's mission is to nurture growth and foster sustainability within the global food and beverage industry. We are committed to excellence through disciplined management, innovative practices and dynamic culture that embraces change.

Grupo Mariposa is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

At Bulletproof, we craft products to awaken the potential in every coffee aficionado. And we strive to help them transform and build confidence to own tomorrow. We pioneered a category that fused wellness and performance, and we believe now is the time to reclaim our place as one of the most recognizable, talked-about, and culture-shaping brands in health and nutrition.

Job Description

Lead Business Development Manager:

Are you a results-driven leader who combines analytical expertise with a passion for improving business performance? Do you enjoy turning data into meaningful insights, leading high-performing teams, and helping organizations uncover revenue opportunities while mitigating risk? Join us and play a critical role in enabling sales success, optimizing operations, and driving revenue growth across the business.

Key Information:

  • Job Type: Remote

Position Summary:

The Lead Business Development Manager is responsible for identifying, developing, negotiating, and executing strategic partnerships that drive long-term growth, strengthen competitive advantage, and support the acquisition and protection of critical data assets.

This role serves as a key contributor to CARFAX's growth strategy by building relationships with strategic partners, suppliers, data providers, and industry stakeholders across multiple sectors. The position is accountable for creating business value through revenue-generating partnerships, data acquisition opportunities, cost optimization initiatives, and strategic market expansion.

Working closely with Product, Sales, Operations, Finance, Legal, and Executive Leadership, the Lead Business Development Manager evaluates emerging opportunities, develops business cases, negotiates complex commercial agreements, and brings innovative partnership opportunities to market.

Success in this role requires strong commercial acumen, executive-level relationship management, strategic thinking, and the ability to influence both internal and external stakeholders to achieve business objectives.

Position Responsibilities:

Strategic Partnership Development

  • Identify, evaluate, and pursue partnership opportunities that support business growth, product innovation, revenue generation, and data acquisition objectives.
  • Develop business cases, growth projections, and recommendations for new strategic opportunities.
  • Build and maintain a pipeline of high-value partnership opportunities aligned with organizational priorities.
  • Monitor market trends, competitive activity, regulatory developments, and emerging technologies to identify future growth opportunities.

Strategic Relationship Management:

  • Establish and maintain executive-level relationships with strategic partners, suppliers, data providers, and industry stakeholders.
  • Serve as the primary business owner for assigned strategic partnerships.
  • Develop and execute plans to strengthen partner engagement and maximize mutual value creation.
  • Represent CARFAX in external industry discussions, events, and strategic meetings.

Commercial Negotiation & Contract Management:

  • Lead negotiations involving data acquisition agreements, strategic partnerships, licensing arrangements, distribution relationships, and revenue-generating opportunities.
  • Develop commercial models, pricing structures, business cases, and financial forecasts related to partnership opportunities.
  • Collaborate with Legal and Finance teams to ensure agreements appropriately balance risk and opportunity.
  • Manage contract renewals, amendments, and ongoing commercial performance.

Revenue Growth & Value Creation:

  • Identify opportunities to increase revenue, improve profitability, and reduce operating costs through partnership initiatives.
  • Develop strategies to maximize the value and utilization of existing partnerships.
  • Lead pricing discussions and commercial negotiations that support sustainable growth objectives.
  • Evaluate and prioritize opportunities based on strategic and financial impact.

Cross-Functional Leadership:

  • Partner closely with Product, Sales, Operations, Marketing, Legal, Finance, and Data Acquisition teams.
  • Influence product roadmap discussions through industry and partner insights.
  • Support implementation activities related to new partnerships and strategic initiatives.
  • Align internal stakeholders around partnership priorities and business objectives.

Performance Management & Reporting

  • Establish metrics and success criteria for strategic partnership initiatives.
  • Measure partnership performance and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Prepare executive-level presentations, business cases, forecasts, and strategic recommendations.
  • Communicate risks, opportunities, and performance results to leadership on a regular basis.

Minimum Requirements:

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, Commerce, Economics, Marketing, Finance, or a related discipline.
  • MBA or equivalent business education is considered an asset.

Experience:

  • 7+ years of experience in business development, strategic partnerships, enterprise sales, corporate development, consulting, data acquisition, or related commercial leadership roles.
  • Demonstrated success negotiating complex business, licensing, partnership, or commercial agreements.
  • Proven experience building and managing executive-level stakeholder relationships.
  • Experience developing business cases, financial projections, and growth strategies.
  • Track record of identifying and delivering measurable business growth opportunities.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:

  • Strong understanding of strategic partnership development and commercial negotiations.
  • Excellent relationship-building and stakeholder management capabilities.
  • Exceptional communication, presentation, and influencing skills.
  • Strong financial and business acumen.
  • Ability to evaluate complex opportunities and develop actionable recommendations.
  • Experience managing multiple initiatives simultaneously within a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Ability to work effectively across multiple business functions and levels of leadership.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience within automotive, technology, information services, data, insurance, SaaS, or digital marketplace industries.
  • Knowledge of data acquisition, information licensing, data privacy, and information-sharing practices.
  • Existing industry relationships within relevant partner ecosystems.
  • Experience influencing product, distribution, or go-to-market strategies.

The ideal candidate:

  • Thinks strategically while executing effectively.
  • Builds trust and credibility quickly with senior leaders and external stakeholders.

  • Demonstrates sound judgment and business acumen.
  • Takes ownership and accountability for delivering results.

Success in this role will be measured by:

  • Strategic partnerships secured and expanded.
  • Revenue growth generated through partnership initiatives.
  • Acquisition, retention, and enhancement of critical data assets.
  • Cost savings and business value delivered.
  • Achievement of partnership goals and contractual commitments.
