We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. With a global workforce, we’re remote‑first and grounded in a simple idea: software is a people business. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd.

Why You’ll Love This Role

You will help build Cribl Engineering’s AI platform and productivity rails: the shared systems, runtimes, and workflows that let engineers use autonomous AI across the software delivery lifecycle. Instead of one-off prompts or single-feature AI experiments, you will focus on intent engineering, orchestration and harnesses, and production agent infrastructure that other teams can trust and extend.

You will work with a small, high-impact team alongside tech leads, principals, and partner engineering groups. You will ship systems that plan, implement, review, test, and operate work with strong guardrails, then drive adoption until those tools become part of how Cribl builds software. You will also bring a builder mentality: use the product yourself to solve real team and Engineering problems, then turn that lived experience into better systems. Cribl strives to be a great place to work for everyone.

As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will…

  • Design, build, and operate production agentic workflows and the platform harnesses they run on (orchestration, tool integrations, shared context, extension points for other teams)
  • Practice intent engineering: turn goals into clear specifications, rules, constraints, and acceptance criteria that AI systems can execute reliably
  • Stay current on AI tooling and practices, and evangelize what works across Engineering so partners adopt proven patterns
  • Engage hard in design discussions and healthy debate while the direction is open, then pivot with equal energy into implementation once the team decides
  • Build observability and guardrails: tracing, regression detection, human-in-the-loop controls, safe rollout, and operability for agentic systems others depend on
  • Own critical pieces of agent runtime: job isolation, scheduling, execution environments, secrets and access, and production operations in the cloud
  • Design and operate event-driven architectures where it fits (queues, streams, webhooks, async job fan-out) so agentic systems stay scalable and loosely coupled
  • Ship safely and often: keep agentic systems on automated CI/CD paths with progressive delivery and clear rollback
  • Bring a builder mentality: dogfood what we ship. Use the platform to unblock yourself and the team, surface sharp edges, and turn real usage into product and platform improvements
  • Compress software delivery loops by improving how AI helps engineers write, test, review, debug, and validate changes in real repositories and pipelines
  • Partner across Engineering to understand workflows, ship tools that fit how people work, and drive adoption through playbooks, examples, demos, and enablement
  • Evaluate build vs. buy; stay current on models, agent frameworks, MCP-style tool protocols, and the broader AI tooling ecosystem
  • Define and track success metrics for adoption, quality, reliability, and satisfaction; use feedback and data to decide where to invest
  • Partner on security and data access so tools are useful while respecting permissions and company policy
  • Take designed projects from zero to production: own the path from agreed design through implementation, rollout, and day-two operability
  • This position may include stand-by, on-call, or off-hours duties for systems you own


If You’ve Got It - We Want It

  • Staff-level (or equivalent) professional software engineering experience building and operating production distributed systems
  • Strong TypeScript (and modern JavaScript) plus Node.js experience shipping production services; polyglot comfort is welcome, TypeScript is the primary stack for this team
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to ship quickly: design, testing, debugging, APIs/services, and code quality
  • You have lived (or thrived in) a continuous deployment culture: automated pipelines, progressive delivery or safe rollout, monitoring and rollback, and a bias toward frequent, reversible production changes rather than infrequent manual releases
  • Hands-on fluency with modern LLM and agentic coding workflows in production or serious internal platforms (not curiosity-only)
  • Experience building backend services, integrations, automation, and internal tools; comfort across product surfaces when needed
  • Professional experience with agent orchestration, tool-calling systems, evaluation or guardrail techniques, and connecting agents to reliable backend systems
  • Familiarity with agent frameworks, orchestration layers, and integrating external tools and data sources into LLM-based systems (MCP or equivalent experience is a plus)
  • Experience with event-driven systems: queues, streams, pub/sub, webhooks, or similar async patterns in production
  • Observability fluency: metrics, logs, traces, and using them to operate and improve production systems
  • Clear communication, documentation, and teaching ability; comfort driving adoption, not only writing code
  • Good judgment around security, permissions, data access, and safe tool rollout
  • Ability to problem-solve from first principles, make sound trade-offs, and drive work independently through ambiguity
  • Nice to have
    • Hands-on Kubernetes in production
    • Terraform or similar infrastructure-as-code for cloud provisioning
    • Temporal or other workflow-platform experience
    • Deeper AWS / cloud-native ops fluency (IAM, networking, running production workloads end to end)

In addition to base salary, for sales and some sales-adjacent roles, employees are eligible to earn incentive compensation (commission). For all other roles, employees are eligible to participate in the Cribl Corporate Bonus Program.

jobs.description:
Business Development Manager/Director — North America
United States or Canada · Fully Remote · Full-time

We’re looking for a Business Development Manager/Director to grow Trackunit’s enterprise contractor business across North America. You’ll prospect and close new business with enterprise general and specialty contractors, owning the sales process from initial outreach through signed agreement.

You’ll help enterprise general and specialty contractors reduce the operational and project risks that arise when equipment isn’t fully utilized, available, safe, or properly maintained. By connecting real-time equipment and operational data with actionable insights and AI, you’ll show customers how to uncover hidden risks, prevent equipment issues from disrupting entire jobsites, and improve productivity across their operations.

This is an individual contributor role with no people management responsibilities. You can work remotely from the United States or Canada, with travel for customer meetings, jobsite visits, industry events, and team collaboration.

What’s in it for you?

  • The opportunity to grow your sales career at the intersection of construction, connected technology, and AI.

  • Ownership of enterprise opportunities where you can see the connection between your work and customers’ operational results.

  • Collaboration with an international team, bringing together expertise across sales, technology, product, and customer success.

  • Support for your professional development through coaching, feedback, and opportunities to deepen your industry and platform knowledge.

  • A remote working setup in the United States or Canada.

We welcome different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives, and encourage qualified candidates to apply.

Who are you ideally?

  • You bring approximately 3–5 years of successful B2B technology sales experience, including responsibility for prospecting and closing.

  • You have demonstrated experience selling technical platforms to enterprise general contractors and specialty contractors, and understand how these organizations evaluate, purchase, and adopt technology.

  • You have a track record of generating your own pipeline, winning new customers, and meeting or exceeding sales targets.

  • You can navigate complex buying processes involving executive sponsors, operations, equipment management, IT, finance, and procurement.

  • You’re comfortable discussing platform capabilities, data, integrations, and AI use cases in business terms, bringing in technical specialists when needed.

  • You have strong discovery, presentation, negotiation, and closing skills, and build credibility with both field teams and corporate leaders.

  • You manage your territory, opportunities, CRM records, and forecasts with discipline.

  • You work independently, seek feedback, and collaborate effectively to move opportunities forward.

Experience with construction equipment, fleet operations, telematics, IoT, analytics, or AI platforms would be particularly valuable. Familiarity with a structured sales methodology such as MEDDPICC or value-based selling is also helpful.

If this opportunity interests you and you bring relevant contractor platform sales experience, we’d like to hear how your background could contribute.

Primary responsibilities:

  • Build your enterprise pipeline: Identify target general and specialty contractors, develop account plans, and create opportunities through outbound outreach, referrals, networking, events, and collaboration with marketing and sales development.

  • Own the sales cycle: Lead qualification, discovery, presentations, proposals, negotiation, and close, with accountability for quarterly and annual sales targets.

  • Understand customer priorities: Explore how customers manage equipment, jobsites, and operational data, identifying challenges Trackunit can help address.

  • Develop the business case: Connect platform capabilities to measurable outcomes, including improved utilization, productivity, operating costs, and uptime.

  • Build support across accounts: Develop relationships with champions, technical stakeholders, economic buyers, and executive sponsors.

  • Coordinate technical evaluations: Partner with technical colleagues on demonstrations, integration discussions, and evaluations or pilots with clear success criteria.

  • Guide opportunities through purchasing: Manage agreed next steps, stakeholder alignment, security reviews, procurement, and contract discussions.

  • Maintain accurate forecasts: Keep opportunity records current, assess deal risks, and forecast revenue based on evidence and customer commitments.

  • Ensure a strong customer handoff: Align implementation and customer success colleagues on the customer’s goals, requirements, and commercial commitments.

Success in this role means consistently creating qualified opportunities and converting them into new enterprise customers. You build credible business cases, maintain momentum through complex decisions, and set clear expectations for delivery.

Your impact will be measured through:

  • Revenue performance: New customer bookings and achievement of quarterly and annual sales targets.

  • Pipeline creation: The quality and value of qualified opportunities, including those you generate directly.

  • Sales execution: Win rates, opportunity progression, and effective management of sales cycles.

  • Forecasting discipline: Forecast accuracy and clear documentation of stakeholders, risks, and next steps.

Compensation and rewards

The base salary hiring range for this role is $100,000 to $ 150,000 per year, depending on experience and qualifications.
Once in the role, successful candidates will have the opportunity to progress through the full salary range based on performance and development over time. This range reflects base salary only and does not include additional elements of our total rewards offering, such as our remote work policy, health benefits, retirement savings, and other rewards.

Our hiring process

  • Don't waste your time on writing the perfect cover letter for the job. We want you to create an impact that matters, and that's not in the cover letter.

  • Initial phone conversation with a colleague from our People & Talent team to get to know each other a bit better.

  • Virtual meet and greet. Meet with the hiring manager to explore your experience, motivations, and the opportunity.

  • Team interview. We want you to get an insight into some of the concrete work tasks or challenges related to the role. You will be discussing cases during the interview together with relevant colleagues from across Trackunit, who you’ll also work closely with in the job.

  • Offer presentation and walk-through. We’re lucky to have you!

Coming Together To Connect Construction

Trackunit is a global construction technology company on a mission to eliminate downtime by connecting people, equipment, and processes. For more than two decades, we’ve helped advance the industry through connected technology. Today, our platform brings together equipment and operational data, using analytics and AI to help contractors, rental companies, and equipment manufacturers improve visibility, make smarter decisions, and operate more efficiently.

People are central to that mission. Our global team collaborates across offices, regions, and remote workplaces, bringing different perspectives to the challenges our customers face. Together, we’re building a more connected, productive construction industry.

Are you in?

jobs.excerpt: Description: As the Information Security Manager, you will lead the strategic development and oversight of our organization’s cybersecurity program within a fast-paced software development environment.
jobs.description:
Description:

As the Information Security Manager, you will lead the strategic development and oversight of our organization’s cybersecurity program within a fast-paced software development environment. You will be responsible for defining security roadmaps, managing risk across our software delivery pipeline, and ensuring our products meet the highest standards of data protection. You will bridge the gap between technical engineering teams and executive leadership, translating complex security threats into actionable business risk assessments. This role is pivotal in maintaining our competitive edge by ensuring that security is a core component of our brand and customer trust.

Key Areas of Responsibility:

  • Security Program Leadership: Design and manage the enterprise-wide information security strategy, aligning security initiatives with software development lifecycles (SDLC) and business goals.
  • Risk Management & Governance: Lead comprehensive risk assessments and vendor security reviews to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities across third-party integrations and internal systems.
  • DevSecOps Integration: Collaborate with engineering leads to integrate security automation (SAST/DAST) into CI/CD pipelines, promoting a "shift-left" security culture.
  • Incident Response Management: Oversee the security incident response program, acting as the primary point of escalation and lead investigator during high-priority security events.
  • Regulatory & Compliance Oversight: Ensure continuous compliance with industry-standard frameworks such as SOC2, ISO 27001, and GDPR, managing external audits and certification processes.
  • Security Awareness & Culture: Develop and lead security training programs for non-technical staff and specialized secure-coding workshops for developers.
  • Stakeholder Communication: Present regular security posture reports to senior management and board members, providing data-driven recommendations for security investments.

Objectives:

  • Maintain the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of our SaaS platforms and customer data environments.
  • Minimize organizational risk by implementing robust security controls across the software development and deployment processes.
  • Achieve and maintain industry-leading security certifications (e.g., SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, NIST) along with compliance with our parent company’s policies
  • Foster a proactive security-first mindset across all departments through education and transparent reporting.

Skills:

  • Strategic Leadership: Ability to lead technical teams and influence organizational change without direct authority.
  • Complex Problem-Solving: Expert at analyzing evolving cyber threats and designing creative, scalable mitigation strategies.
  • Effective Communication: Translating deeply technical security vulnerabilities into business-impact terms for executive stakeholders.
  • Regulatory Knowledge: Deep understanding of software-relevant compliance standards (NIST, SOC2, ISO).
  • Technical Proficiency: Familiarity with cloud security (AWS/Azure/GCP), containerization, and automated security testing tools.

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Management Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Master’s degree in a specific area of specialization, such as IT security, may be beneficial.
  • 7–10+ years of experience in information security, with at least 3 years in a leadership or management capacity.
  • Proven experience in a software development or "Software as a Service" (SaaS) environment.
  • Relevant Certifications: CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional) or CISM (Certified Information Security Manager) is highly preferred.

Additional Attributes:

  • Innovative and creative thinking: Ability to anticipate future security trends and prepare the organization accordingly.
  • Composure: Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and remain calm during active security incidents.
  • Strong attention to detail: Ensuring precision in security policy and implementation.
  • Empathy: Balances the need for strict security controls with developers' operational needs to remain productive.

Travel:

  • Occasional travel between Orlando and Pittsburgh offices or for security conferences and audits.

With a career at The Home Depot, you can be yourself and also be part of something bigger.

Position Purpose:

The Salesforce Engineering team is responsible for scaling Home Depot's Pro CRM and enterprise Salesforce ecosystem, and for expanding our use of AI-driven development to accelerate delivery and modernize how we build, test, and migrate Salesforce solutions. The Staff Software Engineer is the technical anchor for the team, setting architecture direction for Salesforce development, integration, and release patterns, and partnering closely with the Engineering Manager, Product Manager, and Principal Engineer. This person owns hard technical decisions on complex Salesforce initiatives, drives disciplined adherence to PDLC/SDLC methodology, and balances delivery speed with long-term platform scalability, security, and maintainability.

In this role you will:

  • Lead end-to-end Salesforce solution design and development – Apex, Lightning Web Components (LWC), Flow, and declarative configuration – across Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, and custom Salesforce applications.
  • Architect and build integrations between Salesforce and enterprise systems using REST/SOAP APIs, Platform Events, Bulk API, and middleware.
  • Own the technical governance of code and configuration migration and release management across sandboxes and production orgs, ensuring adherence to PDLC/SDLC methodology, version control, and CI/CD best practices.
  • Partner with Salesforce admins on user maintenance, licensing, and the security model – profiles, permission sets, and sharing rules – as well as ongoing platform administration.
  • Bring AI into the daily engineering workflow, from AI-assisted development and code review to building AI-powered features directly into Salesforce experiences.
  • Set the technical bar: lead architecture reviews, mentor engineers at every level, and raise the standard for code quality across the team.
  • Partner directly with Product, IT leadership, and cross-functional engineering teams to turn ambiguous business requirements into scalable, shippable Salesforce solutions.

Key Responsibilities:

  • 50% Delivery and Execution – Develops, tests, deploys, and maintains Salesforce solutions with a clear understanding of the business value they provide; takes a broad, enterprise view when approaching integration and platform challenges; builds automated test suites to enable rapid, reliable deployment to production; takes on complex technical challenges with urgency and ownership, consistently delivering results even under tight timelines.
  • 10% Learns and Grows – Actively pursues growth in Salesforce, AI, and cloud technologies through formal and informal channels; learns through both successful and failed experiments when tackling new integration or migration challenges.
  • 20% Plans and Aligns – Creates new and better ways for the organization to scale its Salesforce platform; communicates clearly across technical and non-technical audiences; partners with the Product team to ensure user stories are developer-ready, well-scoped, and testable; collaborates within agile/PDLC processes; adapts approach to shifting business priorities.
  • 20% Supports and Enables – Fields questions from Product, IT, and business teams on Salesforce capabilities; mentors engineers on Salesforce development standards and AI-assisted engineering practices; identifies platform gaps and proposes improvements to development and release processes.

  • This position typically repots to Software Engineer Manager or Sr. Manager
  • This position has 0 Direct Reports

  • No travel required.

Physical Requirements:

  • Most of the time is spent sitting in a comfortable position and there is frequent opportunity to move about. On rare occasions there may be a need to move or lift light articles.

Working Conditions:

  • Located in a comfortable indoor area. Any unpleasant conditions would be infrequent and not objectionable.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Must be eighteen years of age or older.
  • Must be legally permitted to work in the United States.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience, with deep, hands-on expertise in Salesforce development and integration.
  • Salesforce expert-level development – Hands-on, expert-level experience with Apex, Lightning Web Components, Flow, SOQL/SOSL,Platform Event triggers and the Salesforce security/sharing model, not just declarative configuration.
  • Integration architecture – Proven experience designing and building integrations between Salesforce and external systems using REST/SOAP APIs, Platform Events, Bulk API, and middleware.
  • Staff-level technical leadership – Track record leading technical direction on complex, cross-team Salesforce initiatives: architecture design, modernization, and refactors at scale.
  • PDLC/SDLC methodology – Deep familiarity applying structured Product/Software Development Life Cycle methodology to plan, govern, and deliver Salesforce releases.
  • Code migration – Hands-on experience managing code and configuration migration across sandboxes and production orgs, including release/version management and rollback planning.
  • Salesforce user maintenance – Experience with user provisioning, licensing, profiles, permission sets, and ongoing org administration.
  • AI development – Experience building AI-powered features or using AI tools (e.g., Claude Code and similar) as part of the daily engineering workflow to accelerate delivery.

jobs.description:
Are you passionate about making a difference in people's lives? Do you enjoy working in a service-oriented industry? If so, this opportunity may be the right fit for you!

The Process Improvement Specialist is responsible for evaluating, improving, and streamlining workflows across Clinical Operations to increase efficiency, reduce unnecessary manual work, and support scalable service delivery. This role works closely with operational teams to understand existing processes, identify opportunities for improvement, and develop practical solutions that simplify, standardize, and better organize work. This includes optimizing manual workflows, improving coordination across teams and systems, and leveraging available business tools, AI-enabled technologies and lightweight automation where appropriate. In addition to optimizing existing workflows, the Process Improvement Specialist supports the design and operational development of new clinical programs and services, helping ensure that processes are efficient, practical, and scalable from the outset. This position serves as a bridge between immediate operational needs and longer-term technology enhancements, identifying and implementing improvements that can be achieved through existing business tools while collaborating with Product and Development teams on solutions requiring more advanced technical capabilities.


This role…

  • Process Analysis and Workflow Improvement

· Work directly with Clinical Operations teams to develop a thorough understanding of existing workflows, processes, and operational challenges.

· Document current-state workflows, including process steps, system interactions, manual activities, and dependencies.

· Identify inefficiencies, redundant activities, bottlenecks, and opportunities to simplify or eliminate unnecessary work.

· Identify opportunities to better coordinate and connect related workflows, activities, systems, and teams to reduce duplication, unnecessary handoffs, and operational complexity.

· Optimize processes that must remain manual by improving the organization, sequencing, standardization, and coordination of activities to maximize efficiency and minimize unnecessary effort.

· Design and document improved future-state workflows that support operational efficiency, quality, and scalability.

· Collaborate with operational leaders and frontline staff to validate proposed changes and ensure solutions address practical business needs.

· Maintain documentation of existing and redesigned workflows, including process maps and standard operating procedures.

  • Process Optimization and Practical Solution Development

· Develop practical solutions that improve workflow efficiency through process simplification, better organization, standardization, and the effective use of existing business tools, including AI-enabled technologies, and lightweight automation where appropriate.

· Research, develop, and test practical process improvements using approved tools such as ChatGPT, Microsoft Excel, and other accessible business applications.

· Evaluate proposed solutions for effectiveness, usability, accuracy, and operational feasibility prior to implementation.

Our Why At Dotmatics

At Dotmatics, a Siemens company, we believe science, data, and decision-making must be deeply intertwined for innovation to thrive. Our Portfolio includes Luma, LumaLab Connect, ELN Platform, Graphpad Prism, Geneious, SnapGene, Protein Metrics, OMIQ, FCS Express, LabArchives, NQuery, EasyPanel, SoftGenetics and Virscidian.

We have a vision for a new Lab of the Future that will change the future of scientific research.

We have created the world’s most comprehensive digital science platform – best-of-breed software applications already used by more than 2 million scientists, together in a single ecosystem united by a powerful, flexible enterprise data platform. This is not flat data buried away in digital graveyards. This is dynamic, multi-dimensional decision-making.

Scientific enterprises need a new level of effectiveness to achieve tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Illness will not wait. The biosphere will not wait. We are tireless in our vision, because the time for innovation is now.

Shaping the Future of Science At Dotmatics

Our global team of more than 800 colleagues are dedicated to supporting our customers in over 180 countries. Together, with our scientific community of users, we accelerate scientific innovation in order to make the world a healthier, cleaner, and safer place to live.

You’ll join a collaborative, global team pushing the boundaries of scientific innovation. Your ideas and efforts will have a tangible impact, accelerating scientific progress and discovery. We offer a dynamic, remote-friendly environment that fosters high integrity and collaboration, empowering you to excel. Dotmatics is a company built by scientists, for scientists. Combined, we are now the world’s largest cloud-based scientific research R&D platform. We need your help to keep growing and pioneering the future.

We are Science Driven. We are Customer Centric. We are Better Together.

What do we need

As a Manual Exploratory Tester (User Testing) , you will play a critical role in validating the quality of our Luma platform. You will focus on exploratory/user testing—investigating new features, workflows, and edge cases to uncover unexpected behaviours and usability issues. You’ll work closely with developers, product owners, and automation engineers to ensure defects are caught early, well-documented, and resolved quickly.

A background in science (chemistry, biology, or related field) is required as you will understand the scientific workflows and real-world use cases of our customers.

In this role you will get to:

  • Conduct exploratory and manual testing (UAT) across web-based applications within the Luma platform.
  • Develop tests/exploratory test guides to ensure business requirements are met and provide detailed feedback to design/product.
  • Validate new features, integrations, and scientific workflows, ensuring functionality aligns with product requirements and user expectations.
  • Log clear, reproducible bug reports and collaborate with developers for quick resolution.
  • Provide critical feedback on usability, scientific workflow efficiency, and overall user experience.
  • Collaborate with automation engineers to identify areas suitable for automated coverage and review assertions.
  • Participate in sprint planning, backlog refinement, and release readiness activities.
  • Advocate for quality throughout the software development lifecycle.

We are looking for people who have an education in, or significant work experience in Biology, Chemistry, Bioinformatics, Life Sciences or similar scientific field and can demonstrate experience as a User Tester, Scientific Application administrator/owner, Software Tester, QA Analyst/User Testing, with a strong focus on exploratory testing

The key skills we are looking for

  • Extensive knowledge of biology or chemistry, with the ability to understand and test scientific user experiences and workflows.
  • Experience using or testing scientific/informatics software, ideally within a scientific environment.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with curiosity to probe beyond obvious test cases.
  • Excellent attention to detail and ability to spot inconsistencies, edge cases and usability issues.
  • Personal experience using AI-driven tools and workflows to support day-to-day work.
  • Understanding of SaaS architecture, integrations and security.

You may also have:

  • Experience testing SaaS or complex web applications
  • Familiarity with tools such as Jira, Zephyr Scale, or similar test management/bug tracking systems
  • Hands-on experience with backend validation, including API testing and database checks
  • Calling APIs with tools like Postman/Bruno
  • Practical knowledge of GraphQL, including querying, mutations, and schema validation
  • experience with backend validation of APIs, services, and database interactions to ensure data integrity and system reliability.
  • Tools like Postman/Bruno for RESTful API testing and validate GraphQL queries/mutations against backend services.

Research shows us the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting outstanding candidates, so please don’t hesitate to apply — we’d love to hear from you.

Please review the job details below.

Lanteris Space LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Intuitive Machines, is seeking a Senior Cybersecurity Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) Engineer responsible for advancing the organization’s enterprise cybersecurity governance, risk management, and compliance programs. This role can be based remotely in the US. This role leads enterprise cybersecurity assessments, policy development, compliance initiatives, third-party risk management activities, and cybersecurity governance operations. While the position is primarily enterprise-focused, it may also support customer and program-specific cybersecurity requirements as needed. The position partners with IT, Engineering, Supply Chain, Legal, Contracts, and business stakeholders to ensure cybersecurity risks are identified, managed, and communicated appropriately while supporting regulatory, contractual, customer, and corporate requirements. This position reports to the GRC Lead.

Intuitive Machines is a leading space infrastructure company that builds spacecraft, connects networks, and operates infrastructure-as-a-service for commercial, civil, and national security customers. With a proven track record across the space domain, the Company, through organic growth and portfolio expansion, has built over 300 spacecraft, delivered over 260 kilograms of payload to the lunar surface, and provided precision navigation expertise that has guided spacecraft across our solar system.

Responsibilities:

  • Conduct cybersecurity risk assessments for enterprise systems, software, suppliers, vendors, and business initiatives, with support for customer or program-specific environments as needed.
  • Maintain cybersecurity risk registers and track remediation activities through closure.
  • Develop and maintain cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures, and governance documentation.
  • Provide cybersecurity guidance and consultation to technical and business stakeholders.
  • Support compliance initiatives related to NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171, CMMC, RMF, SOX, and other applicable frameworks and requirements.

  • Conduct vendor risk assessments, software risk assessments, and third-party cybersecurity reviews.
  • Support supply chain risk management activities and cybersecurity due diligence efforts.
  • Administer and maintain the organization’s GRC platform, including framework mappings, control management, evidence collection, continuous monitoring, and compliance reporting.
  • Develop metrics, dashboards, and reports that communicate cybersecurity risk and compliance posture to leadership.

  • Must be U.S. citizen with the ability to obtain a secret level security clearance.

  • Experience conducting cybersecurity risk assessments and compliance evaluations.
  • Experience developing cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures, and security documentation.
  • Working knowledge of security frameworks such as NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171, RMF, and CMMC.
  • Experience with vendor risk management and cybersecurity supply chain risk management.
  • Current CompTIA Security+ certification or an equivalent baseline cybersecurity certification.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience administering GRC platforms such as Vanta, ServiceNow GRC, Archer, Hyperproof, AuditBoard, Drata, or similar solutions.
  • Experience managing framework mappings, control libraries, compliance evidence, continuous monitoring, and audit-readiness activities.
  • Experience supporting SOX-related audits or cybersecurity and IT general control assessments.
  • Experience supporting federal, aerospace, defense, NASA, DoD, or other regulated environments.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with demonstrated ability to collaborate cross-functionally with engineers, program management, and compliance stakeholders to drive security outcomes in a matrixed environment
  • Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, CGRC, CISA, or SecurityX.

Are you passionate about software-defined networking, secure connectivity, and making large-scale cloud infrastructure safe to change?

Join our Site Reliability team

The Cloud Networking SRE team designs, deploys, and maintains the applications and infrastructure behind Akamai Cloud's networking products. Our VPC and Cloud Firewall stack gives customers isolated private networks, stateful traffic filtering, and secure site-to-site and multi-cloud connectivity.

Help us shape the future of the Internet

In this role, you will own day-to-day reliability of our private networking, firewall, and IPSec Gateway services. You'll work with software engineering, product, and operations teams to ship dataplane and control-plane changes safely across a global fleet. You will run release rollouts, automate operational toil, build monitoring, and troubleshoot customer-impacting networking issues down to the packet. You will use open-source tools alongside internal Akamai tooling.

As a Site Reliability Engineer II, you will be responsible for:

  • Planning and executing phased rollouts of VPC and Cloud Firewall dataplane binaries and feature-flag enablements
  • Operating and troubleshooting private networking (subnets, routing, overlay/encapsulation) and stateful firewall rule enforcement on Linux hosts.
  • Supporting operation and readiness of the IPSec Gateway and Multi-Cloud Networking services, including tunnel health, IKE/IPsec negotiation issues, and cross-cloud connectivity.
  • Automating rollout steps, health checks, and recurring operational tasks using Python, Shell, and SaltStack.
  • Building and maintaining Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, alerts, and runbooks; support and improve SLOs for VPC, Cloud Firewall, and IPSec Gateway.
  • Joining on-call and incident triage for networking issues, drive mitigation to reduce MTTR, and contribute to post-mortem reviews and follow-up actions.
  • Contributing to Technical Readiness Reviews (TRRs) for new features, and keep SOPs and team knowledge bases current.

  • Have 2 years of relevant experience and a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or its equivalent
  • Have an understanding of core networking: TCP/IP, subnetting, L2/L3 routing, NAT, DNS, and stateful firewalling.
  • Possess hands-on Linux networking experience: network namespaces, bridges, virtual interfaces, iptables/nftables, and connection tracking (conntrack).

jobs.description:
Director of Product Marketing

Boston, MA, USA (Boston preferred; remote candidates in the US will be considered)

Summary

QuEra Computing is the leader in commercializing quantum computers using neutral atoms, which is widely recognized as a highly promising quantum modality. Based in Boston and built on pioneering research from nearby Harvard University and MIT, we are developing large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computers to tackle classically intractable problems. QuEra operates the world’s largest publicly accessible quantum computer, available over a major public cloud and for on-premises delivery. We are passionate about both the science we advance and the inclusive, collaborative culture we cultivate.

We are seeking a Director of Product Marketing to own how the market understands QuEra’s products and progress. Quantum computing is a field where bold claims are common and trust is scarce. Your job is to do the opposite of hype: translate real technical achievements, from error-correction milestones to system-level capabilities, into positioning, messaging, and sales tools that are specific, credible, and effective with the world’s most demanding technical buyers.

You will work across QuEra’s full portfolio, including our Gemini-class systems, the Aquila analog quantum computer, premium cloud access, and on-premise deployments, and across our three core market segments: HPC centers, national quantum programs, and enterprise innovators. You will report to the Chief Commercial Officer and partner daily with product management, quantum scientists, and the commercial team.

Why this role exists

You will own the bridge between QuEra’s technical roadmap and the market’s understanding of it, turning cutting-edge science into positioning that helps customers choose QuEra with confidence.

Responsibilities

  • Own positioning and messaging: Develop and maintain messaging frameworks for QuEra’s systems and services, tailored to HPC centers, national programs, and enterprise innovators, and keep them current as our roadmap advances.
  • Translate the science: Work closely with quantum scientists, QEC researchers, and product managers to convert technical milestones and publications into market-facing narratives that survive expert scrutiny.
  • Enable the commercial team: Create and maintain the tools sales needs to win: presentations, battlecards, one-pagers, objection-handling guides, and proposal content, and measure whether they work.
  • Drive competitive intelligence: Track competing quantum modalities and vendors, maintain clear and honest positioning versus superconducting, trapped-ion, and photonic approaches, and brief internal teams on market shifts.
  • Support product launches: Partner with product management and communications on launch messaging, web content, webinars, analyst briefings, and conference presence.
  • Be the voice of the market: Bring segment and win/loss insights back into product and roadmap discussions so that customer needs shape what we build and how we talk about it.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in physics, engineering, computer science, or a related technical field.
  • 8+ years of B2B product marketing or technical marketing experience in deep tech, such as quantum computing, HPC, semiconductors, scientific instruments, or enterprise infrastructure.
  • Demonstrated ability to master complex technical subject matter and write about it with precision and clarity; strong preference for specificity over hype.
  • Track record of building messaging frameworks and sales enablement assets that measurably improved commercial outcomes.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; comfortable engaging both PhD-level scientists and executive buyers.
  • Experience running cross-functional projects with product, science, sales, and communications teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in a technical field or an MBA.
  • Working knowledge of quantum computing concepts (qubits, error correction, logical qubits, quantum modalities) and the quantum vendor ecosystem.
  • Experience marketing to government programs, national laboratories, or HPC centers, including familiarity with public procurement dynamics.
  • Experience supporting analyst relations and public speaking at industry events.
  • A portfolio of technical marketing content: messaging frameworks, launch materials, white papers, or competitive analyses.

QuEra is committed to cultivating a diverse work environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We highly value diversity in our current and future employees and do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The approximate base salary range for this position is $200,000 to $245,000

jobs.description:
Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the country in which the role is being hired. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment visa at this time.

Grants Strategy Manager

Mark43’s mission is to empower communities and their governments with new technologies that improve the safety and quality of life for all. We build powerful, scalable, and elegant software that sets a new standard for the tools upon which our first responders rely. Our users are diverse, and we are therefore committed to embracing diversity of thought and experience within our team.

We are looking for a Grants Strategy Manager to join our Business Development & Capture organization. In this role, you will serve as Mark43’s in-house expert on grant funding for state, local, and tribal public safety agencies — helping our customers identify, pursue, and use grant funding to acquire and deploy Mark43 capabilities as authorized expenses. You will work as a customer-facing advisor, plugging into active sales pursuits where grant funding is a meaningful factor, and operating as a strategic partner to the Account Executives and Proposal Managers running those deals.

This is an individual contributor role for someone who has spent their career at the intersection of public safety operations and grant funding, and who knows how to translate agency needs into compelling, fundable proposals. You will work closely with Mark43’s Account Executives, Proposal Managers, and the Federal Capture Manager, and will report to the VP of Business Development & Capture. Beyond deal support, you will identify funding-led account development opportunities — agencies that are strong grant candidates and represent good inroads for Mark43 — and bring those to Sales as a prospecting motion. Over time, you will help build the operating structure for grants strategy across the broader Mark43 customer base.

What You’ll Do

If you were part of our team last week, here are some things you would have done:

  • Joined a capture call with an Account Executive and a state agency prospect to advise on the federal and state grant programs that could fund their planned RMS, CAD, or analytics modernization — and outlined the timeline and steps the agency would need to take to be ready for the next funding cycle.
  • Reviewed an upcoming BJA, COPS Office, or DOJ solicitation, identified Mark43 customers and prospects whose needs map to it, and brought a prioritized target list to the relevant Account Executives.
  • Worked with a customer agency to scope a project narrative that aligns Mark43 capabilities with the funding agency’s priorities and allowable cost categories, and supported the customer’s grant writing efforts where appropriate and permissible.
  • Advised an agency on the structure of a multi-year project plan that uses grant funding for initial deployment, with clear paths to sustainment funding once the grant period ends.
  • Identified an agency that is an excellent grant candidate but currently has no active engagement with Mark43, and brought that opportunity to the Account Executive responsible for the territory as a funding-led account development inroad.
  • Partnered with a Proposal Manager on an active solicitation response, contributing the funding strategy section and ensuring our proposal speaks credibly to the customer’s funding pathway.
  • Tracked the federal and state grants calendar, surfaced upcoming opportunities to the Sales team, and helped translate funding signals into account-level pursuit actions.
  • Coordinated the orderly transition of work currently performed by an external grants research vendor into our in-house function, building the playbook, templates, and operating cadence that will support the function long-term.
  • Educated Account Executives on how to recognize grant-funded opportunities, what questions to ask customers about funding, and when to engage you in a deal.
  • Worked with the Federal Capture Manager and the Federal Capture Analyst on cross-over opportunities where federal grant programs intersect with state and local pursuits.

What You’ll Need

We’re looking for a Grants Strategy Manager with deep, hands-on experience securing and managing grant funding for public safety agencies, and who has worked the customer-facing side of the grants motion in a vendor or consulting capacity. This experience matters because the role requires the judgment to advise customers credibly, the operational fluency to plug into active sales pursuits without slowing them down, and the discipline to operate within the legal and ethical boundaries of a vendor supporting customer grant activities.

You should also bring:

  • Significant experience (typically 7+ years) in grant strategy, grant writing, or strategic funding roles supporting public safety, law enforcement, or emergency management agencies.
  • Demonstrated track record of securing federal and state grant funding, including programs administered by the COPS Office, Bureau of Justice Assistance (BJA), Department of Justice, Department of Homeland Security, FEMA, and comparable state agencies.
  • Hands-on familiarity with the federal grants ecosystem — SAM.gov, Grants.gov, agency-specific portals, NOFO and NOFA cycles, allowable cost categories, match requirements, and post-award compliance and reporting.
  • Strong understanding of state and local grant funding mechanisms, pass-through funding, and the budget cycles of state and local public safety agencies.
  • Direct operational experience in a public safety or law enforcement agency — enough to credibly advise customers on how grant funding intersects with operational needs, procurement processes, and the realities of implementing technology in active environments.
  • Experience working with or for technology vendors that serve public safety agencies, including familiarity with how grant strategy supports customer technology procurement decisions.
  • Strong writing, editing, and communication skills, with the ability to produce clear, compelling, and well-organized funding strategy artifacts and proposal content.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple opportunities, deadlines, and customer engagements simultaneously.
  • Experience partnering with sales, business development, and account management teams in support of customer pursuits.
  • Practical understanding of the legal and ethical boundaries of vendor support for customer grant activities, and the judgment to operate cleanly within them.
  • Bachelor’s degree preferred. Certifications such as Certified Grants Management Specialist (CGMS) or Grant Professional Certified (GPC) are a plus.
  • Passion for supporting public safety, government modernization, and mission-critical technology.

People who thrive on our team also tend to share the following characteristics:

  • Customer-first and trusted. You build trust quickly with public safety customers and earn the right to advise them on consequential decisions about funding and technology.
  • Structured and dependable. You bring order to ambiguity, keep teams on track, and create repeatable processes that make grants strategy more effective and scalable over time.
  • Collaborative and mission-aligned. You enjoy working across teams, value shared success, and care deeply about the public safety mission behind the work.
  • Strategic and proactive. You look ahead, identify funding opportunities and risks early, and help customers and internal teams make thoughtful decisions on the pursuits where grants are a meaningful factor.

Where You’ll Work

Mark43 is a remote-friendly company. For this role, we welcome candidates from across the continental U.S. Occasional travel for customer meetings, conferences, and internal planning sessions is expected.

Mark43 is approved to hire in Canada, the UK, and 36 U.S. states, including Alabama, Arizona, California (excluding San Francisco), Colorado, Connecticut, Washington D.C., Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Massachusetts, Maryland, Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, North Carolina, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin, and West Virginia. Before applying to a remote role, please ensure that you are able to perform the position in one of the states listed above. State locations and specifics are subject to change as our hiring requirements shift.

Our Privacy Notice describes how Mark43 uses and protects the personal information of prospective employees during the recruitment process. It informs you about our handling of the personal information you provide to us when you apply for a position in our organization and in general when you express your interest in joining our team.

As a part of Mark43's security measures all employees must: Engage in appropriate use of the company's electronic information resources; Become knowledgeable about and follow relevant security policies and guidelines; Protect the resources under their control, such as passwords, computers, and data that they create, receive, or download; and Promptly report security-related incidents and violations, and responding to official reports of security incidents involving their systems or accounts.

Mark43 is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or genetic information. As part of this commitment, we will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed, please email requesting the accommodation.

jobs.title: Senior Clinical Reimbursement Specialist
jobs.excerpt: At Veracyte, we offer exciting career opportunities for those interested in joining a pioneering team that is committed to transforming cancer care for patients across the globe.
jobs.description:
At Veracyte, we offer exciting career opportunities for those interested in joining a pioneering team that is committed to transforming cancer care for patients across the globe. Working at Veracyte enables our employees to not only make a meaningful impact on the lives of patients, but to also learn and grow within a purpose driven environment. This is what we call the Veracyte way – it’s about how we work together, guided by our values, to give clinicians the insights they need to help patients make life-changing decisions.

Our Values:

  • We Seek A Better Way: We pursue bold ideas, embrace complexity, and keep pushing forward.
  • We Make It Happen: We act with urgency, deliver with excellence, and always find a way.
  • We Are Stronger Together: We engage with empathy, align around what's best for Veracyte, and celebrate as one team.
  • We Care Deeply: We show up with integrity, kindness, and respect for one another.

The Position:

We are seeking an experienced Senior Clinical Reimbursement Specialist to serve as a clinical subject matter expert on our Clinical Reimbursement Operations team. In this role, you will independently manage complex pre- and post-service appeals, mentor junior team members, and drive process improvements that measurably improve overturn rates and revenue capture across the revenue cycle.

You will apply advanced clinical judgment and deep payer policy expertise to handle the team's most complex, high-dollar, and precedent-setting cases - including Level 2 appeals, external reviews, and payer escalations. Beyond individual casework, you will contribute to workflow design, SOP development, and cross-functional initiatives that strengthen the team's overall performance.

Success in this role requires advanced knowledge of reimbursement systems (including payer utilization management and claims adjudication), fluency in payer medical policies, sound and independent clinical judgment on complex cases, and the ability to influence outcomes through both direct case ownership and informal leadership.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Independently manage complex pre- and post-service appeals across Level 1, Level 2, and external review pathways, including the review, development, and submission of clinically robust appeal documentation.
  • Serve as a clinical subject matter expert on payer medical policies, translating complex policy criteria into patient-specific clinical justification and guiding appeal strategy for high-dollar, ambiguous, or precedent-setting cases.
  • Own end-to-end resolution of assigned cases, including follow-up, coordination with ordering providers, and appropriate escalation to leadership when warranted.
  • Partner with ordering physicians and practice staff to coordinate peer-to-peer reviews, gather supplemental clinical documentation, secure Authorized Representative forms and signatures, and support collaborative initiatives that strengthen appeal outcomes.
  • Mentor and provide informal guidance to Clinical Reimbursement Specialists, including case review, appeal letter quality feedback, and coaching on payer policy interpretation.
  • Lead analysis of denial patterns and appeal outcomes to identify root causes, and drive upstream feedback to reduce future denials.
  • Contribute directly to the development and refinement of appeal letter templates, clinical evidence packets, payer reference guides, and other scalable operational tools.
  • Monitor payer behavior and policy changes across all lines of business; flag material changes and partner with leadership on remediations, coverage reviews, and payer escalations.
  • Support the maintenance and continuous improvement of SOPs, ensuring workflows remain consistent, compliant, and scalable as the team grows.
  • Serve as point of contact for complex patient- or provider-facing inquiries, ensuring accurate, empathetic, and compliant communication.
  • Support digital transformation initiatives, including automation and AI/agentic workflow pilots that improve appeal readiness scoring and clinical documentation review.
  • Represent the Clinical Reimbursement team in cross-functional initiatives and special projects that support evolving reimbursement and operational priorities.

Who You Are:

Qualifications

Required

  • Active clinical licensure (e.g., RN, NP).

jobs.excerpt: Who We Are BioMarin is a leading rare disease biotechnology company focused on genetically defined conditions.
jobs.description:
Who We Are

BioMarin is a leading rare disease biotechnology company focused on genetically defined conditions.

Guided by our purpose to develop medicines that make a profound impact on people’s lives, our global teams have delivered a portfolio of therapies since our founding in 1997. Our revolutionary treatments for conditions like achondroplasia (the most common form of dwarfism), PKU (phenylketonuria), CLN2, a form of Batten disease, and a number of forms of MPS (mucopolysaccharidosis) offer new possibilities for patients and families who previously had few, if any, available options. More recently, with the close of the Amicus acquisition, our portfolio has expanded to include therapies for Fabry disease and Pompe disease, expanding our ability to reach more people living with rare genetic conditions.

Our success comes from our unwavering commitment to excellence, our deep understanding of patient needs, our scientific expertise, and our world-class manufacturing capabilities. At the heart of BioMarin is a dedicated team of the brightest minds in the industry working together to deliver innovative therapies to patients and families around the world.

About Commercial

Be part of the worldwide infrastructure that gets our drugs to underserved patients around the world. Our global sales force solidifies BioMarin’s commercial presence in the United States and Europe and is rapidly growing in other regions, such as South America, EuMEA, and Asia-Pacific.

Position Overview
BioMarin is a global biotechnology company focused on developing and delivering therapies that provide meaningful advances for people living with serious and life-threatening rare genetic diseases. The Patient Education Specialist will help patients, caregivers, and families better understand rare diseases, available support resources, and the practical considerations associated with navigating care.
The initial focus of this role will include phenylketonuria (PKU), a rare inherited metabolic condition that requires lifelong management and often involves complex nutritional considerations. This is a remote inside sales position: the specialist will conduct proactive outbound calls and virtual outreach to eligible patients and caregivers, delivering clear, empathetic, non-promotional education through approved scripts, programs, and materials, while partnering closely with healthcare professionals, patient services, advocacy organizations, and internal teams.

Role emphasis: remote inside sales, proactive patient and caregiver phone and virtual outreach, health literacy, nutrition-informed engagement, and connection to appropriate support resources.

Position Summary

The ideal candidate is an experienced patient educator who can make complex clinical and nutritional information understandable, relevant, and actionable. A Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN), licensed dietitian, or professional with a strong dietetics or metabolic nutrition background is strongly preferred, particularly someone who has supported individuals with PKU or other inherited metabolic or rare diseases.
This remote, inside-sales role requires strong phone and virtual communication skills, cultural awareness, sound judgment, and the ability to build trust with patients and caregivers quickly and while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries. The Patient Education Specialist must operate in a compliant, privacy-conscious manner and use only company-approved educational resources and call guidelines.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct proactive outbound calls and virtual outreach to eligible patients and caregivers to deliver disease education for PKU and other rare diseases using approved scripts, programs, and materials.
    • Explain complex disease-state, nutrition, treatment-navigation, and support information in clear, accessible language, tailored to different levels of health literacy.
    • Help patients and caregivers identify appropriate company-sponsored and community-based resources, while directing individualized medical or dietary questions to the treating healthcare professional.
    • Partner with metabolic clinics, healthcare professionals, patient advocacy organizations, and approved community partners to identify educational needs and generate awareness of available programs and eligible patients.
    • Coordinate virtual educational events and outreach campaigns in collaboration with Patient Services, Medical, Marketing, Compliance, Legal, and commercial colleagues, consistent with role boundaries.
    • Provide education that complements, rather than replaces, guidance from the patient’s healthcare team or dietitian.
    • Capture program activity, educational needs, and non-identifiable insights in approved systems to improve future patient education and resource planning.
    • Share recurring educational gaps and patient-resource needs with internal partners without documenting unnecessary personal health information.
    • Maintain current knowledge of PKU, relevant rare-disease care pathways, approved product labeling, patient resources, and applicable company policies.
    • Support onboarding, peer learning, best-practice sharing, and consistent call execution across regions.
    • Develop a regional outreach plan with clear call and engagement objectives, priority patient and caregiver segments, follow-up cadence, and measures of reach and quality.
    • Work effectively in developing inside sales model, adapting to evolving patient and business needs while remaining accountable for high-quality execution.

Performance Measures

Performance will be assessed through a balanced set of compliant, education-focused measures, which may include:
• Quality and consistency of patient and caregiver education delivery.
• Call activity, patient and caregiver reach, and completion of approved educational programs and virtual engagement activities.
• Timely and accurate documentation in approved systems.
• Identification and communication of relevant educational needs and resource gaps.
• Cross-functional collaboration, training completion, and adherence to company policies.
• Progress against regional education objectives and managed-by-objectives goals.

Scope and Working Conditions

  • Remote, home-based inside sales role supporting a multi-state geography and a diverse patient and caregiver population; no field travel expected.
    • Dedicated home office with reliable high-speed internet and a professional phone and video setup; comfort with CRM and virtual meeting tools.
    • Ability to work some evenings and weekends, as needed, to reach patients and caregivers and support approved virtual educational events.
    • Advanced phone and virtual engagement skills to conduct outbound calls to patients who may be eligible for different treatments, with ability to handle sensitive information with discretion and follow privacy, pharmacovigilance, adverse-event reporting, and product-complaint procedures.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree required.

  • 2-4 years of relevant experience in inside sales, patient outreach, patient education, dietetics, nutrition services, rare disease, patient advocacy, healthcare, or a related field.
    • Demonstrated ability to communicate complex health information in a clear, empathetic, and culturally responsive manner.
    • Experience conducting outbound calls and educational conversations with patients, caregivers, or community groups.
    • Strong organization, call and territory planning, presentation, and phone and virtual engagement skills.
    • Ability to work independently, collaborate across functions, and operate effectively in an evolving environment.
    • Commitment to ethical, compliant, and non-promotional patient engagement.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN), licensed dietitian, or formal dietetics or clinical nutrition background strongly preferred.
    • Experience in inside sales or a call-based outreach role, metabolic clinic, specialty pharmacy, patient-services organization, advocacy organization, or biopharmaceutical patient-education program.
    • Knowledge of medical nutrition therapy concepts and the practical challenges of long-term dietary management, while recognizing that individualized dietary advice remains with the treating clinical team.
    • Bilingual or multilingual capability is relevant to the assigned geography.

Compliance and Role Boundaries

The Patient Education Specialist provides general education using approved materials and does not diagnose, prescribe, recommend individualized treatment or dietary changes, or replace the patient’s healthcare professional. All interactions must comply with company policy and applicable privacy, promotional, pharmacovigilance, product-complaint, and healthcare compliance requirements.

Note: This description is not intended to be all-inclusive, or a limitation of the duties of the position. It is intended to describe the general nature of the job that may include other duties as assumed or assigned.

Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled

An Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability.

Consultancy Opportunity: Associate Manager, LAC (EN-8)
Duration: 12 months, anticipated from 4th January 2027 to 15 December 2027
Application deadline: 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on December 11, 2026

Location and availability: This is a remote consultancy. Applications are welcome from consultants based in any location, with applications particularly encouraged from Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, and Colombia. The Consultant must be able to coordinate across time zones.

ABOUT EQUALITY NOW:

At Equality Now, we aspire to create a world in which women and men have equal rights under the law and full enjoyment of their human rights. Our mission is gender equality. And how we get there matters. Here are the values behind everything we do.

Founded in 1992, we are an international human rights organization that works to protect and promote the rights of all women and girls around the world. Our campaigns are centred on four program areas: Legal Equality, End Sexual Violence, End Harmful Practices, and End Sexual Exploitation, with a cross-cutting focus on the unique needs of adolescent girls. We are truly global, and we have a team of 80+ people located all around the world. We have team members in Benin, Beirut, London, Geneva, San Jose, El Salvador, Argentina, Nairobi, Tbilisi, New York and Washington, DC among others. We offer a great experience for talented people who are passionate about equality. To work here, you’ll need to share our core values of integrity and accountability, inclusiveness, resilience, and empathy. For more information, visit

MISSION OBJECTIVE:

Equality Now seeks an independent consultant to play a central role in the design and delivery of communications activities that promote Equality Now’s work and impact across the region. The Consultant will ensure regionalised media engagement, content and event production and digital experiences, directed to key audiences to accelerate the campaigns and advocacy objectives for the region. The Consultant will also ensure the communication work aligns with, and is represented in, the global Equality Now communications strategy. The assignment will support Associate Managers in the Communications team, act as an ambassador for quality, process improvement and a culture of trust, care and excellence.

SCOPE OF WORK AND EXPECTED DELIVERABLES:
The Consultant will undertake the following activities and deliver the agreed outputs. This scope provides a general outline of the assignment and may be refined in consultation with the Associate Director, Advocacy Communications to reflect evolving organisational needs and priorities.

Purpose: Apply Foundational Knowledge

  • Apply their understanding of communication strategy and planning to the objectives of the LAC campaigns to design, (supported by the Associate Director, Advocacy Communications and in consultation with Program colleagues) to create an umbrella communications strategy for the region, with individual plans for campaigns where needed - that is also aligned to worldwide thematic communication strategies.
  • Within the strategy, create a loyalty-building infrastructure for LAC audiences, using Equality Now platforms such as the website, email function, social media, and events.
  • Maintain and expand a regional media contact list.
  • Work with the media team to place stories in national and regional media by coordinating pitches, preparing spokespersons, and tracking media coverage.
  • Create and maintain key messaging for the region - ensuring this is applied to digital and media content.
  • Collaborate with the global media team to align regional media activities with international strategies.
  • Create and schedule social media content focused on LAC-based initiatives and campaigns on the LAC regional channels.
  • Collaborate with the Digital and Production team to amplify regional messages on Equality Now’s global channels.
  • Monitor online engagement and adjust content based on trends and feedback.
  • Organise and deliver events that further advocacy objectives.

Engagement: Knowledge Building & Collaboration

  • Create and maintain a database of target audiences with the ability to advance legal reform, to influence thinking and accelerate work.
  • Work with partners, and the program and communications team to maintain and update a calendar of LAC-focused communications activities to inform planning and resource allocation, and identify opportunities to engage audiences - aligned to the strategy and in collaboration with other regional and thematic communications representatives.
  • Proactively identify and respond to partnership opportunities that accelerate advocacy and reputation goals
  • Track and monitor the efficacy of communications work through stated KPIs as a route to continuous improvement of future work.
  • Share findings and trends with the wider communications team and organisation.
  • Work with the Associate Director, Advocacy Communications to identify materials and content that can be used for the Equality Justice Academy.
  • Act as a liaison with communications staff in coalitions and campaigns, attending virtual meetings and contributing content.
  • Ensure regional voices are reflected in global communications planning and materials.

Delivery: Operational Awareness & Action

  • Support the Associate Director, Advocacy Communications in embedding a culture of excellence and accountability across all communications processes.
  • Work within and contribute to the continuous improvement of content and knowledge product production processes
  • Assist in identifying compelling case studies and visuals that highlight the experiences and voices of women, adolescent girls and girls in the region.
  • Ensure all content is culturally relevant, accurate, sensitive, and rights-based and act as an ambassador for the same within the wider Communications team.
  • Work with the program and development teams to articulate communications elements to grant proposals, ensuring that resources are aligned to activities and objectives, whilst ensuring budgetary oversight of communications activities in active campaigns.
  • Contribute to the development of impact tracking and impact narrative building.

CONSULTANT REQUIREMENTS & TARGET SKILLS PROFILE:

Substantive Knowledge

  • Strong understanding of the socio-political landscape across the LAC region and its relevance to gender equality, legal advocacy, and coalition-based work.
  • Familiarity with international human rights frameworks and institutions and advocacy cycles, as well as donor-funded project communications deliverables.
  • Awareness of the storytelling sensitivities and reputational risks associated with rights-based and survivor-centred communications.

Communication Skills

  • Fluent in Spanish and English
  • Adept at fostering cross-cultural collaboration and cultivating trust-based relationships consistent with the mission and values of Equality Now.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with high-quality writing and editing experience across formats, including digital, social media, press materials, and knowledge products.
  • Proven track record of pitching and placing stories with regional, national, and international media outlets.
  • Skilled in tailoring messaging to diverse audiences such as policymakers, donors, journalists, grassroots partners, and the general public in the LAC context.
  • Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills to engage internal teams, partners, external coalitions, and media contacts.
  • Comfortable representing the organisation in external coalitions, media interactions, and advocacy forums.

Execution Skills

  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage large-scale communications strategies and campaigns with measurable impact.
  • Strong project management and stakeholder management skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, collaborate across cross-functional teams, and deliver high-quality outputs on deadline.
  • Creative and proactive problem-solver who responds rapidly to media opportunities, integrates strategic and reactive communications, and seeks feedback to improve outputs.
  • Competency in multi-channel content planning and working across platforms (e.g., Twitter, Instagram, Facebook).
  • Experience managing media outreach, content production workflows, and donor reporting requirements.
  • Builds and maintains relationships with national partners, regional coalitions, media contacts, and other external stakeholders to amplify organisational messaging and advocacy impact.
  • Willingness to supervise, train and mentor others.
  • Willingness and ability to travel internationally and domestically, sometimes on short notice, to support regional teams, engage with partners, and represent Equality Now.

Targeted Specialised Knowledge

  • Bachelor’s degree required, preferably in International Affairs and Communications; Master’s degree or equivalent certification preferred.
  • 5+ years of communications experience in national or international contexts, preferably in human rights, advocacy, or non-profit sectors.
  • Working knowledge of digital tools, including CMS, social media scheduling platforms, media monitoring systems (e.g., Meltwater), Google Suite, and digital design/production processes (in collaboration with production teams).
  • Understanding of off- and online advocacy tactics, influencer engagement, and content adaptation using insights and analytics.
  • Familiarity with donor reporting and impact measurement in communications.

CONSULTANCY FEE AND TERMS:

The advertised amount of $31,439 - $40,926 USD represents the available budget for the full assignment, based on an estimated 220 working days. The final fee may be lower than this amount, depending on the consultant’s location, relevant local market rates, experience and expertise, and the agreed scope and level of effort. Equality Now and the selected consultant will agree to the fee before signing the consultancy agreement.

The Consultant is responsible for ensuring they are legally authorised to provide the services from their jurisdiction and for maintaining any required registrations, licences, or permits. The Consultant is also responsible for applicable tax filings, payments, and statutory contributions arising from the consultancy. Equality Now will meet any withholding or reporting obligations required by applicable law. Any extension is subject to available funding and mutual written agreement. Renewal is not guaranteed.

HOW TO APPLY:

Consultants must submit a resume or CV and a cover letter. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and the vacancy will close once a suitable candidate is appointed. The application period will close at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on December 11, 2026. Due to the anticipated volume of applications, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an interview.

Equality Now is strong because it is diverse. We actively seek a diverse applicant pool and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. Equality Now is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employees are selected based on their qualifications and ability, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, language, political or other opinion, nationality, ethnic or social origin, disability, pregnancy, mental status, HIV status, age, marital status, sexual orientation, or any other status protected by applicable law. We welcome and value all forms of diversity.
