jobs.title: Sr. Project/Program Manager II
jobs.excerpt: Who we are Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

We are looking for a Senior Project/Program Manager II to be a hands-on partner to our accounting, tax, and O2C leaders. You are an AI wizard, up to date on the newest technology, and ready to support teams through the self supported transition to automated workflows. You will turn business ideas into well-defined, well-tested system and process improvements, serving as the translator between finance and technical teams from first intake through go-live and hypercare. Over time, you will own a portfolio of projects aligned to these teams, while staying flexible across all three areas because they are closely connected.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except Alaska, Austin Metro, Boulder Metro, California, Chicago Metro, Connecticut, Dallas Metro, Denver Metro, Houston Metro, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Rhode Island, Seattle Metro, and Washington, D.C. Relocation assistance will not be provided for this role.

You should apply if:

  • You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
  • You like solving puzzles: You enjoy untangling a messy process or system problem, determining root cause and impact, and landing on a solution that works.
  • You enjoy making other people’s jobs easier: You get energized by partnering with business stakeholders to make their work more efficient, and you measure success by the problems you take off their plate.
  • You like hands-on work across teams: You would rather be in the details with people from finance, accounting, tax, and IT than managing from a distance, and you build trust by being a reliable partner to each of them.
  • You are a self-starter who works well remotely: You think critically, take ownership of your projects, and keep work moving day to day from your own workspace, with a collaborative team and leaders you can lean on when you need them.
  • You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. Youwill be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.

In this role, you will:

  • Partner with business stakeholders across accounting to intake and discuss their challenges and project ideas, assess scope and initial level of effort, identify the right technical resources, and help leaders prioritize work using our project intake framework, including sizing the business backlog (for example, with t-shirt sizes) so you can talk with IT about capacity. Turn those ideas into clear business requirements documents (BRDs) and detailed requirements that state the problem to solve, not the solution design, with defined in-scope and out-of-scope items, and maintain project artifacts such as timelines and RAID logs.
  • Put AI to work, and know it well. You understand how models work under the hood (neural networks, training and backpropagation, tokens and context windows), the difference between a model and the agents and applications built on it, and the difference between LLMs and agentic AI. You consult with business stakeholders on AI solutions that don't need IT to build or support: you know skills, workflows, and MCPs, can spot where AI is the right tool for a problem and where it isn't, and know its limits (hallucinations, security, data privacy). You use it to speed up drafting of requirements, test scenarios, and project reporting, keep a human in the loop, and check every output.
  • Act as the key contact between business stakeholders and IT teams (such as FinSys, GTMS, and Integrations) through design and development. Translate between finance and technical language, and between IT teams (such as Salesforce, NetSuite, and integrations) to help pinpoint root causes, document key design decisions and trade-offs, and use good judgment on which decisions you can guide and which to bring back to stakeholders for confirmation.
  • Coordinate user acceptance testing (UAT) end to end: draft unit test scenarios and UAT and end-to-end test cases with stakeholder input, maintain the requirements traceability matrix (RTM), manage timelines and tester availability across concurrent projects, triage defects hands-on with business and technical teams (digging into the fields, logic, and formulas to understand how the system should work and why) through resolution and retesting, and provide UAT summaries against entry and exit criteria.
  • Lead go-live readiness and support hypercare, including go/no-go decisions and sign-offs, steering committee updates, and joint business and IT status reporting, escalating risks early.
  • Connect business stakeholders with our enablement teams on SOPs and training materials, and clearly explain what is changing so enablement can work with the business audience to update guides, SOPs, and training to match what is being deployed.
  • Grow into owning a portfolio of projects while remaining flexible across corporate accounting, tax, and O2C, offering guidance to teammates as the team grows.
  • Work with IT in their language: understand agile concepts such as epics, stories, bugs, story points, and sprints, and protect IT's capacity by offering MVPs and phases when a request that looks simple to the business is complex underneath.
  • Build SOX controls into projects: determine which systems are in or out of scope for IT general controls (ITGCs), plan control design and evidence, run user access reviews with IT, and understand how SOC 1 and SOC 2 reports apply to finance systems.
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 5+ years of project or program management experience, including leading cross-functional projects
  • 2+ years of financial accounting experience
  • Strong understanding of financial accounting (including general ledger accounting, ASC 606 revenue recognition, and accounting for taxes such as sales and use tax) and project management principles
  • Understanding of SOX controls, including key reports, monthly versus quarterly controls, control evidence, and IT general controls (ITGCs), including which systems are in or out of scope
  • Understanding of the accounting close (monthly, quarterly, and annual) and of financial reporting, such as 10-Ks and 10-Qs
  • Experience managing projects through the full lifecycle, from requirements and design through testing and go-live
  • Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to present facts clearly to influence outcomes
  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
  • Must reside in a US location eligible for this remote role (see location statement above)

An ideal candidate also has:

  • PMP (preferred) or CAPM certification, or a CPA license (active, or inactive and in good standing)
  • Experience with NetSuite, or another ERP such as SAP or Oracle
  • Familiarity with Salesforce, Vertex, and Databricks
  • Experience in revenue accounting, order-to-cash, accounting for tax (such as sales and use tax and how it differs by country), or international accounting
  • Experience writing BRDs, test cases, and UAT plans for finance or accounting systems
  • Working knowledge of agile project management, including epics, stories, bugs, story points, and sprints
  • Experience working with control owners, auditors, and IT on system changes, including ITGC scoping, user access reviews, and familiarity with SOC 1 and SOC 2 reports
  • Experience with Google Workspace and Slack
  • Experience using AI tools to improve efficiency while validating the results

The compensation range shown spans approved pay zones for this role. Your primary work location determines the range applicable to you, which may be narrower than the full range displayed.

The range of annual base salary for full-time employees for this position is below. Please note that base pay offered may vary depending on factors including your city of residence, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. This role is also eligible for an initial RSU grant with no vesting cliff, and ongoing refresh opportunities tied to performance, subject to plan terms and conditions. Learn more about our total rewards and benefits below.

Annual Base Salary
$115,727—$155,600 USD

Total Rewards

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you’re ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual’s ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable.

Belonging at Samsara

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email or click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity

We use Tofu, a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

Fraudulent Employment Offers

Samsara is aware of scams involving fake job interviews and offers. Please know we do not charge fees to applicants at any stage of the hiring process. Official communication about your application will only come from emails ending in @samsara.com, @us-greenhouse-mail.io or @mail3.guide.co. For more information regarding fraudulent employment offers, please visit our blog post here.

jobs.title: Deputy General Counsel
jobs.excerpt: Role Overview CAA is seeking a Deputy General Counsel to serve as the organization’s senior legal leader for enterprise contract management, National Board committee management, and corporate governance.
jobs.description:
Role Overview

CAA is seeking a Deputy General Counsel to serve as the organization’s senior legal leader for enterprise contract management, National Board committee management, and corporate governance. Reporting to the General Counsel & Secretary, the Deputy General Counsel is accountable for building and operating scalable contracting and governance frameworks that support CAA’s mission and multi-state growth, as well as assist on significant litigation, regulatory challenges, and disputes.

  • Act on the General Counsel's behalf, as delegated.
  • Own enterprise contract strategy, negotiation standards, lifecycle management, and contract governance.
  • Manage National Board committee operations in partnership with the General Counsel & Secretary, including meeting planning, materials, resolutions, minutes, and follow-up.
  • Advise executive leadership on corporate governance, entity management, and delegated-authority matters.
  • Lead and develop team members and external resources assigned to contracts and national governance.

This role is intentionally focused on leading enterprise contracting, National Board committee management, and corporate governance. State-specific regulatory interpretation, state board support, and operational compliance programs are outside the role’s primary ownership except when needed to address a material contract, corporate governance issue or litigation risks.

Key Responsibilities

Role Scope & Organizational Distinction

  • Act as the General Counsel’s principal deputy for National Board and corporate governance matters, including assuming those responsibilities in the General Counsel’s absence.
  • Act as the organization’s senior legal leader for enterprise contracting.
  • Set the strategy, annual priorities, budget, service model, and operating standards for the contracting and national governance functions.
  • Serve as the primary internal escalation point for material contract risk, governance questions, and National Board committee matters.
  • Establish or build upon existing decision rights, delegated-authority rules, approval matrices, and escalation thresholds for contracts and corporate governance actions.
  • Counsel personnel at all levels within the organization on enterprise transactions, governance decisions, and significant disputes, as well as coordinate with other Legal leaders on state regulatory, employment, intellectual property, information governance, or general litigation portfolios.
  • Select, direct, and manage outside counsel engaged on matters within areas of responsibility.
  • Lead, develop, and manage personnel – including those assigned to enterprise contracting - including workload, performance, succession, and capability development.
  • Measure and continuously improve the effectiveness, timeliness, controls, and stakeholder experience of the contracting and governance functions.

Corporate Governance & Entity Oversight

  • Enhance and maintain the enterprise corporate governance framework, including governing documents, committee charters, delegated authorities, conflicts processes, approval structures, and governance calendars.
  • Lead periodic governance reviews and recommend updates to bylaws, charters, resolutions, delegations, and governance practices as the organization evolves.
  • Ensure National Board committee records accurately reflect decisions, delegated authority, recusals, approvals, and required follow-up, in coordination with the General Counsel & Secretary.

Enterprise Contract Management

  • Lead and scale a centralized, high-volume contracting function with defined service levels, intake paths, approval requirements, and escalation protocols.
  • Own the development and continuous improvement of contract templates, clause libraries, fallback positions, negotiation playbooks, and approval matrices.
  • Own the contract lifecycle management (CLM) platform and operating model, including intake, workflows, approvals, signatures, obligations, metadata, retention, and reporting.
  • Establish and report contract performance and risk metrics, including volume, cycle time, aging, deviations, obligations, and recurring risk trends.
  • Lead strategy and negotiation for complex, high-risk, or enterprise-significant agreements involving programs, producers, service providers, and other interest holders.
  • Own contract governance after signature, including obligation tracking, renewal and termination controls, recordkeeping, audit readiness, and accountable business-owner follow-through.

Contract Escalation & Dispute Prevention

  • Manage escalated contract claims, performance disputes, cure plans, renegotiations, and termination decisions, engaging subject-matter or disputes counsel when specialized support is required.
  • Build dispute-prevention mechanisms into templates, negotiation playbooks, governance controls, and post-signature obligation management.

Litigation & Dispute Strategy

  • Partner with the General Counsel on strategy for significant litigation, regulatory challenges, and enterprise disputes.
  • Direct or co-manage outside litigation counsel, including selection, scoping, budgets, and case-management cadence.
  • Prepare litigation briefings for executives and Board leaders on posture, exposure, and decision points.
  • Oversee and/or coordinate litigation holds, privilege, and document preservation with the Legal team and business owners.

Standards, Training & Continuous Improvement

  • Develop and maintain policies, procedures, and controls around enterprise contracting, National Board operations, corporate governance, and litigation and dispute-management protocols.
  • Provide role-based training and guidance to enhance organizational compliance in connection with areas of responsibility.
  • Other job-related duties as assigned.

Skills & Competencies

  • Experience leading the full lifecycle of complex commercial transactions and enterprise contract portfolios.
  • Strong commercial judgment and disciplined contract and governance risk assessment.
  • Experience managing outside counsel and budgets.
  • Ability to balance contractual and governance risk with organizational objectives and decision timelines.
  • Experience managing high-volume contract workflows, service levels, approval paths, and escalation queues.
  • Hands-on experience with CLM tools and contract process optimization.
  • Mission-Driven and passionate about sustainability.
  • Highly detail-oriented, with precision in drafting and issue spotting across complex agreements and governance documents.
  • Excellent communicator with proven ability to translate complex concepts for executives and other personnel.
  • Proactive and collaborative, with the presence and judgment to work effectively with executives, Board and committee leaders, contract owners, and external counterparties.
  • Comfort working in a lean, entrepreneurial, and mission-driven organization.
  • Ability to develop and mentor professionals.
  • Leadership skills and ability to set strategic direction for enterprise contracting and national corporate governance.
  • Ability to build trusted relationships and influence Board leaders, executives, contract owners, and external counterparties.

Qualifications

  • Juris Doctor (J.D.) from an accredited U.S. law school.
  • Active bar membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state.
  • 15+ years of legal experience, with progressive responsibility for enterprise contracting and corporate governance in a law firm, in-house, or comparable organizational setting.
  • Demonstrated readiness to lead a broader legal function, including the breadth of judgment expected of a general counsel.
  • Advanced contract drafting, negotiation, corporate governance analysis, and Board advisory skills.
  • Experience supervising or substantially supporting complex litigation or significant disputes, including managing outside counsel.
  • Demonstrated experience negotiating complex commercial agreements and developing scalable templates, playbooks, approval matrices, and contract controls.
  • Experience with CLM systems is strongly preferred (ideally, Ironclad).
  • Significant experience supporting a national or enterprise Board and committees, including bylaws, charters, resolutions, and minutes
  • Experience leading and developing lawyers and legal professionals, including hiring, performance management, and supervision.

Compensation & Other Information

  • Location: Remote; Occasional travel to meetings as needs; future work location may be determined.
  • Pay Rate: Based on a variety of factors in accordance with applicable law including the successful candidate’s relevant experience, skills, and knowledge.
  • Reports To: General Counsel & Secretary

jobs.description:
At Cloudary, we are hiring a Senior UI Developer for an international client: a SaaS startup preparing the launch of the next version of its platform.
This is a hands-on, high-ownership contract role. You will be the only UI developer on the team, owning the CSS architecture, the design system and the accessibility of an Angular application built with the NG-ZORRO component library and SCSS. You will work closely with the Project Manager, Angular developers, QA, external designers and business stakeholders.
The ideal candidate sits between design and development: an expert in CSS and design systems who can also create wireframes in Figma when no designer is available.

Requirements

Job requirements
Key Responsibilities

  • Build, evolve and document a scalable design system and a reusable component library for an existing Angular platform.

  • Customize and theme NG-ZORRO components through a centralized, well-documented styling layer that stays maintainable as the library evolves.

  • Ensure the application meets WCAG 2.2 Level AA, including semantic HTML, ARIA, keyboard navigation, focus management and color contrast.

  • Identify accessibility gaps in NG-ZORRO components and fix them through theming, custom wrappers or targeted overrides.

  • Validate accessibility using automated tools and screen readers, and implement the fixes.

  • Translate business requirements into wireframes and layout concepts, applying UI/UX best practices across desktop and mobile.

  • Review, test, approve and merge SCSS/CSS/HTML changes in a Git-based workflow (AWS CodeCommit).

  • Fix QA-reported bugs quickly, and test across browsers, devices and screen sizes.

  • Provide realistic estimates, flag risks early and communicate progress clearly through tickets.

  • Establish front-end styling standards and leave clear documentation and handover notes for the team.


What You Bring

  • 7+ years of front-end UI development experience, including building and maintaining styling systems for large SaaS applications.

  • Expert-level SCSS, CSS and semantic HTML (CSS Grid, Flexbox, custom properties, BEM or ITCSS).

  • Hands-on experience with NG-ZORRO (Ant Design for Angular), including theming and upgrade-safe style overrides. Working knowledge of LESS.

  • Working knowledge of Angular (component templates, view encapsulation, SCSS integration), Node.js and npm.

  • Applied accessibility experience: WCAG 2.2 AA, WAI-ARIA, keyboard accessibility and screen-reader testing.

  • Experience building information-rich interfaces (search, reading, lists, knowledge bases) with strong visual hierarchy and responsive layouts.

  • Strong Figma skills: wireframing, reusable components, variants and shared styles.

  • Experience with Git, code reviews and collaborative workflows (AWS CodeCommit is a plus).

  • Self-directed and able to become productive quickly with minimal onboarding.

  • Fluent English, written and spoken.


Nice to Have

  • Storybook, Stylelint or visual regression testing.

  • JavaScript/TypeScript beyond Angular templates.

  • An accessibility certification (IAAP CPACC or WAS).

  • Experience with research, news or knowledge-management tools.

  • Experience working with external design agencies.

  • Illustrator, Photoshop or Lucidchart for production-ready visual assets.


Hiring Details

  • Location: 100% Remote

  • Employment Type: Contractor, fixed hourly rate (USD).

  • Engagement: Short-term, up to 4 weeks.

  • Working Hours: Availability to work Pacific Time (PST) hours.

  • Start Date: ASAP

  • Languages: Fluent English required.

  • Application: Please include a portfolio or links to CSS / design system work.

Highlights

NG-ZORRO, WCAG 2.2 AA, WAI-ARIA, SCSS, CSS, Semantic HTML, SaaS applications, Git,

About CircleCI

CircleCI is the world’s largest continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) platform, and the hub where code moves from idea to delivery. As one of the most-used DevOps tools - processing more than 3 million jobs a day - CircleCI has unique access to data on how the most effective engineering teams work, and the tools to help software companies successfully leverage the power of AI into their commercial applications. Companies like Hinge, HuggingFace, and Samsung use us to improve engineering team productivity, release better products, and get to market faster.

Ventures, Scale Venture Partners, Owl Rock Capital, Next Equity Partners, Heavybit, and Harrison Metal Capital.

How CircleCI Uses AI in Hiring

At CircleCI, people make our hiring decisions. We use technology to support our recruiting team so they can spend more time on what matters most: getting to know you.

Where we may use AI

  • Job descriptions and messaging: AI may help draft job descriptions and role-specific messaging so they are clear and accurate.
  • Application review: For some roles, we use an AI tool to review applications, including resumes and application responses, against criteria our hiring team sets for the role. The tool generates a fit score and summary to help recruiters organize and prioritize applications.

AI does not make hiring decisions at CircleCI. Our recruiters and hiring teams review candidates and make every decision to advance or reject an application. About Argyle

Argyle is a fast-growing, remote-first, Series C startup solving a consumer data problem.

For decades, financial service providers and other businesses have collected and verified consumer income, employment, and asset data the same way: by hand or via verification databases. These methods are expensive, time consuming, high friction, and/or unreliable. In turn, experiences like applying for a loan or completing a background check are challenging for service providers and consumers alike.

The solution is Argyle. We’re the leading provider of direct-source, consumer-permissioned income, employment, and asset verifications. We make it fast and easy to gain secure and reliable access to the most complete real-time datasets stored in consumers’ payroll and banking accounts, so service providers can automate verification workflows, save time, reduce risks, lower costs, and build better product experiences.

Named one of America’s Best Startup Employers of 2026 by Forbes, Argyle largely serves the mortgage, government benefits, tenant screening, lending, and background check industries as well as the gig economy.

Founded in 2018, Argyle’s commitment to innovation is backed by investors including Bain Capital Ventures, Checkr, Mastercard, Rockefeller Asset Management and SignalFire.

About the team

Revenue Operations runs the critical business operations that keep Argyle’s sales motion moving fast, from deal approvals and contracting to billing, commissions, and the CRM. We’re a small team of experienced operators, and we lean heavily on automation and AI tools to do more with less.

This is a hands-on role for someone early in their career who wants to learn from an experienced RevOps team and own real processes within a few months. You’ll work daily with account executives, customer success managers, marketing, and finance.

What You’ll Do
  • Be the first stop for RevOps requests. Own the request queue for Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success. Handle the routine work yourself, from contract amendments and exports to pricing reviews, SKU setup, and Salesforce cleanup. On every request, engage stakeholders and pressure-test their asks until you land on a solution or a clear escalation path.
  • Own monthly billing preparation. Run most of the pre-invoice process each month, from custom billing processes, credits tracking, and discrepancies review to finalizing amounts each customer owes.
  • Build controls that scale. Run recurring checks that signed contracts, billing setup, and platform access line up, and turn repeat requests into documented processes or automation, including AI-assisted workflows.
  • Handle routine deal desk approvals. Review opportunities in Salesforce for completeness, pricing setup, and contract dates before approval, and resolve setup issues that slow deals down.
  • Manage the customer account lifecycle. Handle activations, terminations, reinstatements, and access changes, and keep Salesforce and our billing platform in sync.
  • Keep CRM data clean. Maintain accounts, contacts, ownership, and pipeline hygiene. Monitor the health of the HubSpot–Salesforce sync to ensure a smooth handoff from Marketing to Sales.
  • Support partner and government reporting. Help prepare monthly and quarterly revenue share reports for channel and integration partners, plus recurring reporting on our government contracts.
  • Co-own sales commissions. Learn our monthly commission process hands-on, then share ownership of running it each month, from calculating payouts to keeping the process accurate and on time.

jobs.description:
The Director of Engineering leads the engineering organization across all STARLIMS products and transform it into an AI-first team. You set the technical vision, unify architecture and practices across all product stacks, and make AI-assisted development the default way software is designed, built, tested and released. You deliver secure, scalable, compliant solutions for regulated laboratory and life-science customers, working closely with Product, Quality, Regulatory, Operations and the executive team.

Key responsibilities:

This role has authority over engineering strategy, SDLC practice and team structure for multiple product lines. This role is expected to partner with architecture team members as we modernize our platforms. Responsibilities may change with business needs.

Organizational transformation

  • Lead the transformation of the engineering organization: assess current structure, skills and ways of working, then design and execute a phased plan to the target operating model.
  • Work with architecture team members to bring the teams for all STARLIMS products together under shared standards, tooling, architecture principles and engineering culture while respecting each product's customers and release commitments.
  • Hire, develop and, where needed, transition engineering managers and technical leads; build the new roles, career paths and skills that an AI-first organization needs.
  • Manage change deliberately: communicate the why, set clear milestones, measure adoption and keep delivery steady throughout.
  • Foster a high-performing, inclusive, collaborative culture across time zones.

AI-first engineering and AI SDLC

  • Define and own the AI-first engineering strategy and roadmap and make AI a default part of how engineers work rather than an optional tool.
  • Redesign the software development lifecycle around AI: AI-assisted requirements and design, code generation and review, test generation, documentation, release and support, with human review at the right gates.
  • Select, roll out and govern AI developer tools (for example coding assistants and agents), and set standards for prompting, review, provenance and acceptable use.
  • Embed validation, traceability, audit trails and security into AI-assisted workflows so they meet FDA, GxP, 21 CFR Part 11, ISO and data privacy expectations.
  • Define and report metrics for AI impact, such as cycle time, deployment frequency, defect escape rate, test coverage, developer adoption and cost per release.
  • Train and coach teams in AI-assisted practice and identify opportunities to embed AI features in all STARLIMS products.

Technical leadership and architecture

  • Partner with Architecture so teams follow agreed architecture and technology decisions, and raise conflicts with product delivery.
  • Support modernization of legacy components by prioritizing and resourcing Architecture initiatives.
  • Own engineering tooling investment decisions, with input from Architecture and the platform team.
  • Guide engineering teams in code quality, automated testing, CI/CD, observability and release management practices, collaborating with the platform and architecture teams

Delivery and cross-functional partnership

  • Partner with Product Management to turn roadmap priorities into execution plans, balancing new features, technical debt and platform stability.
  • Represent engineering with Quality, Product, Operations and customer-facing teams, and in executive discussions.
  • Manage engineering budgets, resourcing and staffing plans, including vendors and AI tooling spend.
  • Report engineering metrics (cycle time, predictability, quality, uptime and reliability) to senior leadership.
  • Drive continuous improvement in processes, tooling and team capability.
  • Perform other duties, as assigned.

Qualifications:

Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology or a related technical field required. Master's degree preferred, or equivalent training and experience.

Experience:

  • 10+ years in software development, with at least 3 years managing engineering managers or team leads.
  • Proven record of leading an engineering organization through a major transformation, such as restructuring teams, changing operating model, consolidating product lines or modernizing practices, with measurable results.
  • Hands-on experience driving AI-first engineering: adopting AI coding assistants or agents at scale, redesigning the SDLC around them, and measuring the impact on throughput and quality.
  • Strong architecture and design experience in multi-tier, distributed enterprise environments, with significant experience in the Microsoft ecosystem.
  • Proven experience leading and mentoring high-performing, globally distributed teams.
  • Experience with Agile methods (Scrum, Kanban), DevOps and CI/CD.
  • Experience with LLMs, LLM hosting both on-prem and in the cloud.
  • Experience with AWS Bedrock, Anthropic and OpenAI APIs.
  • Experience with coding assistants and agents, such as Claude Code.
  • Solid grounding in object-oriented programming, databases, security and networking.
  • Understanding of regulations and standards such as FDA, GxP, 21 CFR Part 11, ISO and data privacy law (for example HIPAA, GDPR).
  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management and problem-solving skills, including translating technical detail into business language and back.
  • Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.

Technology expertise:

  • Required: C#, .NET, ASP.NET Core and JavaScript.
  • Required: Blazor (web UI) and WPF (desktop UI), or equivalent depth in modern .NET UI frameworks.
  • Familiarity with AI development tooling and LLM-based agents, and with validating AI-assisted software in a regulated setting.

Preferred:

Success measures:

jobs.title: Senior Data Engineer
jobs.excerpt: About Us There are 55 million Americans over 65 living at home, and their families are anxious in ways that go far beyond "I hope mom's alright.
jobs.description:
About Us

There are 55 million Americans over 65 living at home, and their families are anxious in ways that go far beyond "I hope mom's alright." We built a phone that works out of the box, AI check-in calls that surface how she's really doing, and a family app that replaces daily dread with peace of mind. Families tell us they used to wake up with a knot in their stomach. They don't anymore.

It is working, with tens of thousands of active customers, a strong financial position, and investors including the YC Continuity Fund behind us.

We are looking for a hands-on owner of finance and operations: a do-er who makes finance a real partner to every leader in the company and runs the operations that keep it moving. You will put the numbers at the center of how we make decisions including telling us when we should be investing more, not just less. This is not a role for someone who wants to hire a team and manage from above. You will build the model, sit in the budget reviews and negotiate the contracts yourself. If building the financial and operational backbone of the company that brings peace of mind to millions of seniors and their families is how you want to spend the next few years, we'd love to talk.

What you will own

  • Own and evolve our data foundation. Today, our data stack and analytics infrastructure are maintained by backend engineers who have taken on data work alongside their primary responsibilities. You will become the first person dedicated to this area: owning the reliability, structure, and evolution of the systems that bring together data from our product, billing, CRM, marketing, and other platforms.
  • Turn raw data into a trustworthy, usable data layer. Build and maintain pipelines, models, views, and shared definitions that make important business concepts easy to understand and analyze. Reduce duplicated logic across dashboards and queries, establish clear definitions for core metrics, and make it easier for others to answer questions without rebuilding the same logic every time.
  • Enable self-service analytics across the company. Make it possible for non-data specialists to answer recurring questions through dashboards, well-designed data abstractions, documentation, and AI-assisted tools.
  • Own recurring reporting and business visibility. Maintain and improve the dashboards and reporting used to understand growth, revenue, retention, churn, customer behavior, product adoption, and operational performance.
  • Investigate questions, not just fulfill data requests. When someone asks why churn increased, which customers adopt a feature, where a funnel is breaking, why a marketing channel is performing differently, or whether an experiment worked, you should be able to take an ambiguous question, find the relevant data, explore it, and come back with a clear answer---or explain what the data can and cannot tell us.
  • Partner closely with product, engineering, growth, marketing, and leadership. Data here is not a separate reporting function. You will work directly with people making product and business decisions, helping them define what should be measured, challenge assumptions, design useful analyses, and interpret results.
  • Build the foundations of our data function. You will have significant influence over how we structure analytics as the company grows: what belongs in the data layer, how metrics are defined and documented, how we monitor data quality, what should be automated, and eventually where additional data specialization or headcount would create leverage.

What we are looking for

  • Strong SQL and relational data skills. You should be extremely comfortable exploring complex production datasets, joining information across systems, understanding imperfect schemas, and turning messy business logic into clear, maintainable queries and models.
  • Production data engineering depth. You understand data pipelines, ETL/ELT, APIs, databases, data modeling, scheduling, monitoring, and failure modes. You do not need a backend engineer to diagnose every pipeline issue or build every new integration for you.
  • Cloud warehouse experience. Hands-on experience with BigQuery or a comparable analytical warehouse, including performance, cost, and maintainability tradeoffs.
  • Strong analytical judgment. You understand funnels, cohorts, retention, conversion, segmentation, experimentation, and the difference between an interesting correlation and something we should actually make a decision around. You know when a dataset is too small or biased to support the conclusion someone wants to draw.
  • Business curiosity. You want to understand why a metric changed, not just calculate it. You ask follow-up questions, inspect unexpected results, notice when two numbers that should reconcile do not, and keep digging until you understand what is happening.
  • The ability to communicate analysis clearly. You can turn a complicated investigation into a concise explanation of what happened, why we think it happened, how confident we are, and what we should look at next. Your audience will often include people who do not want or need to understand the SQL behind it.
  • Pragmatism about data infrastructure. We are not looking to build a sophisticated data platform for its own sake. You should know when a simple solution is enough, when something needs a more durable approach, and how to improve the architecture incrementally as our needs grow.
  • Comfort operating independently. There will not be a larger data team handing you tickets, reviewing every analysis, or deciding what to work on. You will need to prioritize against company goals, clarify ambiguous requests, and identify important data problems before someone explicitly asks you to solve them.

You are probably a fit if

  • You have 4+ years of experience in data engineering, analytics engineering, product analytics, or a similarly hands-on data role.
  • SQL is one of your strongest tools and you are comfortable working directly with PostgreSQL or similar relational databases.
  • You have worked with BigQuery or a similar warehouse.
  • You have built or maintained production data pipelines and worked with data coming from multiple operational systems.
  • You have experience building dashboards and recurring business reporting, but you do not think of dashboards as the end product of analytics.
  • You can independently investigate product or business questions and communicate the conclusions to non-data stakeholders.
  • You have worked closely with marketing, growth, sales, or revenue teams and understand the kinds of questions they need data to answer. Experience with CRM, marketing automation, attribution, or revenue operations is a strong plus.
  • You care deeply about data correctness and notice when definitions, edge cases, or assumptions do not quite line up.
  • You are comfortable inheriting an imperfect but functioning data environment and improving it incrementally rather than rebuilding everything from scratch.
  • You enjoy being both an engineer and an analyst and do not see infrastructure work and analytical work as separate worlds.
  • You are comfortable with ambiguity and biased toward finding answers.

What does your journey look like?

First 30 days: Learn the business and the data

Your first job is to understand how the company works through its data.

You will learn our core systems, data sources, schemas, dashboards, and recurring reports. You will work through how we currently measure revenue, churn, retention, acquisition, product adoption, and growth, and understand where those definitions come from.

At the same time, you will start taking ownership of existing analytics and data work. Fix a broken report. Investigate a real business question. Trace a metric back to its source. Identify places where duplicated or fragile logic is creating risk.

By the end of the first month, you should understand both the shape of our data environment and the major areas where improving it would create leverage.

Days 31 to 60: Take ownership

You are now the primary owner of our day-to-day data and analytics work.

Recurring reporting and pipelines are reliable and understood. Important metrics have clear definitions. When something looks wrong, you know where to start investigating it.

You are independently handling analytical questions from product, growth, engineering, and leadership, and you are beginning to replace one-off or duplicated analysis with reusable data models and shared logic.

You have also developed a point of view on the highest-leverage improvements to our data foundation. Not a theoretical architecture roadmap, but a prioritized list grounded in the problems you have actually encountered.

Days 61 to 90: Build leverage

By month three, the goal is not simply for you to be doing the data work that engineers were doing before. The goal is for the company to be better at using data because you are here.

Common questions are easier to answer. Core metrics are trustworthy and documented. Repeated manual work is becoming automated. Engineers spend less time maintaining analytics infrastructure and answering ad hoc data questions. Marketing and growth have better visibility into acquisition, conversion, and customer behavior. Product and business teams can make decisions with better information and less friction.

Our CRM, billing, marketing, and product data are becoming easier to reason about as a connected customer and revenue lifecycle, even without a dedicated RevOps function.

You have a clear roadmap for what comes next: where our data architecture needs to mature, what analytical capabilities we are missing, and which investments will create the most leverage as the company grows.

The team and structure

You will be our first dedicated data hire and work closely with engineering, product, marketing, growth, and company leadership.

You will inherit a functioning data environment built largely by backend engineers with strong interest and experience in data and analytics. That means you are not starting from zero: there are existing pipelines, dashboards, reporting, and significant institutional knowledge to build from. But data has historically been one responsibility among many rather than anyone's primary focus.

Your role is to change that.

You will have significant autonomy over how the data function evolves, while working closely with engineers who know the systems and business logic deeply. This is a hands-on role: particularly early on, you will move regularly between data engineering, analytics engineering, and analysis depending on where the highest-value problem is.

Why now

As the company has grown, data has become essential to understanding who our customers are, how they find us, whether they adopt our products, where they struggle, why they leave, how our revenue changes, and whether the things we build actually improve those outcomes.

Until now, engineers have owned much of this work alongside their other responsibilities. That has taken us surprisingly far, but it also means valuable engineering capacity is spent maintaining pipelines, building reports, and answering analytical questions, and there is no single person whose primary responsibility is making our data more reliable, accessible, and useful. We are ready for that to be someone's job.

If you like moving between engineering and analysis, digging into messy questions until they make sense, and building the foundations of a data function rather than inheriting a large established team, this is the role.

Interested in joining our Coding team? We have great opportunities, whether you’re looking for entry-level or have been coding for years! Requirements for each position noted below. Not the right fit for you? Keep looking! We have a lot different teams with different focuses (Facility vs Profee).

Within Banner Health Corporate, you will have the opportunity to apply your unique experience and expertise in support of a nationally-recognized healthcare leader. We offer stimulating and rewarding careers in a wide array of disciplines. Whether your background is in Human Resources, Finance, Information Technology, Legal, Managed Care Programs or Public Relations, you'll find many options for contributing to our award-winning patient care.

POSITION SUMMARY

This position is responsible for the interpretation of clinical documentation completed by the health care team for the health record(s) and for quality assurance in the alignment of clinical documentation and billing codes. Works with clinical documentation improvement and quality management staff to: align diagnosis coding to documentation to improve the quality of clinical documentation and correctness of billing codes prior to claim submission; to identify possible opportunities for improvement of clinical documentation and accurate MS-DRG, Ambulatory Payment Classification (APC) or ICD-10 assignments on health records. Provides guidance and expertise in the interpretation of, and adherence to, the rules and regulations for code assignment based on documentation for all levels of complexity to include accounts encountered in Banner’s Academic, Trauma, high acuity and critical access facilities, as well as specialized services such as behavioral health, oncology, pediatric. Acts as subject matter expert regarding experimental and newly developed procedure and diagnostic coding.


CORE FUNCTIONS

1. Provides guidance on coding and billing, utilizing coding and billing guidelines. Demonstrates extensive knowledge of clinical documentation and its impact on reimbursement under Medicare Severity Adjusted System (MS-DRG),All Payer Group (APR-DRG) and Ambulatory Payment Classification (APC) or utilized operational systems. Provides explanatory and reference information to internal and external customers regarding coding assignment based on clinical documentation which may require researching authoritative reference information from a variety of sources.


2. Reviews medical records. Performs an audit of clinical documentation to ensure that clinical coding is accurate for proper reimbursement and that coding compliance is complete. Provides feedback on coding work and trends, and offers suggestions for improvement where opportunities are identified. Reviews accuracy of identified data elements for use in creating data bases or reporting to the state health department. If applicable, applies Uniform Hospital Discharge Data Set (UHDDS) definitions to select the principal diagnosis, principal procedure, complications and co morbid condition, other diagnoses, and significant procedures which require coding. Apply policies and procedures on health documentation and coding that are consistent with official coding guidelines.


3. Assists with maintaining system wide consistency in coding practices and ethical coding compliance. If applicable, initiates and follows through on physician queries to ensure that code assignment accurately reflects the patient’s condition, treatment and outcomes. Identifies training needs for coding staff. Serves as a team member for internal coding accuracy audits and documents findings.


4. Acts as a knowledge resource to ancillary clinical departments, patient financial services and revenue integrity analysts regarding charge related issues, processes and programming. Participates in company-wide quality teams’ initiatives to improve coding and clinical documentation. Assists with education and training of staff involved in learning coding. Assists in creating a department-wide focus of performance improvement and quality management. Assists and participates with management through committees to properly educate physicians, nursing, coders, CDM’s, etc. with proper and accurate coding based on documentation for positive outcomes.


5. Performs ongoing audits/review of inpatient and/or outpatient medical records to assure the use of proper diagnostic and procedure code assignments. Collaborates on DRG and coding denials, billing edits/rejections to provide coding expertise to resolve issues and support appropriate reimbursement. Proficiency in claims software to address coding edits and claim denials utilizing multiple platforms and internal tracking tools. Provides findings for use as a basis for development of coding education and audit plans.


6. Maintains a current knowledge in all coding regulatory updates, and in all software used for coding, coding reviews and health information management for the operational group. Identifies and collects data to allow for monitoring and evaluation of trends in DRG (MS/APR-DRG), APC, HCC, other Heath Risk Adjusted Factors, National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) and the effect on Case Mix Index by use of specialized software.


7. May code inpatient and outpatient records as needed. Works as a member of the overall HIMS team to achieve goals in days-to-bill.


8. Works independently under limited supervision. Uses an expert level of knowledge to provide coding and billing guidance and oversight for all Banner facilities and services they provide. External customers include but are not limited to, practicing physicians, vendors, and the community.

Requires a level of education as normally demonstrated by a bachelor’s degree in Health Information Management or experience equivalent to same.

Extensive critical and analytical thinking skills required. Ability to organize workload to meet deadlines and maintain confidentiality. Excellent written and oral communication skills are required, as well as effective human relations skills for building and maintaining a working relationship with all levels of staff, physicians, and other contacts.


Must consistently demonstrate the ability to understand the Medicare Prospective Payment System, and the clinical coding data base and indices, and must be familiar with coding and abstracting software, claims processing tools, as well as common office software and electronic medical records software.

jobs.description:
About Our Company:
At Infinx, we're a fast-growing company focused on delivering innovative technology solutions to meet our clients' needs. We partner with healthcare providers to leverage automation and intelligence, overcoming revenue cycle challenges and improving reimbursements for patient care. Our clients include physician groups, hospitals, pharmacies, and dental groups.
We're looking for experienced associates and partners with expertise in areas that align with our clients' needs. We value individuals who are passionate about helping others, solving challenges, and improving patient care while maximizing revenue. Diversity and inclusivity are central to our values, fostering a workplace where everyone feels valued and heard.

A 2025 Great Place to Work®

In 2025, Infinx was certified as a Great Place to Work® in both the U.S. and India, underscoring our commitment to fostering a high-trust, high-performance workplace culture. This marks the fourth consecutive year that Infinx India has achieved certification and the first time the company has earned recognition in the U.S.

Summary Description
The Revenue Cycle Engagement Manager is a hands-on, deeply engaged operator who owns the success of their client engagements end-to-end. This is not a role for someone who views leadership as delegating tasks and monitoring status reports. We are looking for a leader who lives inside the work–who reads the data daily, anticipates problems before they surface on a client call, and drives solutions with urgency, precision, and grace.

The ideal candidate combines elite analytical capability with deep Acute Care & Ambulatory (Technical & Professional Claims) Revenue Cycle expertise and the executive presence to stand in front of demanding client stakeholders and answer any question put to them. They remain composed and solution-oriented under pressure, absorb difficult client feedback without losing momentum, and consistently convert challenges into measurable results. They lead from the front–inspiring their team, modeling the standard, and holding the line on performance every day.

This role reports directly to the Vice President of Acute Care Services. As a member of the Infinx Management Team, the Engagement Manager owns the daily operational health of their assigned clients and leads weekly executive-level meetings with client stakeholders, delivering credible status updates, escalating risks proactively, and presenting a clear, data-driven view of performance, root causes, and forward plans.

Location: Remote

Job Responsibilities
  • Own the full operational relationship for assigned clients–performance, communication, issue resolution, and strategic direction
  • Lead and inspire a team of coders, billers, collectors, and payment posters, driving daily accountability and measurable performance improvement
  • Manage AR and denials to consistently meet or exceed contractual SLAs, intervening personally when trends move in the wrong direction
  • Proactively monitor daily workflow, productivity, and quality metrics; identify deviations early and implement corrective action immediately–before they become client-visible issues
  • Design, refine, and execute client-specific processes and workflows that scale with volume and hold up under audit
  • Build and deliver executive-level reporting and dashboards that tell a clear story: what is happening, why, and what is being done about it
  • Lead weekly client executive meetings with formal agendas, polished presentations, and the analytical depth to answer any question asked–including unfriendly ones
  • Develop ad-hoc analyses and presentations that respond to client questions accurately, professionally, and on short timelines
  • Partner with internal teams, such as operations, technology, product, and client success, to remove barriers and accelerate solutions
  • Represent Infinx on corporate projects and initiatives that extend beyond the assigned book of business
  • Support new client expansion, implementation, and go-live activity
  • Mentor, coach, and develop team members; manage performance directly and constructively
  • Maintain full compliance with HIPAA and all client confidentiality obligations
  • Do what it takes to deliver–including non-standard hours when the situation requires it
  • Other duties as assigned
Core Competencies
  • Hands-on ownership: Treats every client engagement as their own business. Is not satisfied reading dashboards but reviews work queues, listens to calls, opens accounts, and verifies that what is being reported matches what is actually happening.
  • Anticipatory problem-solving: Spots leading indicators of trouble–shifts in denial rates, aging buckets, payer behavior, staffing productivity–and acts on them before they escalate. Does no wait for a client to raise an issue to address it.
  • Deep domain expertise: Commands a working knowledge of acute care hospital revenue cycle operations: AR follow-up, denial management, charge capture, payment posting, credit balance resolution, underpayment recovery, and the end-to-end lifecycle of a claim across both facility and professional billing.
  • Payer fluency: Expert-level understanding of Medicare IPPS and OPPS, Medicaid, Tricare, VA, and commercial payer behavior, including contract interpretation, appeal pathways, and reimbursement methodology (DRG, APC, EAPG, fee schedules, etc.)
  • Analytical rigor: Uses revenue cycle data to drive decisions, not to decorate slides. Comfortable building, interrogating, and defending models, pivot analyses, and trend work. Can explain every number on every slide and trace it back to its source.
  • Executive presence under pressure: Presents with clarity and confidence to demanding C-suite and VP-level client stakeholders. Handles pointed, skeptical, or harsh questioning without defensiveness. Stays composed, solution-oriented, and credible.
  • Strategic thinking: Understands the correlation between staffing, productivity, net cash collected, avoidable write-offs, and the client's bottom line. Makes resource and prioritization decisions with that full picture in view.
  • Process discipline: Creates, reviews, updates, and implements process improvements that reduce avoidable write-offs and measurably lift performance. Holds team members accountable through clearly defined standards and expectations.
  • Communication and de-escalation: Communicates flawlessly in writing and verbally. De-escalates client, team, and peer conflict with professionalism. Delivers difficult messages directly while preserving the relationship.
  • Adaptability: Adjusts to shifts in direction, priority, or scope and executes through change without losing momentum.
  • Team leadership: Inspires and develops remote staff in a high-volume, high contact environment. Drives performance without burning people out.

Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university preferred
  • 5-7 years of experience managing back-end revenue cycle teams in a hospital enterprise or healthcare outsourcing environment
  • Strong Paragon and Sunrise revenue cycle management knowledge
  • Certified Revenue Cycle Representative (CRCR) or equivalent industry certification preferred
  • Must have experience managing the revenue cycle for acute care hospitals
  • Data driven; ability to use revenue cycle data to make decisions, develop strategies and prioritize work
  • Expert level executive presentation skills, including ability to handle all questions regarding revenue cycle performance. Must have formal agendas and PowerPoint presentations for each weekly meeting with clients
  • Ability to quickly identify areas of concern that affect cashflow and develop plans to correct
  • Proven analytical skills to resolve unresolved claims or account issues
  • Expertise in major payer processes, including Medicare IPPS and OPPS, Medicaid, Tricare, VA, and commercial payors
  • Proven ability to deescalate client, team member, and peer issues
  • Proven understanding of quality audit reviews and ability to effectively communicate any changes or training needed
  • Proven ability to work more than 40 hours per week when needed to get the job done
  • Proven team building facilitation and feedback
  • Proven ability to collaborate with leaders both within Infinx and outside partners
  • Proven ability to create, review, update, and implement process improvements
  • Proven ability to develop internal processes that hold team members accountable
  • Proven ability to make informed decisions
  • Ability to manage multiple AR’s and manage multiple AR teams
  • Proven ability to be adaptable with changes in direction or strategy and ability to execute on the changes
  • Demonstrate the ability to identify process improvements that will reduce avoidable write offs and communicate that to the client effectively
  • Understanding the correlation between staffing, net cash collected, and the bottom line
  • Strong organizational skills
  • Takes initiative to complete tasks rapidly and accurately
  • Strong analytics/data science skills
  • Experienced leading and managing remote employees in a high contact center environment
  • Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint
  • Outstanding time management skills and the ability to simultaneously manage multiple tasks while remaining self-directed

Company Benefits and Perks:
Joining Infinx comes with an array of benefits, flexible work hours when possible, and a genuine sense of belonging to a dynamic and growing organization.

  • Access to a 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan.
  • Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage.
  • Paid Time Off.
  • Paid Holidays.
  • Additional benefits, including Pet Care Coverage, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and discounted services.

If you are a dedicated and experienced Revenue Cycle Engagement Leader ready to contribute to our mission and be part of our diverse and inclusive community, we invite you to apply and join our team at Infinx.

Who We Are

Pindrop is a cybersecurity company delivering continuous identity verification across voice, video, and digital interactions. Powered by the Pindrop Intelligence Network, our unified trust platform helps enterprises answer three critical questions:

Is this identity synthetic? Detect AI-generated and manipulated voice and video.
Is this identity risky? Identify fraud, suspicious behavior, and other risk signals.
Is this identity known? Authenticate identities using voice, device, behavioral, and other signals.

Pindrop brings this intelligence together across purpose-built trust engines to help organizations make informed decisions in real time — protecting customers, workforce interactions, and emerging AI-driven interactions.

At AVANT Global Solutions, we build software that redefines how businesses operate. Our products automate key processes for our clients, many of them in manufacturing, bringing traceability, fewer human errors and greater efficiency. We are a fully remote, cross-disciplinary team that values ownership, clear communication and continuous learning.

About the Role

You will join the team building our ERP platform, used daily by our factory clients to run their operations.

As a Full-Stack Developer on our cross-functional team, you’ll play an important role in designing, building and maintaining robust web applications. Your expertise in both frontend and backend development will be essential: you will work on unique features in the larger system and take ownership of the development lifecycle from end to end.

You may find yourself working alongside other developers on a small part of a larger system, or working solo on a larger part of a smaller system.

Front-End Development

  • Use TypeScript and Angular to build web applications.
  • Collaborate with UI/UX designers to create responsive, visually appealing UIs.
  • Implement web components in Angular, ensuring a seamless UI and smooth UX.
  • Optimize front-end performance through lazy loading, AOT compilation and efficient data binding.

Back-End Development

  • Use TypeScript and Node.js to build RESTful APIs, services and microservices.
  • Handle authentication, authorization and session management.
  • Integrate with external APIs and third-party services.
  • Write automated tests for your code.

Database Management

  • Design and maintain relational database schemas in PostgreSQL.
  • Optimize queries, indexes and database performance.
  • Ensure data consistency, integrity and security.

DevOps and Infrastructure

  • Work closely with our Platform team to manage infrastructure (containers, VMs) using tools like Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Troubleshoot production incidents promptly.

Agile Development and Teamwork

  • Take part in sprint planning, stand-ups and retrospectives.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (front-end, back-end, QA) to deliver high-quality features.
  • Automate repetitive tasks and improve development workflows.
  • Take an active part in code reviews and the discussions around them.
  • Communicate your status and be reachable when needed: emergencies happen, and reachability is essential in remote work.

Documentation and Knowledge Sharing

  • Maintain clear, concise documentation for code, APIs and deployment processes.
  • Share knowledge through code reviews, tech talks and mentoring.

About You (required)

  • You have experience with TypeScript and JavaScript, and understand the TypeScript type system.
  • You have frontend experience, ideally with Angular; React or Vue.js is also valid.
  • You have experience building backends and RESTful APIs with Node.js.
  • You have experience designing and using relational databases such as PostgreSQL or MySQL.
  • You have deployed your own projects.

Soft Skills

  • Communication: You explain technical topics clearly to non-technical colleagues, document your ideas and respond to questions.
  • Problem-solving: You make decisions under pressure and explain your reasoning.
  • Teamwork: You work well with people from many backgrounds toward common goals.
  • Asking for help: You raise problems early and accept support.
  • Openness to feedback: You take critical feedback in stride and use it to grow.
  • Adaptability: You learn quickly and take the initiative to keep improving.
  • Attention to detail: You manage complex systems carefully to prevent errors.
  • Time management: You can balance several tasks when needed.

Pluses

  • A preference for either frontend or backend development.
  • Experience with Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Experience writing automated tests on the backend and/or frontend.

We work together as one team with one common goal. We are building a cross-disciplinary, self-managing team that spans the world, collaborating openly and in a friendly way. If this sounds like you, we can’t wait to hear from you.

jobs.title: Software Engineer 5, AI Observability
jobs.excerpt: At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world.
jobs.description:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

The Opportunity

The AI Observability team makes AI, ML, and Agentic systems transparent, reliable, and production-ready at scale. We build end-to-end observability for ML and GenAI workloads, capturing model inputs, features, predictions, outcomes, and behavior across online and batch systems. Our platform enables teams to monitor model performance, data quality, drift, latency, and failures, turning the ML system from a black box into an explainable, debuggable system. We provide developer-friendly libraries, dashboards, and alerts so teams can debug issues, respond to incidents, and ship AI-powered products with confidence.


We're looking for a hands-on senior engineer to build the frameworks behind Netflix's AI Observability platform, model performance, evaluation, and vendor integration surfaces. You will design reusable infrastructure that enables ML/AI practitioners across domains to monitor model quality in production, evaluate LLM and agentic systems, and adopt vendor tooling through a consistent, self-serve platform. AIP owns the generic, reusable infrastructure; domain teams own their domain-specific evals and remediation. You will partner closely with engineering, product, machine learning, and data teams to turn their needs into reusable platform capabilities. To succeed, you will bring a strong background in AI or ML infrastructure and a passion for building scalable, robust systems.

In this role, you will:

  • Build the observability framework and platform capabilities that give ML and GenAI systems metrics, logs, and distributed traces across online inference, batch scoring, feature pipelines, and agent orchestration, so teams can instrument their systems consistently.
  • Build the primitives that let teams monitor model performance (accuracy, calibration, error rates), data quality, drift, and degradation on their own systems, rather than monitoring individual models yourself.
  • Build and extend evaluation frameworks for LLM and agentic systems that support response quality, grounding and hallucination, task success, tool-use and trajectory correctness, and LLM-as-a-judge and human-in-the-loop scoring, giving teams reusable building blocks to define and run their own evals.
  • Lead build-vs-buy evaluations for observability and eval tooling, and own the SDKs, connectors, and APIs that integrate vendor platforms into a consistent, well-supported interface, so ML and product teams can onboard models and agents with minimal friction.
  • Build reusable libraries, SDKs, and templates that make observability and evaluation the default for new systems ("observability-by-default"), lowering the barrier for teams to instrument and evaluate their work.
  • Provide the dashboarding, alerting, and SLO/SLI building blocks (plus sensible out-of-the-box templates) that teams use to track model performance, latency, cost, and reliability.

To succeed in this role, you will need:


  • Experience in software, AI/ML, or platform engineering, with hands-on time in production observability, monitoring, or ML/LLM evaluation
  • Proven track record of designing standards, libraries, SDKs, or frameworks that other teams build on and adopt, reflecting a platform and enablement mindset rather than shipping features for a single use case.
  • Strong coding skills in Python and at least one of Java, Go, or Scala, with experience building production services
  • Practical experience operating ML models in production (online serving and/or batch), including drift, model performance, and data quality.
  • Hands-on experience with modern observability stacks (e.g., Prometheus/Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry, ELK/OpenSearch, Jaeger/Tempo, or similar).
  • Solid understanding of distributed systems, microservices, and at least one major cloud platform (AWS, GCP, or Azure).
  • Ability to work cross-functionally with ML, data, infra, and product teams, and to communicate clearly about system behavior, quality, and risk.
  • Experience with vendor integration and VPC deployment.
  • An AI-Native Engineering Mindset who uses AI tools as a core part of their own workflow to accelerate design, development, testing, and code review.

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on experience with ML/LLM observability and evaluation tools (e.g., Arize, Braintrust, LangFuse, Weights & Biases, Galileo, Vertex AI Model Monitoring, SageMaker Model Monitor).
  • Experience building or shipping LLM/GenAI applications and evaluating them: prompt/result logging, evaluation metrics, LLM-as-a-judge, and human-in-the-loop review.
  • Experience evaluating agentic systems: tool use, multi-step reasoning, and trajectory/task-success measurement.

To learn more about our AI Platform, you can review the relevant talks/blog posts on the Netflix AI Platform Research website.

Generally, our compensation structure consists solely of an annual salary; we do not have bonuses. You choose each year how much of your compensation you want in salary versus stock options. To determine your personal top of market compensation, we rely on market indicators and consider your specific job family, background, skills, and experience to determine your compensation in the market range. The range for this role is $500,000.00 - $860,000.00. This compensation range will vary based on location.

Netflix provides comprehensive benefits including Health Plans, Mental Health support, a 401(k) Retirement Plan with employer match, Stock Option Program, Disability Programs, Health Savings and Flexible Spending Accounts, Family-forming benefits, and Life and Serious Injury Benefits. We also offer paid leave of absence programs. Full-time hourly employees accrue 35 days annually for paid time off to be used for vacation, holidays, and sick paid time off. Full-time salaried employees are immediately entitled to flexible time off. See more details about our Benefits here.

Netflix is a unique culture and environment. Learn more here.

Inclusionis a Netflix value and we strive to host a meaningful interview experience for all candidates. If you want an accommodation/adjustment for a disability or any other reason during the hiring process, please send a request to your recruiting partner.

We are an equal-opportunity employer and celebrate diversity, recognizing that diversity builds stronger teams. We approach diversity and inclusion seriously and thoughtfully.
