At Bayer, we believe work should matter. Every day, our teams push toward a future where "Health for all, Hunger for none" is within reach, and every role, from the lab to the field to the boardroom, helps us get there. We give people the ownership to shape outcomes, the support to grow through new skills and experiences, and a global community where different perspectives are valued. If you want your work to count and the room to become your best, you'll find it here.

We’re changing the way we work at Bayer, for higher productivity, faster innovation, and better results. We call it Dynamic Shared Ownership (DSO). Learn more about what DSO will mean for you in your new role here


The Field Medical Value Lead will lead Bayer’s integrated US medical-value engagement strategy, connecting clinical, health-economic and real-world evidence with the needs of health systems and health payers. Lead both the Medical Account Director (MAD) team and the Field Health Economics & Outcomes Research (HEOR) team, enabling credible scientific partnerships, appropriate evidence-informed access and improved population-health decision making across the product lifecycle. Preserve the independence, scientific integrity and nonpromotional character of the medical function.

YOUR TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The primary responsibilities of this role, Field Medical Value Lead, are to:

Integrated Medical-Value Strategy

  • Set an integrated national strategy and operating priorities for both teams, aligned with US Medical, therapeutic-area and HEOR strategy.
  • Translate evolving clinical, economic and population-health needs into differentiated health-system and payer engagement plans.
  • Define a shared scientific agenda without erasing the teams’ distinct expertise or customer responsibilities, and adapt priorities across development, launch and established-product stages.

People Leadership and Capability Development

  • Lead, coach and develop both reporting teams, with clear objectives, role ownership and expectations for scientific quality and collaboration.
  • Build capability through field coaching, joint customer visits, structured feedback and clinical/economic evidence training.
  • Lead talent selection, development and succession planning within HR processes.
  • Apply Visionary, Architect, Catalyst and Coach behaviors by setting direction, designing effective ways of working, removing barriers and growing others’ judgment.

Strategic Customer Partnerships and Account Planning

  • Guide long-term scientific relationships with health-system and payer medical, pharmacy and population-health leaders. Set standards for account insight, stakeholder mapping and medical outcomes planning, reflecting formulary, utilization-management and care-delivery processes.
  • Support complex engagements and ensure coordinated execution by MADs and Field HEOR, with MSL and Medical Director involvement where appropriate. Resolve overlapping coverage through explicit ownership and purposeful collaboration.

Coverage, Priorities and Resource Stewardship

  • Prioritize account coverage, deployment and customer engagement using scientific need, evidence readiness, strategic relevance and team capacity. Allocate work and manage approved resources and expenditure within delegated authority, making trade-offs transparent and escalating unmet needs.
  • Align national priorities with regional realities and sustained field presence. Maintain an adaptable operating model that reduces duplication and protects time for high-value scientific work.

Evidence Insights and Research Partnership

  • Establish a systematic process to synthesize customer insights, evidence gaps and emerging population-health priorities across both teams.
  • Partner with HEOR Research Strategy and therapeutic-area researchers to inform evidence priorities and feasible collaborations, including real-world evidence (RWE), retrospective database analyses, burden-of-illness studies and economic modeling.
  • Guide field input and customer relevance; retain study design, funding, approval and execution responsibilities within established research governance.

Scientific and Economic Communication Excellence

  • Ensure balanced, accurate and audience-appropriate interpretation of clinical, epidemiologic and economic evidence.
  • Set expectations for communicating model assumptions, uncertainty and population applicability, including budget-impact and cost-effectiveness models. Strengthen team readiness for scientific education and unsolicited questions through approved processes.
  • Maintain standards for evidence quality, methodological understanding and medical account planning rather than substituting promotional messages for scientific exchange.

Matrix Alignment and Lifecycle Readiness

  • Align engagement, evidence education and launch readiness with US Medical, HEOR, Market Access and relevant therapeutic-area partners.
  • Coordinate with Medical Science Liaisons (MSLs), Medical Directors and national account/customer-engagement colleagues to translate national priorities into coherent customer support.
  • Bring external scientific, congress and competitive HEOR/RWE insights into planning while maintaining distinct Medical and Commercial accountabilities and appropriate information-sharing boundaries.

Governance, Impact and Continuous Improvement

  • Embed FDA/OIG requirements, company policies and research governance in the operating model, with timely escalation of scientific, compliance and resource risks.
  • Establish meaningful measures of scientific engagement quality, team capability, evidence-insight usefulness and execution.
  • Review progress with partners, act on feedback and improve ways of working.

Key Relationships

Internally, partner with US Medical leadership, therapeutic-area Medical Directors, MSL leadership, HEOR Research Strategy, Market Access, national account/customer-engagement teams, Health Systems marketing/support, Compliance, Legal and HR. Externally, engage senior clinical, pharmacy, economic and population-health stakeholders across health systems, IDNs, ACOs, health plans, payers and PBMs. Build trust through scientific credibility and responsiveness, coordinating cross-functional involvement without compromising Medical independence.

Leadership Accountability and Decision Rights

jobs.excerpt: About Extend: Extend is revolutionizing the post-purchase experience for retailers and their customers by providing merchants with AI-driven solutions that enhance customer satisfaction and drive revenue growth.
jobs.description:
About Extend:

Extend is revolutionizing the post-purchase experience for retailers and their customers by providing merchants with AI-driven solutions that enhance customer satisfaction and drive revenue growth. Our comprehensive platform offers automated customer service handling, seamless returns/exchange management, end-to-end automated fulfillment, and product protection and shipping protection alongside Extend's best-in-class fraud detection. By integrating leading-edge technology with exceptional customer service, Extend empowers businesses to build trust and loyalty among consumers while reducing costs and increasing profits.

Today, Extend works with more than 1,000 leading merchant partners across industries, including fashion/apparel, cosmetics, furniture, jewelry, consumer electronics, auto parts, sports and fitness, and much more. Extend is backed by some of the most prominent technology investors in the industry, and our headquarters is in downtown San Francisco.

About the Role

The AI Enablement team gives every team at Extend the AI tooling it needs to do its best work. We pair directly with business users in finance, support, claims, sales, recruiting, and operations to understand how they work, then build the agents, connectors, and skills that change it. This is an engineering role first. Sitting beside a business user is how you find the right problem. Solving it takes real engineering judgment about agent harnesses, protocols, security, and reliability.

You will build on the platform that turns one-off prototypes into durable, secure, measurable tooling: MCP connectors to the systems we run on, agent-to-agent (A2A) integrations, a shared library of agent skills, and the evaluation practice that tells us whether any of it actually works.

What You'll Do

  • Pair with business users to run workflow analysis and process mapping, find the highest-leverage problems, and turn ambiguous requests into scoped technical plans.
  • Design and ship secure MCP connectors to Extend's internal systems and third-party SaaS: finance, CRM, data warehouse, expense management, product analytics, support, ATS, and the long tail beyond.
  • Build agent-to-agent integrations using A2A and similar protocols, so specialized agents can delegate to each other safely across domains.
  • Choose and configure the right agent harness or orchestrator for each job, and build multi-agent patterns (planner/executor, specialized sub-agents) where they genuinely help.
  • Stand up Extend's evaluation practice for agents and skills: golden datasets, regression suites, LLM-as-judge, tracing, and drift detection. Every shipped skill should have a way to prove it works and to notice when it stops working.
  • Build and curate the shared library of agent skills every team composes from. Codify patterns and raise the floor for what a safe, high-quality skill looks like. Treat every engagement as a source of reusable skills and connectors.
  • Design credential scoping and vending for agent connectors: per-user, per-skill, per-connector keys, OAuth/OIDC where it fits, least-privilege everywhere.
  • Build the risk-tier and review model for shared skills, including sandboxing and dependency scanning for skills that pull in untrusted packages. Partner with legal, security, and privacy on governance review for agents that touch sensitive data or take autonomous actions.
  • Instrument the platform end to end with OpenTelemetry so every MCP call, skill execution, and credential use is visible in Coralogix.
  • Own adoption. Write self-serve guides, onboard teams, and run the feedback loop between what shipped and what users actually need. The work is done when the team using it is self-sufficient.
  • Mentor more junior engineers on the team in evals, agent design, and secure integration work.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years shipping production systems, and you can point to where they held, where they broke, and what you changed.
  • Proficient in TypeScript/Node, Python, or Rust.
  • Hands-on experience building with MCP and at least one agent framework or harness (Claude Code, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain/LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, Google ADK). Familiarity with A2A or other agent interoperability protocols.
  • Experience designing and running evals for LLM or agent systems, and using the results to make shipping decisions.
  • You can build real third-party integrations: OAuth flows, credential scoping, webhooks, pagination, rate limiting, retries.
  • You've built developer tooling, platforms, or internal tools that other people depended on, and you measure that work by adoption.
  • You can work directly with non-technical stakeholders: run a working session, challenge assumptions constructively, and explain trade-offs in plain language.
  • Comfortable on AWS (Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, S3) with solid security fundamentals: IAM, KMS, serverless attack patterns.
  • Familiarity with AI governance and legal or privacy review processes, including risks around data access, permissions, tool use, and autonomous actions.
  • You use AI tooling every day and have opinions about what works.

Nice to Have

  • Eval and observability tooling: LangSmith, Langfuse, Braintrust, OpenTelemetry, Coralogix, Datadog.
  • LLM application security: OWASP Top 10 for LLMs and agentic applications, prompt injection defense, agent sandboxing.
  • AWS CDK, CloudFormation, or similar infrastructure-as-code.
  • Background in platform engineering, internal developer platforms, or enterprise integration.
  • Prior IC role at an early-stage startup with a small team and a wide surface area.
Expected Pay Range: $155,000 - $170,000 per year salaried*

* The target base salary range for this position is listed above. Individual salaries are determined based on a number of factors including, but not limited to, job-related knowledge, skills and experience.

Extend does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role.

Life at Extend:

  • Working with a great team from diverse backgrounds in a collaborative and supportive environment.
  • Competitive salary based on experience, with full medical and dental & vision benefits.
  • Stock in an early-stage startup growing quickly.
  • Generous, flexible paid time off policy.
  • 401(k) with Financial Guidance from Morgan Stanley.

jobs.description:
Why Go1 exists:

Work keeps changing. Skills evolve, compliance requirements increase, and people need to continually learn and adapt. Go1 builds technology around how people learn and work. We bring together technology innovation, trusted content and intelligence to help organizations develop their people and support workforce progress.

Why join Go1?

  • Build what comes next. Go1 is evolving from a trusted learning foundation into a broader workforce enablement portfolio, including Morgan by Go1. There is still plenty to shape, build and improve.
  • Have real ownership. We’re founder-led, start-up minded and deliberately low on layers. You’ll have scope to influence decisions, solve problems beyond a narrow job description and be accountable for outcomes.
  • Work AI-native. AI is becoming part of how we work across Go1. We expect people to experiment, build smarter workflows and use technology to improve the quality and speed of their work, while applying strong judgement.
  • Grow through the work. Growth isn’t limited to promotion. It comes through harder problems, broader scope, new capabilities, cross-functional exposure and increasing the impact you can have.
  • Work globally, with flexibility and trust. We’re remote-first across APAC, EMEA and North America. You’ll have autonomy and flexibility, alongside the responsibility to communicate clearly, build relationships proactively and stay connected across time zones.

We’re looking for a Finance Systems Engineer who is obsessed with end-to-end operational outcomes across systems. You’ll improve the reliability and efficiency of Go1’s finance operations, starting with quote-to-cash, working with Finance, RevOps and technical partners. Strong finance-domain expertise comes first, supported by practical familiarity with data, APIs and AI tools. Experience applying AI to finance workflows is a bonus.

What you’ll do

  • Own defined improvements to NetSuite order-to-cash workflows, from customer and sales-order data through invoicing, payments, credits, refunds, reconciliation and close support.
  • Configure and troubleshoot NetSuite workflows, transaction forms, saved searches and invoice templates. Work with technical partners on changes that require deeper scripting or integration expertise.
  • Follow data between systems, investigate mapping and integration errors, and help improve APIs, webhooks and automated workflows. Check that records remain complete, accurate, and reconciled.
  • Investigate financial-system incidents and data-quality issues. Identify root causes, coordinate fixes, and reduce recurring manual work.
  • Work with Accounting, Tax and RevOps to turn operational needs into clear requirements. Escalate accounting and tax-policy decisions to the accountable owner.
  • Test changes in the appropriate environment, coordinate user acceptance and release readiness, and maintain clear documentation and support guidance. Preserve approvals, exception handling, and financial controls.
  • Use AI tools where they help with analysis, documentation, troubleshooting, or test preparation. Check their outputs, protect financial data and retain human review before using results in a financial workflow.

What you’ll bring

Four or more years of experience in finance systems, ideally in B2B. We’ll assess your experience in this order:

1. Finance-domain expertise
Hands-on NetSuite experience and a strong understanding of operational finance and order-to-cash. You understand invoices, payments, refunds, reconciliation, revenue dates, and multi-currency considerations, and can explain the downstream impact of a system chang. You can demonstrate ownership of a finance workflow or system improvement, investigate discrepancies methodically, and recognise when Finance or Tax approval is needed. Clear communication and careful testing are essential. Familiarity with record to report is nice to have.

2 Data and API fundamentals
You understand records, identifiers, field mappings and how data moves between systems. You can inspect an API request or response, follow an integration error and work with technical partners to diagnose the issue.Practical familiarity with APIs, webhooks or workflow automation is expected. You do not need to be an integration architect or an expert across every tool in our environment.

3. Practical AI familiarity
You have some experience using AI tools for everyday work, such as analysis, documentation, troubleshooting or test preparation. You can check the output, recogniselimitations and explain when human review is We value curiosity and a willingness to develop this capability. Advanced AI engineering, machine-learning expertise and production agent-building experience are not prerequisites.

The Technology environment
Hands-on NetSuite experience is required. Experience with the other platforms listed below is helpful, but not essential.

  • NetSuite: OneWorld, ARM, SuiteScript, SuiteFlow, SuiteAnalytics, SQL, SuiteQL, consolidated reporting, reconciliation and reporting
  • Experience in a subscription based B2B or multi-entity environment, or with more advanced integrations and AI-assisted workflows preferable
  • Salesforce, Stripe and Upflow across customer and order data, billing, payments and collections.
  • Tipalti, Expensify and Brex across supplier payments, expenses and spend management.
  • Vertex and Pagero for indirect-tax and e-invoicing workflows.
  • Workato, APIs and webhooks to connect systems, investigate data flows and improve automation.
  • NetSuite reporting tools, SQL and emerging AI capabilities to support analysis, troubleshooting and controlled improvement
  • Enterprise access to Chatgpt and Codex

What this role is not

  • A NetSuite administrator role limited to access management and routine configuration.
  • A transactional accounting, invoice-processing or reporting-only role.
  • A project manager coordinating technical work without hands-on involvement.
  • A role limited to maintaining existing workflows without addressing underlying problems

Benefits:

At Go1, our employee benefits go far beyond a pay cheque, ensuring our team feels supported, valued, and empowered to bring their best selves to work each day at each stage of life.

  • In addition to your base salary: Annual bonus or commission plan.
  • Employee Stock Option Plan: Opportunity to share directly in our success through stock options.
  • Public Holiday Swap: Swap a public holiday for another preferred day.
  • Flexible Working: We are a fully remote organisation with team events and travel throughout the year.
  • Wellbeing & Learning Days: An additional five days of paid leave per year.
  • Learning Budget: $500 USD per financial year, plus access to additional Career Growth Budget.
  • WFH/Transport Budget: Monthly allowance for internet/phone expenses or public transport.
  • Home Office Setup Budget: One-off allowance for desk, chair and/or monitor.

jobs.title: GTM Recruiter, OpenRouter (Fixed Term)
jobs.excerpt: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses.
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

To help support that mission, in August we announced that Stripe had agreed to acquire OpenRouter, a leading AI model gateway and routing platform. While that acquisition is under regulatory review and has not yet closed, our intent is that this role will support the OpenRouter team following the closing of the acquisition.

About the team

OpenRouter helps developers and businesses access and use a broad range of AI models through a unified platform. This role sits at the intersection of OpenRouter and Stripe, supporting hiring across Tech, GTM, and Core teams. You’ll serve as a bridge between the 2 organizations, bringing Stripe’s recruiting standards, talent networks, and resources to OpenRouter while protecting its speed and minimizing operational overhead.

You’ll align to Tech, GTM, or Core, but you won’t be dedicated to a single job profile within that function. For example, a GTM Recruiter may support Sales, Solutions Architecture, Marketing, or other GTM roles as priorities shift. The same model applies across Tech and Core.

What you’ll do

Own full-cycle recruiting for your aligned function, moving across job profiles based on business priority, from intake and market mapping through offer acceptance and onboarding handoff. You’ll combine direct execution with consultative partnership, working closely with hiring managers to clarify needs, advise on talent markets, build and engage qualified pipelines, and move candidates through structured, timely processes.

You’ll operate with startup speed while leveraging Stripe’s infrastructure and reach. You’ll use metrics to identify risk and guide action, while keeping recruiting outcomes, not reporting or process for its own sake, at the center of the work.

Responsibilities

  • Own full-cycle recruiting across the full range of roles within your aligned function, Tech, GTM, or Core, moving between job profiles as business priorities shift
  • Build qualified and inclusive pipelines through hands-on sourcing across communities, referrals, events, market mapping, relationship-based outreach, and other creative channels beyond inbound applications and standard LinkedIn outreach
  • Partner consultatively with hiring managers to translate business priorities into clear role requirements, search strategies, structured assessments, and timely decisions
  • Use funnel metrics, market evidence, and candidate feedback to identify risks, recommend actions, and communicate progress without allowing reporting or process to substitute for recruiting
  • Deliver a thoughtful candidate experience and maintain relationships with prospective candidates for immediate and future needs
  • Serve as an operational bridge between OpenRouter and Stripe by absorbing coordination where possible, maintaining continuity, and reducing the time OpenRouter leaders spend navigating recruiting processes
  • Flex across job profiles within your aligned function when priorities shift or additional coverage is needed

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, including direct ownership of sourcing, assessment, stakeholder partnership, and closing
  • Experience recruiting in a high-growth technology startup, preferably during a stage below 200 employees
  • Demonstrated recruiting depth in at least 1 of the following areas: Tech, GTM, or Core, with experience recruiting across multiple job profiles or clear evidence you can move between profiles as business priorities shift.
  • Demonstrated interest in and ability to personally conduct hands-on sourcing and build qualified pipelines through creative channels beyond inbound applications and standard LinkedIn outreach
  • Experience partnering consultatively with hiring managers, managing multiple searches, and using recruiting metrics and market evidence to identify risk and guide action
  • Ability to work through ambiguity, adapt quickly as priorities change, and balance direct execution with longer-term pipeline building

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience recruiting across both startup and larger-company environments and helping teams work effectively across different operating models
  • Experience supporting structured, competency-based hiring processes
  • Experience recruiting across multiple geographies or advising on location strategy
  • Practical experience using recruiting technology, talent intelligence, or AI tools to improve sourcing and candidate experience

jobs.excerpt: About SuiteOp Hospitality is one of the most human businesses in the world, and one of the hardest to run.
jobs.description:
About SuiteOp

Hospitality is one of the most human businesses in the world, and one of the hardest to run. Behind every great stay is someone who answered a guest at midnight, a cleaner who turned a home in two hours, and an operator holding it all together with spreadsheets and group chats.

We started SuiteOp because we've been those operators. Our founders ran rentals before they built software for them, and that's still how we build: we sit with operators, watch where their day breaks, and fix it.

Today more than 30,000 units run on SuiteOp, across short-term rentals and boutique hotels. With SuiteOp V2, AI agents take on the repetitive work, from guest messages to turnovers, so operators and their teams can get back to the part that matters: hospitality.

We're a small team (seed stage, $3M+ raised), headquartered in New York with customers around the world. We care deeply about the craft. We sweat the details operators feel every day, we ship fast, and we use AI in everything we do because it lets a small team build something great.

About the role

Be one of SuiteOp's first people in Europe. Spain is one of the most exciting vacation rental markets in the world, full of operators who are growing fast and running on spreadsheets and WhatsApp groups. You'll start the conversations, in Spanish and English, that turn them into SuiteOp customers.

You'll own the top of the funnel: find the right operators, reach them by phone, email, and LinkedIn, and book qualified meetings for our Account Executives. The phone is where you shine. Operators don't buy from bots. They buy from people who understand their business and ask sharp questions.

You'll work side by side with our Account Executives and sales leadership, and what you hear from operators will shape our messaging and our product.

What you'll do

  • Make 100+ outbound dials a day to Spanish and European operators managing anywhere from 10 to 1,000+ units
  • Book qualified demos for our Account Executives, with clear handoff notes
  • Run multi-touch outreach across phone, email, and LinkedIn, in Spanish and English, personalized for every operator
  • Research every account and prep every call, so you can hold a real conversation without a script
  • Keep HubSpot clean: every call, every note, every next step
  • Bring back what you hear from operators: what's landing, what's not, and why
  • Help build the outbound playbook for Spain and Europe, from target lists to talk tracks

AI is how we work

Our reps run on Claude. It isn't a trend for us. It gives every rep hours back each week to spend on the phone instead of on busywork. We're looking for someone who already works this way and loves it.

  • You build your own AI workflows and agents for research and call prep, and you can't wait to walk us through one you're proud of
  • You use AI to understand each operator more deeply, not to send more generic emails
  • You know when to put the tools down and pick up the phone
  • Bonus: you've built with Claude Code, Clay, n8n, or similar tools

What you bring

  • You love the phone, and a hard no rolls right off you
  • You're competitive, coachable, and hungry to grow
  • Fluent Spanish and English, written and spoken (Portuguese, French, or Italian is a plus)
  • 1+ years in an SDR, BDR, or other outbound sales role, ideally in B2B SaaS
  • A track record of booking meetings through real conversations, not automation alone
  • Clear, confident writing: your emails sound like you, not like a template
  • Comfortable with a modern sales stack: CRM, dialer, and sequencer
  • Bonus: competitive athlete, or anyone who's thrived in a high-rep, high-feedback world
  • Bonus: experience in hospitality, property management, or short-term rentals

Why you'll love it here

  • You'll see your meetings turn into customers, and learn from a team that coaches every day
  • You'll work closely with the founders, and your ideas will shape how we sell
  • You'll build real AI workflows with a team that does it every day, a skill few sales roles will teach you
  • Your role grows with Europe: the playbook you build becomes the one every future rep here uses

Compensation

  • Base salary: €32,000 to €38,000
  • On-target earnings (base + commission): €45,000 to €55,000, with uncapped commission
  • Equity in SuiteOp

This is a remote role based in Spain, working European business hours. Madrid or Barcelona is a plus.

If you love the phone, love hospitality, and want to help build the sales engine behind SuiteOp, we'd love to meet you.

It also introduces a Coin-to-Company model, creating a structured pathway for token holders to potentially participate in the equity of companies built around scientific research.

By bridging science, and real-world commercialization, Molecule aims to make scientific research more transparent, accessible, collaborative, and economically sustainable.

The Role

You will be an AI Scientist at Molecule. In your first four weeks, you will live on-site, embedded with the founding team, and ship your first autonomous agent fleet into production against a real disease area. From day one you own the loop: design the agents, deploy them, pilot them, iterate, and generate scientific output that moves IP forward.

This is not a research role with a roadmap handed to you. You will pick targets, stand up infrastructure, recruit your sub-agents, and prove that autonomous science works at the bench-to-IP level. After the residency, you scale: more fleets, more disease areas, more shots on goal.

What You'll Do

  • Architect and deploy fleets of scientific agents spanning literature mining, target identification, molecular design, assay design, and data analysis

  • Pilot each fleet against a specific disease area and drive it to a tangible deliverable — a validated target, a candidate molecule, a novel dataset, an IP-NFT

  • Run multiple fleets in parallel across disease areas, reporting results directly to the CEO

  • Own the full stack: agent design, orchestration, evaluation, and scientific judgment on outputs

  • Define and set the standard for how autonomous science gets done at Molecule

Who You Are

  • Entrepreneurial to the core. You ship. You don't wait for permission.

  • Technically deep across LLMs, agent frameworks, and at least one wet-science domain - chemistry, biology, pharma, structural biology, or genomics

  • Comfortable with ambiguity. You may be the only person in the room who knows how to do what you do, and that energizes you

  • Credential-agnostic. PhD, MSc, BSc, or straight from high school - output matters, not titles. If you hold a degree, it should be from a top-tier institution (Oxbridge, Ivy League, MIT, Caltech, Stanford, ETH/EPFL, Imperial, or equivalent). If you skipped the degree, show us what you built instead.

  • All-in on intensity. Willing to live on-site for 4 weeks and operate at founder pace

What We Offer

  • An early seat at the company building the infrastructure for autonomous science

  • Direct ownership over a frontier no one else is running at

  • The fastest path from idea to deployed IP that exists in biotech today

Our platforms combine multi-sensor fusion, 3D imaging, and AI technologies to create complete, accurate underground maps that enable confident decision-making for customers across the built world. We transform the project lifecycle for our customers, who include key community stakeholders in the utilities, transportation and government sectors.

We are experiencing sky-rocketing growth and closed a historically large $96M Series B round in July of 2025.

Job description

Exodigo engineers the underground without digging. Our platform combines multi-sensor fusion and AI to produce complete, accurate 3D maps of buried utilities, foundations, and geotechnical conditions, which utilities, transportation agencies, and engineering firms use to plan, design, and build with confidence. Behind every map is a team of civil engineers, BIM modelers, and mapping specialists who turn raw subsurface data into engineering-grade deliverables.

We are looking for an AI BIM Engineer to help that team move faster, stay consistent, and scale with our growth. You will work alongside our Mapping, Delivery, and Engineering Services teams, learn how a project moves from field scan through interpretation to Civil 3D and OpenRoads models and client-ready utility maps, and find where AI can take on the repetitive work so our engineers can focus on engineering judgment.

This is a hands-on, builder role. You will scope the problem, build the solution, ship it into live projects, and stay with it until it becomes part of how the team works. You will be the bridge between engineers who know the underground deeply and the AI agents that can amplify them: you can discuss utility quality levels, model QA/QC, and client CAD standards in the morning, and write a new integration for an AI agent in the afternoon. What you learn on our projects will shape the AI capabilities we give every team.

What You'll Do

Embed with engineering teams

  • Work side by side with highway, structures, water, and site development teams to understand their design processes, tools, standards, and pain points.
  • Lead discovery sessions with engineers and project leads, and translate what you hear into clearly scoped, prioritized opportunities for AI and automation.
  • Own delivery end to end: from first conversation and rapid prototype through to a stable tool in daily production use.
  • Coach engineers on using AI effectively and safely in their work, through hands-on sessions, office hours, and one-on-one support.

Turn expertise into repeatable workflows

  • Partner with senior engineers to capture their know-how (checking procedures, design criteria, QA/QC steps, naming and modeling standards) as reusable AI workflows, prompts, and playbooks.
  • Design workflows that are repeatable and reviewable: clear inputs, clear outputs, and an engineer in the loop wherever professional judgment or sign-off is required.
  • Build evaluation sets from real project data so we can measure whether a workflow is accurate and reliable before it scales.
  • Document what you build and help teams own and extend their workflows themselves.

Extend what our AI agents can do

  • Design and build integrations that let AI agents read, query, and act on civil engineering data: BIM models, alignments, surfaces, pipe networks, drawings, specifications, and project records.
  • Develop tools and connectors on top of platforms such as Autodesk Civil 3D, Revit, and Autodesk Platform Services / ACC, Bentley OpenRoads and iTwin, and open formats such as IFC and LandXML.
  • Build automations with Dynamo, pyRevit, Python, and C#/.NET where a deterministic script is the right answer and expose them as capabilities an AI agent can call.
  • Make sound trade-offs between speed, scope, and quality, and keep everything you ship secure, version-controlled, and maintainable.

Close the loop

  • Spot patterns across teams and turn one-off solutions into shared, reusable capabilities.
  • Feed field insights back to our digital, IT, and data teams to shape platform priorities and roadmap.
  • Contribute to our AI governance, data-handling, and BIM standards so adoption stays responsible as it grows.

Requirements

  • Degree in Civil Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • 4+ years combining software development with BIM, CAD, or digital delivery work, ideally on infrastructure or civil projects.
  • Strong coding skills in Python, plus experience with C#/.NET or TypeScript.
  • Hands-on experience automating BIM workflows using tools such as Dynamo, pyRevit, the Civil 3D or Revit APIs, or Autodesk Platform Services.
  • Practical experience building with large language models: prompt and workflow design, tool or function calling, retrieval over documents, and evaluating model output.
  • A working understanding of civil design deliverables: alignments and profiles, corridors, grading, drainage and utility networks, sheet production, and model coordination.
  • Comfort working directly with end users: you listen first, explain clearly to non-technical audiences, and build trust by shipping.
  • Ownership and a bias for action. You are happy working in ambiguity, scoping your own work, and seeing it through to adoption.

Nice to Have

  • Experience building agent integrations, for example using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or similar tool frameworks.
  • Familiarity with openBIM and infrastructure data standards such as IFC 4.3, LandXML, and ISO 19650.
  • Experience with Bentley OpenRoads, OpenFlows, or iTwin; Navisworks; or GIS platforms such as ArcGIS.
  • Experience with document AI on drawings, specifications, and reports, including PDF and OCR pipelines.
  • Background as a practicing civil engineer or BIM coordinator before moving into software.
  • Experience delivering training or leading change-management programs in an engineering organization.

Learn more

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you will have:

  • Embedded with several project teams and built a clear map of where AI can save the most time and reduce the most risk.
  • Shipped AI workflows that engineers use every week, with measurable time savings and quality improvements.
  • Added new civil-specific capabilities to our AI agents, so they can work directly with the models and data our teams produce.
  • Built a library of documented, evaluated workflows that other teams can pick up and adapt.
  • Become the go-to person engineers call when they think, "There has to be a better way to do this."

Why Join Us

  • Real impact: your work goes straight into the maps that help infrastructure owners avoid utility strikes, delays, and safety risks on major projects.
  • An AI-native company: AI already sits at the core of how we read the subsurface. You will extend it to how we engineer and deliver.
  • A rare mix of disciplines: geophysics, civil engineering, BIM, and modern AI in one role, with a global team spanning the US, Israel, and beyond.
  • Room to shape, from the ground up, how a fast-growing company scales its engineering delivery with AI.
  • Close collaboration with field, mapping, and engineering experts who care about getting the underground right.

Our mission is to power the next era of underground exploration – saving time, money, lives, and the planet. We are focused, intentional, confident, and hard working. We solve big problems, but we are approachable, open-minded, and love hard questions.

You can learn more about us on our website or check out this short video.

Description

​​Centralized monitoring is an integral part of a risk-based monitoring strategy, defined as the timely, remote review of accumulating subject and operational data to help distinguish between reliable and unreliable data, trends, outliers, and unusual variability using analytics and statistical methods.

The central monitor is responsible for conducting a holistic and centralized statistical review of study data from study start through to study database lock according to the centralized monitoring plan, using analytical tools to identify emerging and existing risks to critical study data and process. The central monitor enables proactive identification, communication, escalation and management of risks at the study/country/site level. ​

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • ​​Follow established procedures for the review of clinical trial data (Operational and Subject data) using a variety of tools and systems in alignment with the centralized monitoring plan and with support from the senior team members.
  • ​Identify data quality trends indicative of systematic errors and potential performance issues at study/country/site and track the evidence of issues and potential risks with support from senior team members.
  • ​Ensure results of reviews are appropriately documented per procedures.
  • ​Support Central Monitoring teams with performance of assigned reviews with high quality, on-time results.
  • ​Provide input to senior team member as needed to support development of risk characterization and reporting.
  • ​Support review set-up as directed by assigned lead including updating department database, pulling reports, etc. as assigned.
  • ​Share the responsibility for data quality at the study, country and site levels.​

Requirements

Education

  • ​​Bachelor’s degree in a field relevant to clinical research.

Experience

  • ​Minimum of 1 year of experience in central statistical monitoring with overall 6 years of experience in two or more operational areas such as clinical monitoring, data management, drug safety, medical monitoring, biometrics, or project management.
  • ​Basic understanding of statistical monitoring and Risk Based Quality Management (RBQM) and their impact on data integrity.
  • ​Thorough understanding of the processes associated with clinical study management, data management, and regulatory operations.
  • ​Knowledge of clinical trial database systems (EDC, IRT, CTMS, etc.).
  • ​Good computer skills, with knowledge of advanced MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and the ability to learn and use interactive computer systems and tools.
  • ​Ideally a basic level of understanding of descriptive analysis e.g. means, medians, significance, confidence intervals.
  • ​Must have been involved in the analysis and review of clinical data, ability to extract pertinent information from standard study documentation, such as protocols, electronic study data systems with the ability to learn to identify trending of site/study data.
  • ​Must be able to work in non-traditional work environments.

Attributes

  • Fluent in English (excellent oral and written).
  • Must be able to communicate clearly and effectively at all levels in an organization and with external customers.
  • Must be a fast learner and able to understand new concepts quickly.
  • Prioritization skills with ability to plan, monitor and manage workload fluidly in response to changing project demands.
  • Satisfactory understanding of project protocol, project documentation including centralized monitoring and risk-based monitoring.
  • Broad working knowledge of the roles, functions and process of conducting clinical trials.
  • Must be able to manage time effectively, working with multiple functions and requirements.
  • Must have been involved in the use of trial management or data management systems.
  • Good knowledge of good clinical practices, and applicable Health Canada and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulations/guidelines.

Our company

The work environment

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive advancement opportunities.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

  • Flexible work schedule
  • Permanent full-time position
  • Ongoing learning and development

Work location

You’ll work alongside a multidisciplinary team of engineers, architects, and 3D visualization experts to design tools that serve builders, buyers, and everyone involved in bringing homes to life. You’re a product-minded designer who thrives on solving complex problems and crafting user-centered solutions. You’re passionate about improving how people design and live in their homes—and energized by the opportunity to make a meaningful dent in an outdated industry.

You have:

  • 7+ years of experience designing web-based software

  • A track record of shipping high-quality, thoughtful product experiences in complex domains

  • A strong portfolio that showcases your process, thinking, and ability to simplify complexity

  • Deep user empathy and a clear, confident communication style—especially when working with cross-functional teams

  • A systems-thinking mindset with the ability to balance detail with big-picture product vision

  • Experience in defining and delivering net-new experiences, not just iterating on existing patterns

  • Comfort articulating trade-offs, managing ambiguity, and driving toward clarity in fast-moving environments

Familiarity with major application-layer protocols, including HTTP, HTTPS, FTP, SFTP, FTPS, SMTP, and DNS. Ability to read and understand packet traces and interpret network access control lists.

jobs.excerpt: We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production.
jobs.description:
We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable.

Our stack is Python (FastAPI) on AWS, with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows.

Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD.

What You Will Do:

  • Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end.

  • Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails.

  • Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production.

  • Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

  • Drive the full software development lifecycle, translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans.

What We Are Looking For:

  • 5+ years building and operating production backend systems, with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end.

  • Deep fluency in your primary backend language, and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly.

  • Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one.

  • Sound reasoning under ambiguity: you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change.

  • Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations, including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar).

  • Professional written English, enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs.

Even Better:

  • AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience.

  • Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions.

  • A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal.

How We Hire:

We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build:

  • 1. A 120-minute conversation focusing on your background and a collaborative system-design exercise and cultural fit..

  • 2. A 120-minute live technical session involving code review, live coding, and a self-review.

You may complete the technical session in your strongest language (Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, or TypeScript/Node.js). Web search is encouraged; AI assistants are not used. We want to see your fundamental engineering judgment.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive USD-based salary and a comprehensive benefits package.

  • Hybrid work flexibility with hours that support deep work.

  • The opportunity to work at the frontier of agentic AI, tackling hard problems with high ownership.

  • A highly educated, agile senior team that values pragmatism, learning, and continuous improvement.

If you would rather be judged on how you think than on a buzzword list, we would like to talk!

jobs.title: Penetration Tester - Hardware (Canada)
jobs.excerpt: Packetlabs is a cybersecurity consulting firm specializing in advanced Penetration Testing.
jobs.description:
Packetlabs is a cybersecurity consulting firm specializing in advanced Penetration Testing. We exist to eliminate the false sense of security that comes from shallow testing and checkbox-driven assessments. Our slogan, "Ready for more than a VA scan?", reflects a simple standard: real security work should be rigorous, manual, and built to uncover what automated approaches miss. Our clients span government, technology, law enforcement, retail, healthcare, and financial services, and they rely on us because credibility matters when the stakes are high.

Packetlabs is looking for an Penetration Tester - Hardware to lead security assessments of embedded and IoT devices, the physical products where a vulnerability lives in silicon, firmware, and board layout, rather than in a web request. The Ethical Hacker - Hardware is a specialized technical role focused on assessing embedded systems across all industries, from consumer IoT to industrial and connected devices. This role involves getting hands-on with a device, opening it up, and proving what an attacker with physical or local access can really do.

This role requires the rare combination of offensive security instinct and genuine hardware fundamentals. You will work directly with clients to understand their devices and deliver findings that improve security posture.

Who we are looking for

  • No egos, ever. Egos don't belong at Packetlabs. The more you learn, the less you know. You stay humble, ask questions, and work to help clients improve their security.
  • Customer-first mentality. You are an excellent communicator with clients, project managers, and teammates. You are responsive, reliable, and professional throughout every engagement.
  • You deliver work that you take pride in. Your work is an autograph of your excellence. You hold yourself to a high standard, and it shows in what you produce.
  • Digs deeper into every finding. You don't stop until impact is proven, while understanding that restraint is the right call in sensitive OT environments where high-risk activity is not appropriate.
  • Comfortable being uncomfortable. You move toward obstacles, not away from them. Consulting is not a typical job and requires adapting to rapidly changing environments.
  • Always learning. Cybersecurity changes every day, and you keep up because you want to. You are deeply aware of your skillset and committed to improving it.
  • Self-motivated and dependable. You take ownership of your work and your outcomes without needing to be managed into them.

What you’ll be doing

  • Hardware Penetration Testing
    • Plan and execute end-to-end hardware penetration tests on embedded and IoT devices, against a defined scope and rules of engagement
    • Identify, access, and exploit on-board debug interfaces: JTAG, SWD, UART, and similar, to gain code execution or memory access
    • Extract firmware via debug ports, in-circuit flash reads (SPI / I2C / NAND), or chip-off when required, and analyze it for vulnerabilities
    • Intercept and analyze data on common embedded buses (SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, USB) using logic analyzers and protocol decoders
    • Where in scope, perform side-channel analysis and fault injection (power analysis, voltage/clock glitching) to bypass secure boot, readout protection, or authentication
  • Firmware Analysis & Reverse Engineering
    • Reverse engineer firmware and embedded binaries (Ghidra, IDA, Binwalk, etc.) to find logic flaws, hardcoded secrets, and exploitable conditions
    • Assess physical attack surface, tamper resistance, and key/secret storage
    • Distinguish between theoretical and operationally relevant risk to keep findings actionable
  • Client Advisory & Remediation
    • Write high-quality technical reports and present findings to client stakeholders, both technical and non-technical
    • Advise on practical, prioritized remediation that clients can act on
    • Build client confidence through credibility, clear communication, and proven impact
  • Methodology, Research & Continuous Improvement
    • Build and maintain lab tooling, test rigs, and internal methodology
    • Contribute to research, responsible disclosure, and internal knowledge-sharing
    • Stay current on hardware attack techniques, embedded architectures, and defensive controls
    • Help raise the standard of hardware security work across the firm

What success looks like

  • Clients gain a clear, accurate understanding of their hardware risk, backed by proven, reproducible impact
  • Findings are credible, actionable, and land for both technical and leadership audiences
  • Engagements are delivered to a consistently high standard with strong client confidence
  • Scope and rules of engagement are managed well as engagements evolve, with risk surfaced early and clearly
  • Packetlabs' hardware testing methodology and lab capability continue to mature through your contribution
  • Clients trust Packetlabs as the partner that can break their hardware before someone else does

Education and Experience

  • A graduate of an Information Security, Computer Science, or Computer/Electrical Engineering degree program (or equivalent hands-on experience)
  • Strong electronics fundamentals. Able to read schematics and datasheets and reason about a board from them
  • Hands-on soldering ability, including surface-mount (SMD) rework and basic chip removal
  • Demonstrated experience accessing debug interfaces (JTAG, SWD, UART) and extracting firmware from real devices
  • Comfort with core bench instruments: logic analyzer, oscilloscope, and multimeter
  • Firmware reverse-engineering skills and scripting proficiency in Python, plus enough C to read embedded code
  • Familiarity with common embedded architectures (ARM/Cortex-M, MIPS, AVR, RISC-V) and RTOS/bare-metal concepts
  • Clear written and verbal communication.
  • Nice to have (one or more would be an asset):
    • Side-channel / fault-injection experience (e.g., ChipWhisperer)
    • RF and wireless work: SDR, BLE, sub-GHz, Wi-Fi
    • Knowledge of secure boot chains, TEEs, secure elements, and HSMs
    • PCB design familiarity (KiCad / Altium) for understanding target boards
    • Published CVEs, conference talks, CTF placements, or open-source tooling
    • Relevant certifications (e.g., OSCP for breadth, or hardware-focused training)

Why us?

  • The opportunity to work on high-stakes hardware engagements where your judgment and bench skills genuinely matter
  • Receive immediate and ongoing offensive security training, mentorship, and professional development to advance your technical capabilities
  • Play a key role in shaping the growth, direction, and methodology of Packetlabs' expanding hardware practice
  • A leadership team that values substance, quality, and disciplined execution
  • Collaboration with a highly skilled team of security professionals who are passionate about technical excellence and raising the bar
  • Competitive compensation and growth opportunity
  • Flexible work environment that empowers employees to do their best work
  • Fully remote within Canada

Job Title: ​

Lead AI Insights Engineer

Job Description: ​

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship, now or in the future.

As an AI Insights Engineer at agilon health, you will deliver production-grade AI products within agilon’s Tech Group. Key areas of development include unstructured data processing, clinical suspect identification, and clinical risk models. In this role, you will develop and deploy clinically appropriate AI products using LLMs, NLP, and ML tools. You will work closely with stakeholders across the organization to understand the clinical, business, and technical requirements, and be responsible for communicating the impact that AI products create at agilon.

*Only candidates with healthcare experience will be considered.

Essential Job Functions:

  • Leverage LLM tools to drive early disease identification and clinical recommendations through agilon’s unstructured clinical data, including notes and images.
  • Create production-grade AI products, including the supporting data pipelines, monitoring, and performance analysis.
  • Communicate the value and opportunities of AI to internal stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with Market Operations, Insights Engineering, and Clinical teams to drive real-world outcomes.
  • Contribute to the development of our AI products in a fast-paced, agile environment.

Required Qualifications:

Minimum Experience

  • 7+ Years of experience in a related field, including Analytics, Data Science, or Data Engineering.
  • 3+ Years in a healthcare setting, preferably value-based care.

Education/Licensure

  • Bachelor’s and/or master’s in a quantitative field, such as Computer Science, Data Science, or Mathematics.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Strong SQL skills and experience (prefer Snowflake + dbt) with data visualization tools (prefer Sigma).
  • Advanced knowledge of at least one programming language outside of SQL (prefer python).
  • Experience with cloud data engineering and AI infrastructure tools, such as Snowflake Cortex, dbt, AWS Sagemaker/Bedrock, etc.
  • Experience with AI-enabled development practices and tools (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), including MCP server development and context engineering best practices.
  • Deep knowledge of data sources and common analytical methods in healthcare, including FHIR sources, claims, pharmacy, and lab data.
  • Understanding of value-based care concepts in the US, including Medicare payment models, medical margin, and quality of care.
  • Intellectual curiosity and a passion for using data to solve real-world problems at scale.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to proactively explain complex concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Enthusiasm for learning and adapting in a dynamic environment.
